title: ECONNRESET errors crashing app
body:
### Describe the bug
Hello,

We are receiving a ECONNRESET error about 1-2 times daily when ingesting data into our clickhouse cloud cluster. This error causes our nodejs app to crash because its thrown asynchronously (caught by our unhandledRejection root error handler). This has been occurring non-stop for over a year.

Stack trace:
```
Error: read ECONNRESET
  File "node:internal/stream_base_commons", line 217, col 20, in TLSWrap.onStreamRead
  File "node:internal/async_hooks", line 128, col 17, in TLSWrap.callbackTrampoline
```

Example request payload:
```
http.method: POST,
http.query: query_id=a448c0c3-badb-4cfd-9719-8545fdf9d880&async_insert=1&async_insert_deduplicate=1&async_insert_busy_timeout_ms=200&parallel_view_processing=1&query=INSERT+INTO+datapoint+FORMAT+JSONEachRow
```

I tried to look up that query id, but did not find it in the system, so I presume the request fails before/while being processed by clickhouse servers.

Our ingestion implementation is very simple:
```
try {
  await client.insert({
    table: "datapoint",
    format: "JSONEachRow",
    values: [... array of values ...],
    clickhouse_settings: {
      async_insert: 1,
      async_insert_deduplicate: 1,
      async_insert_busy_timeout_ms: 1,
      parallel_view_processing: 1,
    },
  });
} catch (error) {
  // why the error is not returned here?
  ... handle error ...
}
```

One interesting thing to notice is that the requests are taking a very long time (26s ~ 27s) before failing.

Clickhouse support recommended I open an issue here since there's something clearly wrong with the error handling in the clickhouse js client, but did have this to say:
```
The request did reach the ClickHouse server and completed in ~738ms.

The query type was INSERT INTO datapoint FORMAT JSONEachRow, and it used async insert.

However, it shows that 0 rows were written.

No exceptions were logged (exception_code: 0), which means from ClickHouse's point of view, this was a valid and successful (but empty) insert.

This might explain the behavior you're seein  especially the long duration (26 ~ 27 seconds) before the ECONNRESET. It seems likely that the actual HTTP body (with the JSONEachRow payload) wasn't successfully streamed to ClickHouse.
```

We are investigating http agent settings to reduce the socket errors, but regardless these errors shouldn't be bubbled up as unhandledRejection(s).

Related: [386](https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/issues/386)

### Expected behaviour
Socket/ECONNRESET errors to be caught by the try/catch block.

### Configuration
#### Environment
* Client version: 1.11.0
* Language version: nodejs 18.19.0
* OS: Debian 12.10

#### ClickHouse server
* ClickHouse Server version: 24.10 (clickhouse cloud production service)

title: ❌ TupleField Fails to Parse Nested Tuple Input in ClickHouse
body:
While testing tuple field functionality for table creation and data insertion, the following error was encountered during the test:

```
Cannot parse input: expected '{' before: '"{\"lat\": 40.7128, \"lon\": -74.006}"}\n': (while reading the value of nested key location): (while reading the value of key address): (at row 1)
: While executing ParallelParsingBlockInputFormat.
```

### ✅ Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a table using the following query:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS real_tuple_test (
  id Int32 DEFAULT 1,
  address Tuple(
    street String,
    city String,
    location Tuple(lat Int32, lon Int32)
  ) DEFAULT ('Main St', 'Test City', (0, 0))
) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY (id)
```

2. Try to insert the following object:

```ts
{
  id: 1,
  address: {
    street: 'Test Street',
    city: 'Test City',
    location: { lat: 40.7128, lon: -74.006 }
  }
}
```

Using 

```ts
await client.insert({
      table: tableName,
      values: [
        {
          id: 1,
          address: {
            street: 'Test Street',
            city: 'Test City',
            location: '{"lat": 40.7128, "lon": -74.006}',
          },
        },
      ],
      format: 'JSONEachRow',
    })
```

3. Error occurs during parsing due to the nested `location` tuple.

### 📝 Notes

- Appears to be a serialization issue — `location` is being passed as a JSON object instead of a proper tuple format.
- Possible mismatch between how the ORM serializes nested tuple data vs. what ClickHouse expects.

title: Does the node client support batched queries?
body:
I don't see support for this currently. The use case is when we want to execute a list of reads from the client, currently we do:

```ts
await Promise.all(
  queries.map(({ query }) => chClient.query({ query })),
);
```

I'd like to try batching the queries to the client to see if it helps our response time

Release notes

Sourced from lint-staged's releases.

v16.0.0

Major Changes

  • #1546 158d15c Thanks @​iiroj! - Processes are spawned using nano-spawn instead of execa. If you are using Node.js scripts as tasks, you might need to explicitly run them with node, especially when using Windows:

    {
  "*.js": "node my-js-linter.js"
}

  • #1546 158d15c Thanks @​iiroj! - The --shell flag has been removed and lint-staged no longer supports evaluating commands directly via a shell. To migrate existing commands, you can create a shell script and invoke it instead. Lint-staged will pass matched staged files as a list of arguments, accessible via "$@":

    # my-script.sh
#!/bin/bash

    echo "Staged files: $@"

    and

    { "*.js": "my-script.sh" }

    If you were using the shell option to avoid passing filenames to tasks, for example bash -c 'tsc --noEmit', use the function syntax instead:

    export default { '*.ts': () => 'tsc --noEmit' }

  • #1546 158d15c Thanks @​iiroj! - Validation for deprecated advanced configuration has been removed. The advanced configuration was removed in lint-staged version 9 and until now validation has failed if advanced configuration options were detected. title: Task API
body:
### Use case
Users need to run long-running queries against ClickHouse. Even though the repository provides an example at https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/blob/main/examples/long_running_queries_timeouts.ts, it's easy to miss and hit a problem with a timeout on an LB.

### Describe the solution you'd like
API that allows running a long-running query without writing a lot of code manually. [The example](https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/blob/main/examples/long_running_queries_timeouts.ts) provides a few options, but a user needs to understand the trade-offs for each of them.

title: `JSONEachRowWithProgress` return types no longer accurate after ClickHouse v25.1
Log a warning about non-consumed HTTP stream in case of an error
body:
The code like this will eventually throw a timeout error, cause the stream is not consumed:

```ts
const client = createClient()
client.exec({ query: 'SELECT 42' })
```

Perhaps we can look at `stream.readableEnded` when we log an error in the connection layer, so it could be a hint to the user about dangling streams in their app.

title: Use a `SELECT` query instead of `/ping` endpoint in the `Client.ping` method
body:
It is more convenient and uniform to just use something like

```sql
SELECT 'ping'
```

instead of sending an HTTP request to the `/ping` endpoint, as many users also want to validate authentication with this request.

Cons `/ping` endpoint:
- does not validate credentials
- does not implement CORS

title: Add a warning on a socket closed without fully consuming the stream
body:
Closes #439 

Adds a warning like this:

```
[2025-07-15T15:28:53.416Z][ERROR][@clickhouse/client][Connection] Query: socket was closed or ended before the response was fully read. This can potentially result in an uncaught ECONNRESET error! Consider fully consuming, draining, or destroying the response stream 
```

Bump ClickHouse to 25.6

title: An option to use a simple SELECT query for ping checks instead of `/ping` endpoint
body:
Closes #440 

`ping` now always uses `SELECT 'ping'` instead of the endpoint for uniform behavior between Node.js and Web versions, as well as it can be used to check if credentials are valid now.

title: Query parameter with special characters and numbers throwing errors
body:
I was trying to query on our DB for some data and noticed an issue. We are trying to keep the payload minimal so we are using short-hands for query parameter names like `$1`, `$2`, etc. which are helpful for use while building complex queries.

The issue is the parameter names, when passed to the `query_params` setting of the driver works fine when the param is used once, but it's throwing the following error when the param is used more than once:
```
... Expected substitution name (identifier). 
 type: "SYNTAX_ERROR",
 code: "62"
``` 

query:
```
SELECT
	name,
	'num' AS type,
	arrayJoin(props_num.keys) AS keys
FROM events
WHERE
	client_id = {$1:String}
	AND created_at > {$2:Int32}
GROUP BY
	name,
	keys

UNION ALL

SELECT
	name,
	'text' AS type,
	arrayJoin(props_text.keys) AS keys
FROM events
WHERE
	client_id = {$1:String}
	AND created_at > {$2:Int32}
GROUP BY
	name,
	keys;
```

params:
```
const params = {
	$1: 'bc92f73c-1d2e-4839-b369-1987b44e2b90',
	$2: 1749955122.034,
};
```

When we try removing the UNION clause and running either of the queries, it works fine and when we try with another param name like `arg` or anything that doesn't contain either a number or a special character, it works fine. I have also tried with different data types and the issue persists.

Is there some regex that we have to follow for naming the query parameters or is this an actual bug?

title: Error: Parse Error: Header overflow
body:
### Describe the bug

Unexpected error, that was a surprise for me.

```
Error: Parse Error: Header overflow
   at TLSSocket.socketOnData (node:_http_client:551:22)
   at TLSSocket.emit (node:events:519:28)
   at addChunk (node:internal/streams/readable:559:12)
   at readableAddChunkPushByteMode (node:internal/streams/readable:510:3)
```

The default Node.js client has a limit for HTTP headers, and whenever ClickHouse reports a lot of 

```
{"read_rows":"3247080671","read_bytes":"38964968052","written_rows":"0","written_bytes":"0","total_rows_to_read":"51997158453","result_rows":"0","result_bytes":"0","elapsed_ns":"14102429650"}
```

It will crash the client, so we disabled it—https://github.com/cube-js/cube/pull/9842—but I believe it requires a fix, right? WDYT about disabling it by default?

### Steps to reproduce
1. Query a table with a large amount of data, which takes 5-10 minutes to process with enabled x progress headers
2. Client will throw an exception

Another way to implement polling...

### Expected behaviour

As a developer who is using an official client, I don't want to care. However, if it's the recommended way to implement pooling, then it's a good idea to have it in the library. refs https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/issues/428

Looking forward to hearing your opinion!

#### Environment
* Client version: 1.12.0 (latest)
* Language version: Node.js
* OS: Debian 12 docker

Huge thanks

title: Intermittent Timeout error in client.query
body:
<!-- delete unnecessary items -->
### Describe the bug

We have a NestJS microservice that queries Clickhouse and we're seeing intermittent "Timeout error" errors when calling client.query with SELECT queries.

This issue seems to be timing sensitive and reproduces more easily on some machines than others.
It is also easier to reproduce the Timeout error if I run our entire test suite which runs several tests in parallel. I am however also able to reproduce the Timeout error by running a single test 10000 times.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run NestJS microservice
2. Run integration tests that make requests to microservice that result in Clickhouse queries

### Expected behaviour
Queries succeed without returning "Timeout error"

### Code example
```
query = `
        WITH sub_tab AS (
          SELECT
            a, b, c, ...
          FROM original_table
          WHERE a = {a:String}
          GROUP BY (a, b, c)
        )
        SELECT
          a, b, c, ...
        FROM sub_tab
        GROUP BY (a, b)
        LIMIT {limit:UInt32} OFFSET {offset:UInt32}
      `;
try {
  const queryResult = await client.query({
        query,
        query_params: {
          ...queryParams,
        },
        format: 'JSONEachRow',
      });
  const rows = await queryResult.json<Entity>();
  return { rows: rows };
}  catch (error) {
      this.logger.error(
        `Error querying ClickHouse: ${error}`,
      );
      throw error;
}

title: Fix CI, examples, bump CH to 25.8

A quick fix for the CI due to a breaking change introduced in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/74079 - the setting `output_format_json_quote_64bit_integers` is not `1` by default starting from 25.8, so `(U)Int64` became unquoted, so it break the tests.

Additionally, the obsolete `Cloud` test variant (old CH Cloud instances with ReplicatedMergeTree instead of Shared) was removed in favor of just `CloudSMT`, which was renamed as just `Cloud`.

Docs entries for some of the examples were also updated.

title: Do not run Cloud tests by default with external PRs or commits
body:
When a PR is created by an external contributor, the GHA cannot pull the secrets required to access the ClickHouse Cloud instance, and the CI run fails. 

The simplest solution is to disable automatic Cloud tests if a PR or commit was submitted by a user who is not a member of the CH organization. 

See the CI source: https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/blob/1.12.1/.github/workflows/tests.yml#L196-L252

Note that it should still do the codecov check.

title: UUID parsing/conversion into uint128 during insertion seems broken in node client
body:
### Describe the bug

When trying to insert a UUID value from the node client into a uint128 column, ClickHouse fails with a parsing error. It seems it's an issue with how the node client constructs the request or whether ClickHouse performs automatic conversion for UUID => uint128s.

### Steps to reproduce

```

   │↳ENGINE = SharedReplacingMergeTree('/clickhouse/tables/{uuid}/{shard}', '{replica}')↴│
   │↳ORDER BY pull_request_id                                                           ↴│
   │↳SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192                                                   │
   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

...       query: `INSERT INTO GitHubBotPullRequestToInferenceMap (pull_request_id, inference_id, original_pull_request_url) VALUES (2864574837, "019982cb-3abf-7e12-9668-c788a9e3639c", "test")`,

title: Bug: `Array(Bool)` doesn't accept `[1,0]` style value, but `@clickhouse/client` forcibly converts `[true, false]` to `[1, 0]`.
body:
### Company or project name

Flyle.inc

### Describe what's wrong

`Array(Bool)` currently does not accept `[0, 1]` style values.
This could likely be addressed as a feature request on the ClickHouse side, but the problem is that the Node.js `@clickhouse/client` library forcibly rewrites `[true, false]` to `[1, 0]`.
Because of this behavior, there is no workaround for the issue at the moment.

```
✅
clickhouse client --query "SELECT hasAll([true,false], {vals:Array(Bool)})" --param_vals='[true,false]' --password 'password'

🙅
clickhouse client --query "SELECT hasAll([true,false], {vals:Array(Bool)})" --param_vals='[1,0]' --password 'password'
```

`Bool` (Not `Array(Bool)`) works nicely.

```
✅
clickhouse client --query "SELECT true = {vals:Bool}" --param_vals=true --password 'password'

✅
clickhouse client --query "SELECT true = {vals:Bool}" --param_vals=1 --password 'password'
```

Migrate from `ts-node` to `tsx`
body:
## Summary

The long beloved `ts-node` hasn't been updated in 2 years. It also uses [acorn](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ts-node?activeTab=dependencies#:~:text=%40tsconfig/node16-,acorn,-acorn%2Dwalk) pure JS parser which also tends to be less popular and performant than the Go-based esbuild used in `tsx`.

Pros:
* actively supported project
* widely used parser / transformer
* snappier experience
* native file-aware `watch` mode

Cons:
* does not support type checking

title: Add a trivial npm package E2E test
body:
## Summary

This little test create an empty npm project, installs the latest client package, requires it and runs a function.

Such a test help verify that the actual published npm package can be installed and used across the supported Node.js versions. This helps to early identify issues with building and publishing the package.

If this change will be found useful we can try to merge this workflow with the `build.yaml` by publishing to the GitHub NPM registry first, installing from there, running some tests against the final artifact and then forward the artifact to the official NPM registry.

title: Reproducible builds
body:
## Summary

To make the builds reproducible and also reduce the surface for supply chain attacks let's start using the npm lock files.

All the commands used should be prepended with `npx` (done in a separate PR) to make sure the right version of the tools is used.

Context:
* https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/pull/493/files#r2624123165

title: Use Vitest for common unit tests
body:
## Why

The PoC looked good and we decided to move forward with Vitest:
* https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/pull/496

## What

Introducing [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/). This PR is just a first step to keep the scope small.

For now only for the common unit tests as the rest of the test suite is cross-dependent and requires some non-standard import mangling.

* running common unit tests in a metric of node versions in CI
* also running common unit tests in two browsers: Chromium and Firefox in CI

It works locally in watch mode for both Node.js and browser runner setup. The future is here 🙂

title: Update the build and publish process
body: ## Why To get ready to full migration to Vitest and also improve reliability by using a built version of the package in integration tests (as opposite to `tsx`-ing it on the fly) we first need to switch to the npm standard [workspace](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v7/using-npm/workspaces)-aware build process where each package has its own `build` directory and is built in order. This enables integration tests to use the as-close-as-it-gets package code during tests. Until we're running fully e2e tests with build-publish-install cycle (if at all needed) this PR is a step in the right direction. ## What * use `npm --workspaces` feature to run workspace global commands like `build` and `pack` * use `jq` to bump the `client-common` dependency in-place * pump the packages using the `npm` built-in `version` command which keeps the JSON formatting the way npm likes it reducing diff-noise in case of other tools used * fix a few self-reference imports that relied on the now non-standard TS `paths` option ## QA I've built all three package using the old setup from main, packed the packages and in another repository checked in all three unpacked. To check if the new setup creates identical packages I then built all three using the new setup and extracted into the original folders in that other repository and checked the `git diff` output. title: Fix CI `insert_quorum` conflicting with `async_insert` in CH `head` version
body:
## Why

CI has been [failing](https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/actions/runs/20375727307/job/58965200290?pr=504#step:6:73) with error:

```
1) insert should work with async inserts
  Message:
    Error: Insert quorum cannot be used together with async inserts. Please disable either `insert_quorum` or `async_insert` setting. 
```

This is a [recent change](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blame/4ff79b46c87b8b5b8d3cd894576af76ce67d8742/src/Interpreters/executeQuery.cpp#L1531) on the `head` CH image tag ([PR](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/89140)):

```cpp
            if (settings[Setting::insert_quorum].valueOr(0) > 0)
                throw Exception(ErrorCodes::SUPPORT_IS_DISABLED,
                    "Insert quorum cannot be used together with async inserts. " \
                    "Please disable either `insert_quorum` or `async_insert` setting.");
```

## What

* made integration tests runnable locally even if the cloud variables are set
* added retries to the async insert test
* removed the now not working combination of `insert_quorum` and `async_insert`

title: Faster exception detection code
body:
> [!TIP]
> Enable ignore whitespace in GitHub code changes tab for better code review experience.

## Why

The new `\r` + exception tag based stream filter adds a bit of overhead to the chunking code. Probably we're relying here on JIT to kick in and inline the check at runtime, but JS JIT is normally hesitant to inline and optimize bigger functions.

## What

Manually inline the hot path of the `checkErrorInChunkAtIndex()` which becomes `extractErrorAtTheEndOfChunk()`. Inlining the hot path checks allowed to get the check for effectively a single local memory comparison (given the branch prediction works as expected).

> [!NOTE]
> There is one more PR coming that is going to match the Rust implementation where we check for `\r\n` higher in the chunking pipeline where all the HTTP chunks have been combined together into a CH chunk terminated by `\n`.

title: [Performance] Replace legacy http/https modules with fetch API or better yet with undici low level api for better performance

### Use case

Performance - the legacy http/https and MUCH slower than using the fetch API or even better undici directly.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Remove all usages of http/https and replace them with fetch/undici.

### Additional context

This SDK seems to be slow on network operation sides, performing this switch will help improve it.

title: Exception detection respect tag
body:
## Why

The current exception detection code is implemented in a way that makes any combination of `\r\n` throw an exception. This works fine for most of the use cases of the JS client as the JSON-based family of response formats is the most widely used and JSON guarantees that the output stream is not going to have a non-escaped `\r` byte.

This heuristics does not work for `\r\n` terminated CSV. A CH client created with the following configuration will trip on the legitimate output:

```ts
const client = createClient({
  clickhouse_settings: {
    output_format_csv_crlf_end_of_line: 1,
    http_write_exception_in_output_format: 0, // is the default in the new versions of ClickHouse
  },
})
```

The JS exception in this scenario describes that there was an exception on the server side but parsing of that exception did not go well. This might be confusing.

## What

This PR proposes to use a more strict error parser for the supported raw formats (based on the list in `SupportedRawFormats`). This stricter parser is less likely to trip on valid input.

The downside is that neither of the parsers are byte-level (meaning they require a certain amount of the stream to be buffered). This introduces a higher risk of the exception marker and message not being recognized (or only partially recovered) when the exception byte sequence is split by a (network, in our case HTTP) chunk boundary. For example:

```json
[
  "0\r\n0\r\n0\r\n0\r\n\r\n__exception__\r\nlehhsmpwopswzufu\r\nCode: 395. DB::Exception: valid exception 2: while executing 'FUNCTION throwIf(equals(__table1.number, 1000_UInt16) :: 0, 'valid exception 2'_String :: 2) -> throwIf(equals(__table1.number, 1000_UInt16), 'valid exception 2'_String) UInt8 : 1'. (FUNCTION_THROW_IF_VALUE_IS_NON_ZERO) (version 26.1.1.200 (",
  "official build))\n320 uxhzkfvbzrfigznc\r\n__exception__\r\n"
]
```

My take on this is that for raw formats it seems to be a better trade-off to potentially miss an exception compared to not being able to process output at all.

This PR also fixes an infinite loop case scenario that happens on a certain exception message split.

## Also

The PR uses blanket implementation for all the raw formats not taking the `\r` setting into account. It might be better to introduce a separate client config option instead that default to the simpler JSON-friendly parser. This may help get consistent results for those rare cases with `\r` terminated SCV and custom output format.

Also, one of the added tests has to have a certain number of output rows to run in both `local` and `local_cluster` modes. This is because in `local_cluster` mode `nginx` repacks the HTTP chunks using it's internal HTTP acceleration-focused logic and changes this way the resulting chunking conditions as seen by the client.

The branch has been rebased onto `main`, resolving two modify/delete conflicts introduced by the Vitest migration and the docker-compose consolidation:
- `docker-compose.cluster.yml` was removed (its content was merged into the unified `docker-compose.yml` in `main`).
- `packages/client-common/__tests__/utils/jasmine.ts` was removed (deleted in `main` as part of the Jasmine→Vitest cleanup); the integration test that depended on it (`node_streaming_exception.test.ts`) was updated to use the new async `isClickHouseVersionAtLeast(client, major, minor)` helper from `@test/utils/server_version` together with Vitest's `skip()`.

## Checklist

- [ ] A human-readable description of the changes was provided to include in CHANGELOG

title: Experimental tracing logging for `command()`
body:
## Summary

In this PR:
* add tracing logs for the Node.js keep-alive connection code with enough context to help with debugging
* making the log level available in all modules
* guard log event generation with explicit guards making log-only code free when not used
* massaged the code to use less of `this` properties for keeping context and more the `params` that brings us closer to thread/async safe Go-like context monad
* parameterized our test even more with "all logs enabled" vs "all logs disabled" config option

## Checklist

- [x] Unit and integration tests covering the common scenarios were added
- [x] A human-readable description of the changes was provided to include in CHANGELOG

title: Add support for running the result parser in a Web/NodeJS worker
body:
### Use case

For bigger chunks it might take some significant amount of time to parse ClickHouse chunks and then parse the corresponding JSON into JS objects which leads to the event loop lag growing or even to some events timing out because of the micro-tasks.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Allows the networking and chunking code to run in a separate thread passing back only the already parsed JS objects using [structured clone](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Workers_API/Structured_clone_algorithm) mechanism. Even though this requires additional CPU cycles and memory copying the benefit of using multiple CPU cores and a separate event loop might be desirable for high load applications reading multiple heavy streams in the same JS isolate.

## Summary

Continuing the endeavor of migrating tests to Vitest.

See also:
* https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/pull/502
* https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/pull/496

## Next steps

* port all tests to Vitest

title: Bump webpack from 5.103.0 to 5.105.0
body:
Bumps [webpack](https://github.com/webpack/webpack) from 5.103.0 to 5.105.0.
Release notes

Sourced from webpack's releases.

v5.105.0

Minor Changes

  • Allow resolving worker module by export condition name when using new Worker() (by @​hai-x in #20353)

  • Detect conditional imports to avoid compile-time linking errors for non-existent exports. (by @​hai-x in #20320)

  • Added the tsconfig option for the resolver options (replacement for tsconfig-paths-webpack-plugin). Can be false (disabled), true (use the default tsconfig.json file to search for it), a string path to tsconfig.json, or an object with configFile and references options. (by @​alexander-akait in #20400)

  • Support import.defer() for context modules. (by @​ahabhgk in #20399)

  • Added support for array values ​​to the devtool option. (by @​hai-x in #20191)

  • Improve rendering node built-in modules for ECMA module output. (by @​hai-x in #20255)

  • Unknown import.meta properties are now determined at runtime instead of being statically analyzed at compile time. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #20312)

Patch Changes

  • Fixed ESM default export handling for .mjs files in Module Federation (by @​y-okt in #20189)

  • Optimized import.meta.env handling in destructuring assignments by using cached stringified environment definitions. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #20313)

  • Respect the stats.errorStack option in stats output. (by @​samarthsinh2660 in #20258)

  • Fixed a bug where declaring a module variable in module scope would conflict with the default moduleArgument. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #20265)

  • Fix VirtualUrlPlugin to set resourceData.context for proper module resolution. Previously, when context was not set, it would fallback to the virtual scheme path (e.g., virtual:routes), which is not a valid filesystem path, causing subsequent resolve operations to fail. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #20390)

  • Fixed Worker self-import handling to support various URL patterns (e.g., import.meta.url, new URL(import.meta.url), new URL(import.meta.url, import.meta.url), new URL("./index.js", import.meta.url)). Workers that resolve to the same module are now properly deduplicated, regardless of the URL syntax used. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #20381)

  • Reuse the same async entrypoint for the same Worker URL within a module to avoid circular dependency warnings when multiple Workers reference the same resource. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #20345)

  • Fixed a bug where a self-referencing dependency would have an unused export name when imported inside a web worker. (by @​samarthsinh2660 in #20251)

  • Fix missing export generation when concatenated modules in different chunks share the same runtime in module library bundles. (by @​hai-x in #20346)

  • Fixed import.meta.env.xxx behavior: when accessing a non-existent property, it now returns empty object instead of full object at runtime. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #20289)

  • Improved parsing error reporting by adding a link to the loader documentation. (by @​gaurav10gg in #20244)

  • Fix typescript types. (by @​alexander-akait in #20305)

  • Add declaration for unused harmony import specifier. (by @​hai-x in #20286)

  • Fix compressibility of modules while retaining portability. (by @​dmichon-msft in #20287)

  • Optimize source map generation: only include ignoreList property when it has content, avoiding empty arrays in source maps. (by @​xiaoxiaojx in #20319)

  • Preserve star exports for dependencies in ECMA module output. (by @​hai-x in #20293)

* had to split to universal (a.k.a. isomorphic) `createClient()` by the help of the all-mighty copy-pasta (gonna refactor it in the following PRs) because it was causing too much coupling between to old and new setup which will likely be dramatically simplified after all the code is on Vitest (hope to have TypeScript on my side by then as now most of the imports are red in tests)
* ported the node-only tls set

UPDATE: a better approach is coming in the next PR: the client creation logic will be injected by the test setup file itself making it possible to just rely on that the proper module is used depending on the runtime (node vs web).

## Next steps

* Finish the node part
* Port the rest of common (now should be way easier because of the separate client creation code)
* compare coverage (number of lines, run on an old commit and after the full port) and remove `nyc`
* fix TS by using worskpace aware package imports
* fix imports
* extract utility code into its own internal-only package
* look into running tests against the final built code

title: Porting tests to Vitest, Part 4
body:
## Summary

This PR is rather big because the node-scpecific, common and web-specific integration tests have a lot of code in common (mostly the `@test` quasi-package and some bits of common tests). I've honestly tried to split this PR into smaller chunks, but it seems the total time spent on gradual approach would be longer.

This PR also splits the type check and lint check out of unit tests. This way we type check and lint the code only once per change and also do not block the unit and integration tests in case of a type mismatch. All checks still run, just in parallel.

title: Always resolve while draining the stream
body:
## Summary

Make sure that an already ended stream does not hang waiting for the `end` event.

While writing tests for `drainStream()` it turned out that `for await` covers all the tests cases.

title: TS/ESLint setup revamp
body:
## Summary

As the worspace-first package-aware approach is becoming the de-facto standard, we're upgrading the tooling to match the trend.

This PR isolates TS/ESLint configs and scripts per package to increase the package-grain isolation.

Note: the configs are repetitive on purpose. It's usually significantly simpler to support diverse platform configurations without turning configs into another programming area. Still, the main config is extracted. Let me know if you'd like to extract more common config options.

title: fix: check the `X-ClickHouse-Exception-Code` for error code
body:
## Summary

Ingesting:
- https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/pull/350

Use the `X-ClickHouse-Exception-Code` header (https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/8786) to detect ClickHouse errors even when the HTTP status is successful. Previously, such 200 responses were treated as successful and the exception text could surface as malformed result data; now the request is rejected with a parsed `ClickHouseError`, consistent with non-2xx error responses.

Related issue: #332 (similar issue can happen with inserts).

Changes:

- **Node.js client** (`socket_pool.ts`): a response is treated as failed when the `x-clickhouse-exception-code` header is present, even with a 2xx status.
- **Web client** (`web_connection.ts`): a 2xx `fetch` response with the header set is rejected via the existing `parseError` path.
- **Unit tests**: in both flavors simulating a 200 response with `X-ClickHouse-Exception-Code: 395` and an exception body — Node via a local `http.Server`, Web via a mocked `fetch` injected through the client config; assert `query`/`insert`/`command`/`exec` all reject with a `ClickHouseError` (proper `code`, `type`, `message`).
- **Integration test** (`packages/client-common/__tests__/integration/exception_header.test.ts`): runs against a real ClickHouse server using `send_progress_in_http_headers: 1` and `http_headers_progress_interval_ms: '100'` to reproduce the exact scenario where ClickHouse commits to HTTP 200 before an exception fires (via `throwIf` at row 10 with `sleepEachRow` and `max_block_size = 1`), then asserts the client rejects with a `ClickHouseError` carrying `code: '395'`. The test lives in `client-common` so it runs under both the Node.js and Web vitest configurations.
- **CHANGELOG**: added a `1.21.0` Bug Fixes entry.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit and integration tests covering the common scenarios were added
- [x] A human-readable description of the changes was provided to include in CHANGELOG

title: Consolidate 11 Vitest configs into 2 runtime-specific configs
body:
## Summary

Reduces Vitest configuration files from 11 to 3 by consolidating them into package-centric configs that use `TEST_MODE` environment variable for scenario selection. All test coverage preserved, CI workflows unchanged.

**Changes:**
- **Created**: `vitest.client-{common,node,web}.config.ts` with multi-mode support via `TEST_MODE` env var
- **Removed**: 9 redundant config files (common/node/web unit/integration/tls/jwt/all variants)
- **Updated**: package.json test scripts to use TEST_MODE, CONTRIBUTING.md test commands

**Config modes:**
```typescript
// vitest.client-common.config.ts
TEST_MODE=unit          // unit tests (default)
TEST_MODE=integration   // integration tests
TEST_MODE=unit-web      // unit tests in browser

// vitest.client-node.config.ts  
TEST_MODE=unit          // unit tests (default)
TEST_MODE=integration   // integration + common integration
TEST_MODE=tls           // TLS tests
TEST_MODE=all           // all tests with coverage

// vitest.client-web.config.ts
TEST_MODE=all           // all web tests (default)
TEST_MODE=jwt           // JWT auth tests
```

**Example usage:**
```bash
npm run test:common:unit      # TEST_MODE=unit vitest -c vitest.client-common.config.ts
npm run test:node:tls         # TEST_MODE=tls vitest -c vitest.client-node.config.ts
npm run test:web              # TEST_MODE=all vitest -c vitest.client-web.config.ts
```

title: Codecov for Web
body: ## Summary Add coverage support to the web client. This brings us closer to per-environment coverage which we can then gather in one go per each step of the matrix (Codecov docs say it's ok to have <100 uploads per workflow). https://app.codecov.io/github/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/commit/e6dff6a4d3c2735c8779381fbcdff169e906d928/tree/packages?dropdown=coverage

title: Export each job code coverage using OTEL
body:
## Summary

As far as the OTEL exporting is set up in this repo it should be handy to also export coverage with a greater level of detail to allow per file per job coverage tracing helping to track down degradations down to a commit. On top of this metrics can be sliced and diced in any way the modern stack allows.

We'd need to run it in parallel with Codecov for some time to see if these two solutions are in sync.

Based on the direction of:
* https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/pull/558

In this PR:
* adding a tiny script (this time in JS 👍) that exports Vitest standard code coverage stats as OTEL metrics
* breaking web tests into matrices too allowing to per-browser coverage tracking (and also evening out job running times)
* exporting a coverage report per job as it's cheap (just about a thousand of metric events per workflow run) and fast  (~1 sec)

This solution should also allow scaling up past the hypothetical 100 exports limit set by Codecov without reorganasing the workflow and/or using artifacts.

* make the test client function simpler by completely relying on the setup specific create function
* also tidy up package scripts to explicitly use the proper config

This should help us merge Vitest configs next time we touch the test infra.

title: Enable OTEL for Web too
body:
## Summary

Following the lead of the Node.js runner, adding OTEL instrumentation to the Browser runners too.

Right now it's off by default (except for the Vitest telemetry itself) as it's unstable in CI and it's not yet the focus to make it work smoothly. Locally it works as expected.

title: Guard query logging with `unsafeLogUnredactedQueries` flag
body:
## Summary

Queries were being logged indirectly through URL parameters without checking the `unsafeLogUnredactedQueries` flag, potentially exposing sensitive data in logs even when users hadn't opted in.

**Fixed locations:**
- `logResponse()`: Redacts `query` parameter from `request_params` (URL search params) before logging, preserving the `?` prefix for log format compatibility
- `logRequestError()`: Redacts `query` parameter from `search_params` before logging

Both Insert operations and some Exec/Command operations send queries as URL parameters, which were being logged at DEBUG and ERROR levels respectively.

**Additional changes:**
- Added `lint:fix` scripts to workspace packages for pre-commit hook compatibility
- Added comprehensive test coverage for query redaction behavior in both DEBUG response logs and ERROR request logs
- Maintained backward compatibility with existing log formats

## Checklist

- [x] Unit and integration tests covering the common scenarios were added

title: Fixing the flaky server down test in CI, Attempt 3
body:
## Summary

* switching to probing `127.0.0.1` explicitly to rule the IPv6 out

Otherwise Node.js returns an [AggregateError](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/AggregateError) with both `127.0` and `::1` tried. It also makes this test slower to probe both.

title: ResultSet.json() may throw "Stream has been already consumed" on first call (JSONEachRow)
body:
### Describe the bug

`ResultSet.json()` can throw `Error: Stream has been already consumed` on the **first** read for `JSONEachRow`, even when `text()`/`stream()`/`json()` were never called before on that `ResultSet`.

This appears related to a timing window where the underlying stream is already ended before `json()` delegates to `stream()`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use `@clickhouse/client` with a fast `JSONEachRow` query.
2. Execute many short queries in a loop (or with concurrency).
3. Call `.json()` once for each result.

Example script:

```ts
import { createClient } from '@clickhouse/client'

const client = createClient({
  url: process.env.CLICKHOUSE_HOST!,
  database: process.env.CLICKHOUSE_DB,
  username: process.env.CLICKHOUSE_USER,
  password: process.env.CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD,
})

async function main() {
  for (let i = 0; i < 5000; i++) {
    const rs = await client.query({
      query: 'SELECT number FROM numbers(1)',
      format: 'JSONEachRow',
    })

    // Yielding to event loop increases likelihood on very fast responses.
    await new Promise((r) => setImmediate(r))

    await rs.json() // sometimes throws: "Stream has been already consumed"
  }
}

main().catch((e) => {
  console.error(e)
  process.exit(1)
})
```

### Expected behaviour

If this is the first consumption call, `json()` should either:
- parse successfully, or
- return a deterministic error that clarifies expected consumption timing.

It is surprising to receive "already consumed" when no prior consumer was used.

### Code example

Related code path in current client:
- `json()` checks `this._stream.readableEnded`, then calls `this.stream()`
- `stream()` checks `this._stream.readableEnded` again and throws

(Observed in `dist/result_set.js` in 1.17.0)

### Error log

```txt
Error: Stream has been already consumed
    at ResultSet.stream (.../result_set.js:135:19)
    at ResultSet.json (.../result_set.js:113:33)
```

### Configuration

#### Environment

- Client version: 1.17.0
- Language version: Node.js v24.13.0
- OS: Windows 11 (also observed in Linux deployment)

#### ClickHouse server

- ClickHouse Server version: 24.x
- ClickHouse Server non-default settings, if any: none relevant
- `CREATE TABLE` statements for tables involved: not applicable (uses `numbers()` table function)
- Sample data for all these tables, use [clickhouse-obfuscator](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/programs/obfuscator/Obfuscator.cpp#L42-L80) if necessary

Not sharing app-internal code/logs here intentionally; happy to provide extra minimal repro details if needed.

title: Split public and internal `drainStream` and cover with tests
body:
`drainStream` previously hung when the server closed the connection before emitting `end`, and had no coverage for terminal stream states (already errored/ended/closed) that create race conditions if encountered before listeners are attached.

## Changes

- **`stream.ts`**: Split into two functions:
  - `drainStream(stream)` — simplified public API (no context), exported from package entrypoint; adds early-exit guards for `errored`, `readableEnded`, and `closed` states; resolves on `close` event to handle server-side connection teardown before `end`
  - `drainStreamInternal(ctx, stream)` — internal variant used by `node_base_connection.ts`; same logic plus TRACE-level logging of chunk counts, byte totals, and drain duration
- **`node_base_connection.ts`**: Switched all call sites from `drainStream` to `drainStreamInternal`
- **`node_stream.test.ts`** / **`node_stream_internal.test.ts`**: New unit test suites covering normal end, already-ended, already-errored, live error, thrown error, and already-closed stream states for both functions

## Checklist

- [x] Unit and integration tests covering the common scenarios were added
- [ ] A human-readable description of the changes was provided to include in CHANGELOG
- [ ] For significant changes, documentation in https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-docs was updated with further explanations or tutorials

title: Add use_multipart_params option for large query parameters
body:
## Summary

- Adds a `use_multipart_params` client config option (default: `false`) that sends query parameters as `multipart/form-data` parts instead of URL query string entries
- When enabled, `query()` moves the SQL into a `query` multipart part and each `param_*` entry into its own named part, avoiding URL length limits that cause HTTP 400 on ClickHouse Cloud with large arrays (25K+ values)
- Uses the multipart format supported by ClickHouse since https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/40055
- Builds multipart bodies natively with `Buffer.concat()` — no new dependencies
- All non-param URL search params (database, query_id, settings, session_id, role) remain in the URL as-is

## Test plan

- [x] 7 unit tests for `buildMultipartBody()`: query part, param naming, array formatting, boundary structure, ordering, Buffer type, special character escaping
- [x] 7 unit tests for connection-level integration: params removed from URL, Content-Type header set with boundary, non-param search params preserved in URL, fallback to normal behavior when params are empty/undefined, default (non-multipart) behavior unchanged
- [x] All 77 existing Node.js unit tests pass
- [x] All 155 existing common unit tests pass
- [ ] Manual E2E test with ClickHouse instance using large array params

title: Add CI step to run examples against ClickHouse and fix example errors
body:
## Summary

Adds a CI job that executes all compatible examples in `./examples` against a live ClickHouse instance (both `head` and `latest`), and fixes two runtime bugs discovered in the process.

### CI / runner script

- **`examples/run-examples.mjs`** — new script that runs all examples sequentially via `tsx`, with:
  - **Skip** logic for infrastructure-dependent examples (TLS, cluster, ClickHouse Cloud, production long-running demo)
  - **Graceful SIGTERM** for examples designed to run indefinitely (`async_insert_without_waiting.ts`, `node/insert_streaming_with_backpressure.ts`) — runs them for 5 s then stops them
  - Non-zero exit on any failure with full stdout/stderr output
- **`examples/package.json`** — added `run-examples` script
- **`.github/workflows/tests.yml`** — new `run-examples` job (matrix: `head`/`latest` ClickHouse), added to the `success` gate

### Bug fixes in examples

1. **`examples/custom_json_handling.ts`** — `valueSerializer` only handled top-level `BigInt`/`Date`/`Array`, so inserting an object like `{ id: BigInt(...), dt: new Date() }` threw `TypeError: Do not know how to serialize a BigInt`. Fixed by adding recursive object traversal:
   ```ts
   if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null) {
     return Object.fromEntries(
       Object.entries(value).map(([k, v]) => [k, valueSerializer(v)]),
     )
   }
   ```

2. **`examples/node/insert_streaming_with_backpressure.ts`** — `CREATE OR REPLACE ${tableName}` was missing the `TABLE` keyword, causing a ClickHouse syntax error (`code 62`).

- [ ] Unit and integration tests covering the common scenarios were added
- [x] A human-readable description of the changes was provided to include in CHANGELOG

title: Fix ResultSet.json() race condition on JSONEachRow streams
body:
## Summary

Fix `ResultSet.json()` throwing "Stream has been already consumed" on the **first** call for `JSONEachRow` format due to a race condition between two `readableEnded` checks.

Fixes #575

## Root Cause

For streamable JSON formats (JSONEachRow, etc.), `json()` calls `stream()` internally:

1. `json()` checks `this._stream.readableEnded` → **false** ✓
2. `json()` calls `this.stream()` 
3. **Race window**: Stream receives all data and fires 'end' event → `readableEnded` becomes **true**
4. `stream()` checks `this._stream.readableEnded` → **true** ✗
5. Throws: `"Stream has been already consumed"` — on the first call!

This is triggered by fast/small responses (e.g. `SELECT number FROM numbers(1)`) where the response arrives fully before `json()` reaches the `stream()` call.

## Fix (44 insertions, 2 files)

**`packages/client-node/src/result_set.ts`:**
- Add `_consumed` boolean flag to `ResultSet` class
- Add `markAsConsumed()` private method that checks `_consumed || readableEnded` and sets `_consumed = true` synchronously
- `text()`, `json()`, `stream()` all call `markAsConsumed()` as their first operation
- Split `stream()` into public `stream()` (with check) and private `_streamImpl()` (without check)
- `json()` calls `_streamImpl()` after already calling `markAsConsumed()`, eliminating the double-check race

This matches the pattern already used by the **web client's** `ResultSet` which uses `isAlreadyConsumed` boolean.

**`packages/client-node/__tests__/unit/node_result_set.test.ts`:**
- Add regression test that yields to the event loop (`setImmediate`) before calling `json()`, simulating the race condition

## Test Plan

- [x] New unit test for the race condition scenario
- [ ] CI (full test suite)
- Existing consumption tests (`text()`, `json()`, `stream()` only-once) continue to pass since `markAsConsumed()` covers all the same cases

v2.6.0

2.6.0

  • fix(resources): update OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTESopen-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification#4856#6261 @​jacksonweber
    • Important: This fix is included in the "breaking changes" section because it can be breaking for some edge case usage of OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES:
      • export OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=foo=bar,spam will now be fully ignored, because the spam entry is invalid (missing =). Per spec, any parsing error results in ignoring the entire environment variable.

Before this change the implementation included brittle double-quoting to allow leading and trailing whitespace in the value. title: [parquet]: failed to parse the message length
body:
<!-- delete unnecessary items -->

### Describe the bug

I try to stream a select query with the parquet format:

```
const result = await clickhouse.query({
     query: sql,
     query_params,
     format: "Parquet",
});
for await (const chunk of result.stream()) {
// do something
}
```

while it actually yields (at least some) chunks, `@clickhouse/client` prints this error on the console:

```
[2026-03-11T16:45:35.080Z][ERROR][@clickhouse/client][Client] Error while processing the ResultSet. 
Arguments: {
  session_id: undefined,
  role: undefined,
  query_id: "65fd505e-e04b-43d5-a728-b961ad2650e3",
} 
Caused by: 34 |             --errMsgLenStartIdx;
35 |         } while (chunk[errMsgLenStartIdx] !== NEWLINE);
36 |         const textDecoder = new TextDecoder('utf-8');
37 |         const errMsgLen = parseInt(textDecoder.decode(chunk.subarray(errMsgLenStartIdx, -bytesCountAfterErrLenHint)));
38 |         if (isNaN(errMsgLen) || errMsgLen <= 0) {
39 |             return new Error('there was an error in the stream; failed to parse the message length');
                            ^
error: there was an error in the stream; failed to parse the message length
      at extractErrorAtTheEndOfChunk (/.../node_modules/@clickhouse/client-common/dist/utils/stream.js:39:24)
      at transform (/.../node_modules/@clickhouse/client/dist/result_set.js:150:41)
      at internal:streams/transform:51:18
      at writeOrBuffer (internal:streams/writable:283:70)
      at internal:streams/writable:249:16
      at ondata (internal:streams/readable:456:19)
      at emit (node:events:95:22)
      at addChunk (internal:streams/readable:265:47)
      at readableAddChunkPushByteMode (internal:streams/readable:243:18)
      at consumeStream (node:_http_incoming:280:20)
```

it might depend on my specific query/data, which of course is a bit hard to share. but perhaps this message already shows that something is off.

#### Environment

- Client version: 1.10.1
- Language version: bun@1.3.10
- OS:

#### ClickHouse server

- ClickHouse Server version: 26.2-alpine
- `CREATE TABLE` statements for tables involved:

```
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS logs
      (
        chain_id          UInt32,
        block_number      UInt64                   CODEC(Delta, ZSTD(3)),
        block_hash        FixedString(32)          CODEC(ZSTD(6)),
        timestamp         UInt32                   CODEC(DoubleDelta, ZSTD(3)),
        transaction_hash  FixedString(32)          CODEC(ZSTD(6)),
        transaction_index UInt32                   CODEC(Delta, ZSTD(3)),
        log_index         UInt32                   CODEC(Delta, ZSTD(3)),
        address           FixedString(20)          CODEC(ZSTD(6)),
        data              String                   CODEC(ZSTD(9)),
        topic0            FixedString(32)          CODEC(ZSTD(6)),
        topic1            Nullable(FixedString(32)) CODEC(ZSTD(6)),
        topic2            Nullable(FixedString(32)) CODEC(ZSTD(6)),
        topic3            Nullable(FixedString(32)) CODEC(ZSTD(6)),
        removed           UInt8
      ) ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree()
      ORDER BY (chain_id, topic0, block_number, log_index, address)
      SETTINGS index_granularity = 8192
```

title: Fix exception tests in CI
body:
## Summary

Fixes cloud CI.

* remove global version cache logic to allow each test request the version explicitly (less state to manage across tests)
* explicitly request the out-of-format exceptions as the server config changes over time breaking the tests
* add more retrospective CH versions to CI (they're virtually free and fast)
* retry racy tests until we get around the `sleep(0)` trick
* setting the default CH server docker version to `head` locally (required `down` -> `up` or `--rebuild` to take action)

title: Replace `run-examples.mjs` with Vitest parallel executor
body:
## Summary

Replaces the bespoke sequential `examples/run-examples.mjs` orchestrator with a Vitest config that runs all compatible examples in parallel using Vitest's `forks` pool — no changes to any example source file.

### Key design decisions

- **`vitest.examples.config.ts`** — root-level Vitest config with:
  - An `await-examples` Vite transform plugin that rewrites `void (async () => {` → `await (async () => {` at compile time, turning each example's top-level IIFE into a top-level `await` so Vitest correctly waits for completion and captures errors — without touching example source.
  - Same exclusion list as the old script (TLS, Cloud, cluster, long-running, infinite-loop examples).
  - `pool: 'forks'` for OS-process isolation; resolve aliases pointing to local `@clickhouse/client` / `@clickhouse/client-common` source.

- **`vitest.examples.setup.ts`** — per-fork setup:
  - `process.chdir('examples/')` so resource-file paths like `./node/resources/data.csv` resolve correctly when Vitest runs from the repo root.
  - `process.exit` override: `exit(0)` → no-op (some examples use it as a final success signal that Vitest would otherwise intercept as an error); `exit(≠0)` → throws a captured `Error`.

title: Fix OTEL SDK teardown errors breaking CI with vitest 4.1.0
body:
## Summary

vitest 4.1.0 (bumped by dependabot) now awaits and propagates OTEL SDK `shutdown()` errors as fatal. When `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is unavailable, the SDK falls back to `localhost:4318`, fails with `ECONNREFUSED` on teardown, and the entire test run exits with code 1 — even though all tests passed.

- **`vitest.node.otel.js`**: Export a `Proxy` wrapping the SDK instead of the raw instance. Intercepts `shutdown()` and `forceFlush()` to catch and warn on errors rather than propagate them. All other SDK method/property access is forwarded transparently via `Reflect.get`.

title: `Date` objects with non-zero milliseconds produce fractional timestamps rejected by `{param:DateTime}`
body:
<!-- delete unnecessary items -->

### Describe the bug

When `Date` objects' milliseconds is not zero, its serialization (https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/blob/22e8610f8731bc7dfd24eeb9c08de1b2a17b0c94/packages/client-common/src/data_formatter/format_query_params.ts#L85) produces fractional timestamps (e.g `1773935682.595`), which are rejected by clickhouse service if the query param is of type `DateTime`, with the following error: `Error: Value 1773935682.595 cannot be parsed as DateTime for query parameter 'startDate' because it isn't parsed completely: only 10 of 14 bytes was parsed: 1773935682`. 
The workaround is to use parameter type `DateTime64(3)` in the query.

The official example at `examples/query_with_parameter_binding.ts` comments `// or a Date object` on the `{var_datetime: DateTime}` param, but this only works when `date.getUTCMilliseconds() === 0`. The client's `formatQueryParams` appends `.XXX` for non-zero ms, which `DateTime` rejects.

**Note**: using `date_time_input_format: "best_effort"` does not fix this.

### Steps to reproduce

```typescript
import { createClient } from '@clickhouse/client';
const client = createClient({ url: 'http://localhost:8123' });

const date = new Date('2025-03-19T10:30:00.500Z');

// FAILS: "Value 1742553000.500 cannot be parsed as DateTime"
await client.query({
  query: `SELECT {d:DateTime} AS dt`,
  query_params: { d: date },
});

// Works — DateTime64(3) accepts fractional timestamps
await client.query({
  query: `SELECT {d:DateTime64(3)} AS dt`,
  query_params: { d: date },
});
```



#### ClickHouse server

- ClickHouse Server version: 26.2.4.23

title: Port release-publisher workflow from click-ui repository

## Summary

Ports the automated release publisher workflow from [click-ui](https://github.com/ClickHouse/click-ui/blob/main/.github/workflows/release-publisher.yml) to automate npm publishing for the clickhouse-js packages.

## Changes

### Added `.scripts/bash/verify-release-commit`
- Bash script that validates release commit message format: `"Release vX.Y.Z"` or `"chore: Release vX.Y.Z"`
- Detects release type (latest, rc, beta, test, alpha) from version suffix
- Returns version and release type for workflow consumption

### Added `.github/workflows/release-publisher.yml`
- Triggers on PR merge to any branch
- Validates commit message to detect release PRs
- Creates and pushes git tags automatically
- Builds all packages via `npm run build`
- Publishes 3 workspace packages to npm: `@clickhouse/client-common`, `@clickhouse/client`, `@clickhouse/client-web`
- Uses npm provenance (`--provenance`) for supply chain security
- Creates GitHub releases with extracted changelog
- Manages maintenance branches (`chore/vX.Y.Z`)
- Includes safeguards to prevent accidental releases from main when maintenance branch exists

### Key Adaptations
- Workspace publishing: `npm --workspaces publish` instead of single package
- Node 20.x (matching repository requirements)
- npm tooling (repository standard)
- Changelog regex adjusted for `# X.Y.Z` format

title: Add GitHub Actions workflow for automated npm publishing with provenance
body:
## Summary

Adds automated npm publishing workflow that triggers on every merge to main, publishing all packages with the `head` tag using npm OIDC authentication and provenance support.

## Implementation

- **Workflow trigger**: Runs on push to main branch
- **npm OIDC authentication**: Uses `id-token: write` permission for passwordless authentication via GitHub's OIDC provider
- **Provenance**: Enables `--provenance` flag for cryptographic package attestation and supply chain security
- **Tag strategy**: Publishes with `head` tag for bleeding-edge releases
- **Workspace publishing**: Builds and publishes all three packages atomically:
  - `@clickhouse/client-common`
  - `@clickhouse/client`
  - `@clickhouse/client-web`

## Configuration

The workflow follows repository conventions:
- Pinned GitHub Actions to commit SHAs with version comments
- Uses Node.js 20 matching other workflows
- Requires `NPM_TOKEN` secret configured for authentication

## Checklist

- [x] A human-readable description of the changes was provided to include in CHANGELOG

title: Addressing PR comments
feat(ResultSet): add rawStream() to access underlying stream without row parsing
body:
## Summary

- Adds `rawStream()` method to `BaseResultSet` interface and both Node.js/Web implementations
- Returns the raw decompressed stream without the row-parsing Transform pipeline
- Useful for bulk CSV/TSV export where you want to pipe directly to a file

## Motivation

When using `.query()` with `CSVWithNames` format, the client enables HTTP gzip compression automatically (~15x smaller transfer). However, the only way to get a stream is `.stream()`, which wraps the response in a row-parsing Transform — unnecessary overhead when you just want the raw CSV bytes.

The alternative, `.exec()`, returns a raw stream but **does not enable HTTP compression**, resulting in ~3x slower transfers for large datasets.

`rawStream()` gives the best of both worlds: compressed transfer + raw byte stream.

### Benchmark (1.4M rows, 121MB CSV)

| Method | Transfer time |
|--------|--------------|
| `.exec().stream` (no compression) | ~6.3s |
| `.query().text()` (compressed, buffered) | ~2.0s |
| `.query().rawStream()` (compressed, streaming) | **~1.8s** |

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for Node.js ResultSet: rawStream returns data, throws after consumption, mutual exclusion with text/json
- [x] All existing tests pass

Langfuse provides unparalleled visibility into AI usage. Installing for the repo.

title: Refactor TTL timeout timer to use timestamp-based validation
body:
- [x] Add timestamp tracking to SocketInfo when socket is freed
- [x] Implement timestamp check when reusing socket to verify TTL hasn't expired
- [x] Destroy socket and create new connection if TTL expired based on timestamp
- [x] Keep existing timeout mechanism for proactive resource cleanup
- [x] Add tests to verify timestamp-based TTL validation
- [x] Run existing tests to ensure no regression
- [x] Enhance tests to capture and verify log messages for socket reuse behavior
- [x] Verify specific trace logs to confirm sockets are reused vs recreated
- [ ] Add test using Vitest fake timers to specifically test timestamp validation without timer firing
- [ ] Verify the "socket TTL expired based on timestamp" log message appears

title: Split the socket management code out
body:
## Summary

Extracting the connection pool logic out of the connection module. This should help with reasoning and refactoring.

title: Refactor socket TTL validation to use timestamp-based checks
body:
- [x] Fix socket TTL expiration bug - remove early return and let Node.js assign a new socket
- [x] Improve test to actually verify timestamp-based TTL check runs
- [x] Run tests to verify the fixes work correctly

## Changes

### Bug Fix in socket_pool.ts
Fixed a critical bug where destroying an expired socket and returning early from the `onSocket` handler would skip `pipeStream()` and request timeout setup, causing requests with a body to hang. Now the code:
1. Destroys the expired socket
2. Continues execution without early return
3. Checks `socket.destroyed` before updating socket info
4. Lets the destroyed socket trigger normal error handling

### Test Improvement
Enhanced the timestamp-based TTL validation test to:
1. Clear logs between test phases for focused assertions

title: Eagerly check for stale sockets
body:
Claude deleted the description reverting without formatting.

Summary
Tracks freed_at_timestamp_ms on each socket when it's returned to the pool, so its actual idle age can be measured independently of the event loop timer.
Adds a WARN log when a socket whose TTL has expired (by timestamp) is about to be reused — a signal that the event loop is delayed and idle timeouts are not firing on schedule.
Adds keep_alive.eagerly_destroy_stale_sockets config option (Node.js only, default false). When enabled, stale sockets are destroyed synchronously before each request, rather than waiting for the idle timeout to fire. This is a best-effort mitigation for CPU-starved or event-loop-delayed processes that may otherwise reuse connections the server has already closed.
Adds keep_alive.eagerly_destroy_stale_sockets config option (Node.js only, default false). When enabled, stale sockets are destroyed synchronously before each request, rather than waiting for the idle timeout to fire. The eager-destroy logic is only active when keep_alive.enabled is true and idle_socket_ttl > 0, so setting idle_socket_ttl = 0 (disabling idle socket management) correctly results in a no-op. This is a best-effort mitigation for CPU-starved or event-loop-delayed processes that may otherwise reuse connections the server has already closed.
Adds integration tests (node_eager_socket_destroy.test.ts) covering both the eager-destruction path (TRACE log emitted when a stale free socket is destroyed before a request) and the stale-reuse warning path (WARN log emitted when eagerly_destroy_stale_sockets is false and a socket whose TTL has expired by timestamp is about to be reused).

v7.0.0

v7 What's new

Direct Uploads

Adds support for uploading single files directly (unzipped). Callers can set the new archive parameter to false to skip zipping the file during upload. Right now, we only support single files. The action will fail if the glob passed resolves to multiple files. The name parameter is also ignored with this setting. Instead, the name of the artifact will be the name of the uploaded file.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

title: feat: add SQL template literal API for ergonomic query parameterization
body:
## Summary

Implements a SQL template literal API (`sql` tagged template function) as an ergonomic alternative to ClickHouse's native `{name: Type}` parameter syntax. Addresses the lack of industry-standard parameter placeholders (`$1`, `?`, `:name`) by providing JavaScript template literals with automatic type inference and built-in SQL injection protection.

**Usage:**

```typescript
import { sql, identifier } from '@clickhouse/client'

// Before: verbose type annotations required
await client.query({
  query: 'SELECT * FROM {table: Identifier} WHERE name = {name: String} AND age > {age: Int32}',
  query_params: { table: 'users', name: 'Alice', age: 30 }
})

// After: automatic type inference, familiar syntax
const tableName = 'users'
const userName = 'Alice'
const age = 30
await client.query(
  sql`SELECT * FROM ${identifier(tableName)} WHERE name = ${userName} AND age > ${age}`
)

// Composable SQL fragments
const whereClause = sql`status = ${'active'} AND verified = ${true}`
await client.query(sql`SELECT * FROM users WHERE ${whereClause}`)
```

**Implementation:**

- **Core API** (`packages/client-common/src/sql_template.ts`): Tagged template function with automatic JS→ClickHouse type mapping (string→String, number→Int32/Float64, Date→DateTime, arrays, tuples, maps)
- **Client integration**: Method overload on `ClickHouseClient.query()` accepting `SQLTemplate` objects alongside existing `QueryParams`
- **Composability**: Nested templates supported with automatic parameter renaming to avoid conflicts
- **Type safety**: `identifier()` helper for table/column names using ClickHouse's `Identifier` type

**Testing:**

- 40 unit tests covering type inference, template parsing, composability, edge cases
- 24 integration tests verifying end-to-end functionality with live ClickHouse server

**Note:** Marked as experimental in CHANGELOG. Existing `query_params` API unchanged and fully supported.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit and integration tests covering the common scenarios were added
- [x] A human-readable description of the changes was provided to include in CHANGELOG
- [ ] For significant changes, documentation in https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-docs was updated with further explanations or tutorials

title: Add client-side detection of load balancer idle timeout scenarios
body:
## Summary

Implements client-side detection of potential load balancer timeout scenarios by monitoring packet activity. A new `idle_packet_timeout` configuration parameter (default: 5 minutes) tracks when no data (headers or body chunks) is received from the server, helping distinguish LB idle timeouts from query execution timeouts.

## Changes

### Configuration
- Added `idle_packet_timeout` parameter to `BaseClickHouseClientConfigOptions` (default: 300,000ms)
- Configurable per-client or can be disabled by setting to `0`

### Implementation
- Idle packet timer starts when request begins
- Timer resets on response headers receipt
- Timer resets on each data chunk received from response stream
- Timer cleared when stream ends, errors, or closes
- On timeout, request aborted with descriptive error: `"Idle packet timeout: no data received from the server for Xms. This might indicate a load balancer idle timeout."`
- Comprehensive logging at TRACE and WARN levels

### Usage Example

```ts
const client = createClient({
  request_timeout: 400_000,      // Total request timeout
  idle_packet_timeout: 300_000,  // Abort if no packets for 5 minutes
})
```

For long-running queries (e.g., `INSERT FROM SELECT`), this helps detect when a load balancer silently drops the connection while the server is still processing, rather than waiting for the full `request_timeout` to expire.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit and integration tests covering the common scenarios were added
- [x] A human-readable description of the changes was provided to include in CHANGELOG
- [x] For significant changes, documentation in https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-docs was updated with further explanations or tutorials

title: Bug: parseEnumType returns escaped backslashes in enum names instead of unescaping them
body:
## Bug Description

When parsing Enum types with escaped single quotes in their names (e.g. `Enum8('f\'' = 1)`), the `parseEnumType` function returns the raw escaped form of the name (`f\'`) instead of the unescaped form (`f'`).

## Root Cause

In `packages/client-common/src/parse/column_types.ts`, the `parseEnumType` function correctly identifies escape sequences to find the closing quote, but does not unescape the extracted name:

```ts
// ~line 330
const name = columnType.slice(startIndex, i)
// name is 'f\'' (with backslash) instead of 'f'' (without)
```

## Example

```ts
parseEnumType({ columnType: "Enum8('f\\'' = 1)", sourceType: "Enum8('f\\'' = 1)" })
// returns: { values: { 1: "f\\'" } }   <- includes backslash (wrong)
// expected: { values: { 1: "f'" } }    <- unescaped (correct)
```

## Related

Reported via cross-repo analysis from ClickHouse/integrations-ai-playground#17.

title: Create cross-repo-bug-relay.yml
body:
Sets up new issue relay for cross-repo investigation.

If you'd rather trigger this on labeling an issue a bug we can do this instead:

```
  on:
    issues:
      types: [labeled]

  permissions: {}

  jobs:
    relay:
      if: github.event.label.name == 'bug'
      uses: ClickHouse/integrations-shared-workflows/.github/workflows/cross-repo-bug-relay.yml@main
      secrets: inherit
```

But there's a triage before the cross-repo investigation that filters out irrelevant issues.

## Summary

Each examples package declared `"@clickhouse/client(-web)": "latest"` in `package.json`, but its `vitest.config.ts` set `resolve.alias` redirecting `@clickhouse/client`, `@clickhouse/client-web`, and `@clickhouse/client-common` to this repo's `packages/*/src`. ## Summary

`vitest.examples.config.ts` skipped 9 examples via `EXCLUDED_EXAMPLES` (Cloud, cluster, TLS, "long-running" demos, indefinite loops). This PR makes all examples runnable by `npm run run-examples` within ~1 minute by handling the special cases at runtime through env vars instead of a static exclude list.

- **`vitest.examples.config.ts`** — empty `EXCLUDED_EXAMPLES`; add `CLICKHOUSE_TLS_URL`, `CLICKHOUSE_CLUSTER_URL`, `EXAMPLE_RUN_DURATION_MS=8000`, `EXAMPLE_LONG_QUERY_MAX_POLLS=60` defaults under `test.env`.
- **Cloud examples** (`create_table_cloud.ts`, node + web) — runtime-skip via `process.exit(0)` (already shimmed by `vitest.examples.setup.ts`) when `CLICKHOUSE_CLOUD_URL` is unset; otherwise read `CLICKHOUSE_CLOUD_URL` / `CLICKHOUSE_CLOUD_PASSWORD`. Engine-less DDL preserved.
- **Cluster examples** (`create_table_on_premise_cluster.ts`, node + web) — URL via `CLICKHOUSE_CLUSTER_URL`; idempotent `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS … ON CLUSTER '{cluster}' SYNC` then `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS … ON CLUSTER '{cluster}' …`.
- **TLS examples** (`basic_tls.ts`, `mutual_tls.ts`) — URL via `CLICKHOUSE_TLS_URL`; the `run-examples` CI job now adds the `server.clickhouseconnect.test → 127.0.0.1` `/etc/hosts` mapping (matching the step already used by other jobs).
- **`long_running_queries_progress_headers.ts`** (node + web) — just unexcluded; the actual work finishes in ms.
- **`long_running_queries_cancel_request.ts`** — `maxPolls` now `Number(process.env['EXAMPLE_LONG_QUERY_MAX_POLLS'] ?? 400)`; production-like default preserved.
- **`async_insert_without_waiting.ts`** — schedules `setTimeout(gracefulShutdown, EXAMPLE_RUN_DURATION_MS)` when set; default `0` keeps the run-forever interactive behavior.
- **`insert_streaming_with_backpressure.ts`** — `SimulatedDataSource` accepts an optional `maxRows` so the demo terminates naturally when `EXAMPLE_RUN_DURATION_MS>0`; fix unguarded burst-mode `setInterval` leak (now stored and cleared in `stop()`); `cleanup` made re-entrancy-safe; correct stream drain on source `end`.
- **`examples/README.md`** — document the new env vars and update Cloud example var names (`CLICKHOUSE_URL`/`PASSWORD` → `CLICKHOUSE_CLOUD_URL`/`PASSWORD`).

> ⚠️ Validation gap: individual previously-excluded files pass when run alone, but a full-suite `npm run run-examples` did not finish in the time available — likely fork concurrency pressure from the indefinite-loop demos sharing the single-node server. Worth investigating `poolOptions.forks.maxForks: 1` (or `fileParallelism: false`) before merge, plus running `npm run lint`/`npm run typecheck` in `examples/{node,web}`.

title: Skip no-op npm head publishes
body:
## Summary

The `head` publish workflow runs on every merge to `main` and unconditionally publishes a new pre-release of all three packages, even when nothing in `packages/` actually changed or when the change was a no-op for the packed contents (e.g. README/CI tweaks, comment-only edits). This results in churn of meaningless `head` versions on npm.

Two gates are added to the `head` job in `.github/workflows/publish.yml`; the `latest` (manual `workflow_dispatch`) job is unchanged.

- **Path-based gate**: checkout uses `fetch-depth: 0` and the job short-circuits if `git diff ${{ github.event.before }}..${{ github.sha }} -- packages/` is empty. Falls back to `HEAD^` for the all-zeros `before` SHA.
- **Content-based gate (all-or-nothing)**: after build, each workspace is `npm pack`ed and its tarball compared to the currently-published `head` tarball pulled via `npm view <pkg>@head dist.tarball`. We publish iff at least one of `client-common`, `client-node`, `client-web` differs — they are treated as a unit because the node/web clients pin `client-common` by exact version. Missing `head` tag or `npm view` failure is treated as "differs"; a real registry outage will surface in the publish step.
- **`.scripts/pkg_content_hash.sh`** (new): computes a deterministic SHA-256 over an unpacked tarball after normalizing `package.json` `version` and the `@clickhouse/client-common` dependency version to a fixed placeholder, so two packs that differ only in their head pre-release suffix hash equal.

## Checklist

- [x] A human-readable description of the changes was provided to include in CHANGELOG

title: Restrict head npm publish workflow to package-relevant changes
body:
## Summary

The `head` npm publish job in `.github/workflows/publish.yml` runs on every push to `main`, including merges that touch only docs, examples, or other non-package files. This adds a `paths` filter to the `push` trigger so it only fires when files that affect the published packages change.

- **Path filter** added under `on.push.paths`:
  - `packages/**` — any change to `client-common`, `client-node`, or `client-web`
  - `package.json`, `package-lock.json` — root dep changes that affect builds
  - `tsconfig.base.json` — shared TS config extended by all packages
  - `README.md`, `LICENSE` — copied into every package by the `prepack` scripts
  - `skills/**` — copied into `client-node` by its `prepack` script
  - `.scripts/update_version.sh` — invoked by the workflow to set the head version
  - `.github/workflows/publish.yml` — re-trigger on workflow edits
- **All-or-nothing publish preserved**: because `client-web`/`client-node` depend on `client-common`, any change under `packages/**` triggers publishing of all three. Per-package filtering is intentionally deferred.
- **`latest` job unchanged**: it is `workflow_dispatch`-only and unaffected by push path filters.

title: Split examples into use-case folders for sharp AI agent skills
body:
## Summary

Reorganizes the flat `examples/node` and `examples/web` directories into intent-driven use-case folders so each folder is a self-contained corpus that can back a focused AI agent skill.

### Layout

```
examples/{node,web}/
  coding/                   # day-to-day API: configure, ping, basic insert/select, params, sessions, types, custom JSON
  performance/              # async/streaming/backpressure/file-stream/progress/INSERT FROM SELECT — node only
  troubleshooting/          # abort/cancel, timeouts, long-running progress, server errors, BigInt pitfalls
  security/                 # TLS (node only), RBAC, parameter binding
  schema-and-deployments/   # CREATE TABLE per deployment shape + URL config + column-shape features
```

`examples/web` has no `performance/` folder — every perf example depends on Node-only APIs.

### Intentional duplication

10 logical examples appear in more than one folder so each category stays self-contained instead of forcing cross-folder references. Each duplicate has a designated *primary* location; secondary copies are listed in `exclude` of the per-package `vitest.config.ts`, keeping CI runtime unchanged (51 node + 34 web test files, matching the pre-split counts). The full duplicate map and the "edit every copy" rule are documented in `examples/README.md`.

### Wiring

- `examples/{node,web}/vitest.config.ts`: `include` switched from `['*.ts']` to `['**/*.ts']`; `exclude` extended with secondary-copy paths.
- `vitest.setup.ts` `chdir` to `examples/` is unchanged, so existing `./node/resources/...` paths in moved files keep resolving.
- No CI workflow, dependency, or tooling changes — the existing `working-directory: examples/${{ matrix.package }}` jobs cover the new layout.

### Documentation

- `examples/README.md` rewritten with category-grouped tables (Node and Web columns side-by-side) plus the duplicate-editing rule.
- New `examples/node/README.md` and `examples/web/README.md` index the categories.
- `AGENTS.md` Examples section extended with the category layout and duplication rule.
