title: [backfill: ClickHouse/clickhouse-js] insert columns parameter does not backtick-quote identifiers with spaces/special chars
body:
## Target client repo
`ClickHouse/clickhouse-js`

## Severity
`sev:1` — visible server-side syntax error (not silent corruption), and a trivial client-side workaround exists: callers can pre-quote the identifier themselves (e.g. `` columns: ['`test id`', 'name'] ``). The default `JSONEachRow` insert path that omits the `columns` parameter is unaffected, since ClickHouse parses column names from the JSON object keys.

## Description
When calling `client.insert(...)` with a `columns` array whose entries contain spaces (or other characters that require identifier quoting in ClickHouse SQL), the generated `INSERT INTO ... (cols) FORMAT ...` statement bakes the raw strings into the SQL without backtick-escaping, and the server rejects it with a syntax error.

The relevant code joins user-supplied column names verbatim:

```ts
// packages/client-common/src/client.ts (getInsertQuery)
if (Array.isArray(params.columns) && params.columns.length > 0) {
  columnsPart = ` (${params.columns.join(', ')})`
}
// ...
return `INSERT INTO ${params.table.trim()}${columnsPart} FORMAT ${format}`
```

For `columns: ['test id', 'name']` this produces `INSERT INTO test.numbers (test id, name) FORMAT JSONEachRow`, which fails to parse server-side (`Syntax error: failed at position ...: id, name) FORMAT ...`). The same applies to the `* EXCEPT (...)` branch.

## ClickHouse server version
Code analysis only; not verified against a running server.

## Reproduction

```ts
import { createClient } from '@clickhouse/client'

const client = createClient({ url: 'http://localhost:8123' })

await client.command({
  query:
    "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS test_numbers (`test id` UInt64, name String) ENGINE = Memory",
})

// FAILS: generated SQL is `INSERT INTO test_numbers (test id, name) FORMAT JSONEachRow`
await client.insert({
  table: 'test_numbers',
  values: [{ 'test id': 1, name: 'one' }],
  format: 'JSONEachRow',
  columns: ['test id', 'name'],
})
```

Expected: insert succeeds (or the client errors with a clearer client-side message about identifier quoting).
Actual: server returns `Code: 62. DB::Exception: Syntax error ... Expected one of: token, ClosingRoundBracket, Comma, Dot`.

Note: the same insert without the `columns` parameter works, because ClickHouse extracts column names from the `JSONEachRow` keys itself. The bug is specific to the `columns` (and `columns.except`) parameter path.

Workaround for users today: pre-quote the column names in the array, e.g. `` columns: ['`test id`', 'name'] ``.

## Suggested fix
In `getInsertQuery` (`packages/client-common/src/client.ts`), wrap each identifier with backticks and escape any embedded backticks before joining, e.g.:

```ts
const quoteIdent = (s: string) => '`' + s.replace(/`/g, '``') + '`'
columnsPart = ` (${params.columns.map(quoteIdent).join(', ')})`
// ...and the same for the `except` branch
```

This matches how ClickHouse itself quotes identifiers and is safe for already-simple names. (If existing users have been pre-quoting their column names as a workaround, the change would need to detect and skip already-backticked input, or be released as a documented behavior change.)

## Source bug
Relayed from https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-cpp/issues/30

title: [backfill: ClickHouse/clickhouse-js] Array(Date) query parameter binding fails: Date elements serialized as bare Unix timestamps not accepted by Array(Date) parser
body:
**Target client repo:** `ClickHouse/clickhouse-js`

**Severity:** `sev:2` — visible parse error (not silent corruption) on a real-world type (`Array(Date)`) with no flag-flip workaround. User has to change the parameter type in the query or convert each `Date` to a string client-side, neither of which is a config toggle. Not sev:3 because `Array(Date)` is not as ubiquitous as scalar `Date`/`DateTime`/`Decimal`, and the error is loud rather than corrupting data.

**Source bug:** https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-connect/issues/188 (Python clickhouse-connect; this is the JS port of the same class of bug — server cannot parse the array literal the client serializes for `Array(Date)` parameters).

## Description

`formatQueryParams` (`packages/client-common/src/data_formatter/format_query_params.ts:79-88`) serializes a JS `Date` as a bare Unix-seconds integer (e.g. `1683244800`). Inside an array literal this becomes `[1683244800]`. ClickHouse accepts that as `Array(DateTime)` but rejects it for `Array(Date)`:

```
Code: 27. DB::Exception: Cannot parse input: expected '\'' before: '1683244800]':
value [1683244800] cannot be parsed as Array(Date) for query parameter 'l'.
(CANNOT_PARSE_INPUT_ASSERTION_FAILED)
```

So passing `[new Date()]` as the value for `{l:Array(Date)}` fails the entire query. The corresponding scalar case `{d:Date}` also fails (`new Date()` → bare `1683244800`, and `Date` parser rejects unquoted integers), but the issue title focuses on the array case since that mirrors the source bug.

The Python bug was that the client emitted unquoted `'2023-05-05'` inside the array. The JS bug surfaces the same class — element serialization that the server-side `Array(Date)` parser refuses — through a different concrete encoding (unquoted integer rather than unquoted bare-date-string).

## ClickHouse server version

Verified against `26.4.2.10` (the Docker Compose stack the repo's tests use) via direct HTTP:

```bash
$ curl -s 'http://localhost:8123/?param_l=%5B1659081134%5D' -d 'SELECT {l:Array(Date)}'
Code: 27. DB::Exception: Cannot parse input: expected '\'' before: '1659081134]':
value [1659081134] cannot be parsed as Array(Date) for query parameter 'l'. ...

$ curl -s 'http://localhost:8123/?param_l=%5B1659081134%5D' -d 'SELECT {l:Array(DateTime)}'
['2022-07-29 07:52:14']
```

Confirms that the integer-only literal works for `Array(DateTime)` but not `Array(Date)`. Same code path is exercised by clickhouse-js because `formatQueryParams` produces exactly that integer literal.

## Reproduction

```ts
import { createClient } from '@clickhouse/client'

const client = createClient({ url: 'http://localhost:8123' })

// Fails with CANNOT_PARSE_INPUT_ASSERTION_FAILED
const rs = await client.query({
  query: 'SELECT {l:Array(Date)} AS l',
  query_params: { l: [new Date('2023-05-05T00:00:00Z')] },
  format: 'JSONEachRow',
})
console.log(await rs.text())
```

Expected:

```
{"l":["2023-05-05"]}
```

Actual: HTTP 400 from server, error surfaced as a thrown `ClickHouseError` with the message above.

The existing unit test `packages/client-common/__tests__/unit/format_query_params.test.ts:94-102` (`formats a date without timezone`) already documents the offending output:

```ts
const date = new Date(Date.UTC(2022, 6, 29, 7, 52, 14))
expect(formatQueryParams({ value: date })).toBe('1659081134')
```

There is no test covering `Array(Date)` or `Array(DateTime)` parameter binding (`grep -rn 'Array(Date)' tests packages` returns no hits), which is why this hasn't been caught.

## Suggested fix

The branching in `formatQueryParams` already distinguishes array context via `isInArrayOrTuple` (used for `boolean` → `TRUE`/`FALSE`). Apply the same idea to `Date`: when emitted inside an array/tuple, wrap the value in single quotes and emit ISO-formatted text (or wrap the existing numeric form in quotes) so the server's Array element parser accepts it for both `Array(Date)` and `Array(DateTime[64])`. Concretely, in `packages/client-common/src/data_formatter/format_query_params.ts` at the `value instanceof Date` branch, when `isInArrayOrTuple` is true, return `'<formatted>'` (quoted). The same fix likely also addresses the scalar `{d:Date}` case if applied unconditionally — but verify scalar `DateTime` regressions first, since the bare numeric form is currently relied on by existing tests in `select_query_binding.test.ts:207-244`.

Do not attempt the fix in the backfill — this issue is investigation only.

title: Fix Array(Date) query param binding: serialize container Dates as quoted date strings
body:
## Description

Fixes https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/issues/946.

`formatQueryParams` serialized a JS `Date` as a bare Unix-seconds integer (e.g. `1683244800`) in **every** context. Inside a container that becomes `[1683244800]`, which ClickHouse accepts for `Array(DateTime)` but **rejects** for `Array(Date)`/`Array(Date32)`:

```
Code: 27. DB::Exception: Cannot parse input: expected '\'' before: '1683244800]':
value [1683244800] cannot be parsed as Array(Date) for query parameter 'l'.
(CANNOT_PARSE_INPUT_ASSERTION_FAILED)
```

The `Date` branch now mirrors the existing `boolean` handling and uses the `isInArrayOrTuple` flag: inside arrays, tuples, and maps a `Date` is emitted as a quoted UTC `'YYYY-MM-DD'` string. Verified against ClickHouse 26.5 that this is the **single** representation the element parser accepts for **all** temporal element types — `Array(Date)`, `Array(Date32)`, `Array(DateTime)`, and `Array(DateTime64)` (bare int, quoted int, and full datetime strings are all rejected by `Array(Date)`). Scalar `Date`/`DateTime`/`DateTime64` binding is **unchanged** (scalar still uses the bare Unix-timestamp form that scalar `DateTime` relies on).

### Behavioral note (deliberate tradeoff)

Because a query parameter is type-agnostic on the client side (the formatter can't see whether the target column is `Array(Date)` or `Array(DateTime)`), a `Date` used inside `Array(DateTime)`/`Array(DateTime64)` is now bound at **day precision** — the time-of-day is dropped (`2022-05-02 13:25:55` → `2022-05-02 00:00:00`). Date-only is the only encoding `Array(Date)` accepts, so this is unavoidable for a type-blind formatter; an integration test pins this behavior. Scalar `DateTime`/`DateTime64` are untouched and keep full precision.

This is the JS analog of a cross-client class also fixed in clickhouse-java (#2898) and reported for clickhouse-connect (#188).

## Changes

- `packages/client-common/src/data_formatter/format_query_params.ts`: in the `value instanceof Date` branch, when `isInArrayOrTuple` is true, return `'${value.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}'`. (This file is the single shared source; `client-node`/`client-web` symlink it, so both clients get the fix.)

## Test

- **Unit** (`format_query_params.test.ts`): `Date` in an array, nested array, tuple, and object value all render as quoted date strings; time-of-day/millis are dropped; a `Date` composes with other element types in a mixed array. Existing scalar `Date` tests are retained as the contrast that pins the unchanged scalar output.
- **Integration** (`select_query_binding.test.ts`): binding `[Date, Date]` to `Array(Date)` round-trips to `["2023-05-05","2021-01-02"]` (fails on `main` with the parse error above); a `Date` bound to `Array(DateTime)` returns `2022-05-02 00:00:00`, documenting the day-precision tradeoff and guarding that `Array(DateTime)` no longer errors.

Verified the unit tests fail on unpatched code with the exact bug (`expected '[1659081134]' to be '['2022-07-29']'`) and pass with the fix; full unit suite (389 passed) and the `select_query_binding` integration suite (31 passed) are green; `prettier`, `eslint`, and `tsc` are clean.

## Pre-PR validation gate

- [x] Deterministic repro confirmed (server rejects `[<unix>]` for `Array(Date)`; new tests fail on `main`)
- [x] Root cause documented above
- [x] Fix targets the root cause (container element encoding)
- [x] Test fails without fix, passes with fix
- [x] No existing tests broken; no existing tests weakened
- [x] Fix on the live runtime path (proven by an end-to-end integration test through `client.query`)
- [x] Convention compliance verified per `AGENTS.md` / `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- [ ] CHANGELOG entries (added in a follow-up commit on this branch)

title: Extended properties in OTel spans
body:
## Background

At [Langfuse](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse) we run a self-built OTEL wrapper around
every ClickHouse call (span per query with summary stats, query text, and app-specific tags).
We tried adopting the client's native tracer support in
[langfuse/langfuse#14687](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/pull/14687) (client `1.23.1`)
with the goal of deleting our wrapper.

The two-span model (`clickhouse.query` ending at response headers, `clickhouse.query.stream`
covering ResultSet consumption) is great — it cleanly separates query execution time from
result streaming time, which is exactly the distinction we look for in flamecharts. But the
default attributes are too sparse for us to drop our own instrumentation.

What we observe today on `clickhouse.query`:

```json
{"application":"langfuse/3.213.0","request":{"query_id":"ab48…"},"response":{"format":"JSONEachRow"}}
```

and on `clickhouse.query.stream`:

```json
{"response":{"decoded_bytes":419}}
```

What our wrapper records on its span (and what we'd like to get from the client instead):

```json
{"elapsed_ns":"10693523","memory_usage":"4580679","query":{"text":"SELECT e.span_id …"},
 "queryId":"ab48…","read_bytes":"3894304","read_rows":"6568","result_bytes":"0",
 "result_rows":"0","total_rows_to_read":"6568","written_bytes":"0","written_rows":"0",
 "tag":{"projectId":"…","route":"events.getAgentGraphData","surface":"trpc","tag_schema_version":"1"}}
```

With these attributes on the client spans we could delete our wrapper span entirely and go
from 4 spans per query (our wrapper + `clickhouse.query` + the HTTP span from fetch/http
instrumentation + `clickhouse.query.stream`) down to 3.

## Requests

### 1. Record the `X-ClickHouse-Summary` counters on the `query()` span too — and record all keys

As of `1.23.1`, `setResponseSpanAttributes` records `clickhouse.summary.*` for `command`,
`exec`, and `insert`, but `query()` only records the HTTP status code. Please record the
summary on the `clickhouse.query` span as well. The values at header time are incomplete
unless `wait_end_of_query=1` — a documented "values as of response headers" caveat would be
fine with us; our wrapper has the same limitation and the numbers are still very useful for
performance triage.

Additionally, the recorded set is currently a hardcoded subset of the typed
`ClickHouseSummary`. We'd prefer the client to iterate over all keys present in the header,
so that:

- `total_rows_to_read` (already in the type, currently not recorded) shows up,
- `memory_usage` (sent by newer ClickHouse versions, currently not in the type) shows up,
- future server-side additions (e.g. `real_time_microseconds`) arrive for free.

### 2. Opt-in query text attribute (`db.query.text`)

The single most useful attribute in practice. We understand it's off by default for
security/PII reasons — an explicit `dangerously_record_query_text`-style client config flag
(as discussed, a prototype + security audit exist on your side) would work for us. We use
parameterized queries, so recording the query text without bound values is exactly what we
want; an optional sanitizer/truncation callback would be a nice extra but not required.

### 3. Row counts for non-streaming result consumption

`db.response.returned_rows` is currently set on `clickhouse.query.stream` for row-streaming
paths only. It would be great to also get it when results are consumed via the
non-streaming ResultSet methods (`json()`, etc.), so the attribute is reliably present
regardless of consumption style.

### 4. A small, scoped hook for enriching span attributes

We tag every query with an app-specific context object (project id, calling route, surface)
— the same object we put into the `log_comment` setting, which has been invaluable for
correlating `system.query_log` with traces. We currently mirror it onto our wrapper span as
`ch.tag.*` attributes.

Implementing the full `ClickHouseTracer` interface just to inject attributes is a lot of
surface to take on (and to keep correct across client versions). A minimal enrichment hook
would cover our use case, e.g. either:

- a per-call option: `query({ ..., span_attributes: { "myapp.project_id": "…" } })`, or
- a client-level callback: `(operation, params) => ClickHouseSpanAttributes`, merged into
  the span's initial attributes.

The per-call option would be enough for us.

title: fix: back-quote insert() column identifiers with special characters
body:
## Description

Fixes https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/issues/945.

`getInsertQuery` built the `INSERT INTO t (<cols>) FORMAT ...` statement by joining the `columns` array (and the `columns.except` list) **verbatim**. A column name containing a space or other special character therefore produced invalid SQL — e.g. `columns: ['test id', 'name']` generated `INSERT INTO t (test id, name) FORMAT ...`, which the server rejects with `Code: 62 ... Syntax error`.

The fix back-quotes each column identifier at the generation site, escaping backslashes and backticks exactly the way the ClickHouse server's own `backQuote` does (`\` → `\\`, `` ` `` → `` \` ``). Identifiers that are **already quoted** (with backticks or double quotes) are passed through unchanged, so callers that pre-quoted their column names as a workaround keep working — the change is backward compatible.

Verified against ClickHouse 26.5:
- `(\`test id\`, \`name\`)` is accepted; the unquoted form is the reported syntax error.
- A backslash inside a back-quoted identifier is an escape character, so it must itself be escaped (naive `` `a\b` `` targets the wrong column) — hence matching `backQuote`.
- Whole-string quoting a dotted/Nested column (`` `n.arr1` ``) targets the same physical column as the unquoted form, so no dot-splitting is needed.

The changed code lives in the shared common module that is bundled into **both** `@clickhouse/client` and `@clickhouse/client-web`, so the fix (and changelog entries) apply to both.

## Changes

- `packages/client-common/src/client.ts`: add an `escapeColumn` helper and apply it to both the array and `columns.except` branches of `getInsertQuery`; update the `InsertParams.columns` JSDoc to document the auto-quoting + passthrough behavior.
- `packages/client-node/CHANGELOG.md` and `packages/client-web/CHANGELOG.md`: add a `# 1.23.2` → `## Bug Fixes` entry.

## Test

- **Unit** (`packages/client-common/__tests__/unit/insert_query_columns.test.ts`, new): asserts the exact generated SQL through the real `client.insert()` path (mocked connection) for plain, spaced, embedded-backtick, embedded-backslash, combined backslash+backtick, lone-backtick, and dotted/Nested identifiers, plus the `columns.except` cases. Includes contrast cases proving already back-quoted / double-quoted identifiers are passed through unchanged.
- **Integration** (`insert_specific_columns.test.ts`): inserts into a space-named column via `columns` and excludes a space-named column via `columns.except`, then reads the data back.
- Both were confirmed to **fail without the fix** (server syntax error / wrong SQL) and **pass with it**; the existing insert tests and the full node unit suite remain green.

## Pre-PR validation gate

- [x] Deterministic repro confirmed (fails on `main`, passes on this branch)
- [x] Root cause documented above
- [x] Fix targets the root cause (back-quoting at the query-generation site)
- [x] Test fails without fix, passes with fix
- [x] No existing tests broken (full node unit suite + insert integration tests green)
- [x] Convention compliance verified per AGENTS.md (changelog in both affected packages, prettier/eslint/typecheck clean)
- [x] Backward compatible: already-quoted identifiers pass through unchanged

## Note

Related source bug in another client: https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-cpp/issues/30 (identifier quoting in generated INSERT column lists is an SDK-level concern each client implements independently). No backport is requested here; maintainers own any backport decision.

title: feat(otel): richer spans — full summary on query span, span_attributes, and dangerously_log_query_text
body:
## Summary

Implements the clickhouse-js instrumentation feedback from **Langfuse** — closes #948 ([Slack thread](https://clickhouse-inc.slack.com/archives/C03B9QS104X/p1784122553160099) with Steffen Schmitz). The goal: make the client's OpenTelemetry spans carry enough detail that a downstream app can drop its own hand-rolled ClickHouse span wrapper.

### Coverage of #948

**1. Record `X-ClickHouse-Summary` on the `query()` span, and record all keys.**
- Node parses the summary on `connection.query` (`parse_summary: true`) and records it on the `clickhouse.query` span (previously only `command`/`exec`/`insert` carried it).
- The **Web** client now parses the `X-ClickHouse-Summary` header for `query`/`command`/`exec`/`insert` — it parsed **none** before.
- `setResponseSpanAttributes` now iterates over **every key** in the parsed summary (`clickhouse.summary.<key>`) instead of a hardcoded subset, so `total_rows_to_read`, `memory_usage`, and future keys (`real_time_microseconds`, …) arrive for free. `memory_usage` added to `ClickHouseSummary`.

**2. Opt-in query text attribute (`db.query.text`).**
- New `dangerously_log_query_text` client option (default `false`). When enabled, the raw SQL is attached as OTEL `db.query.text` and (Node) included in the `error`-level request-failure logs. Bound `query_params` values and credentials are **never** logged or traced. Parameterized queries record only the statement text (with placeholders), which is exactly Langfuse's use case.

**3. Row counts for non-streaming result consumption.**
- `db.response.returned_rows` is now set for non-streaming `json()` consumption (`JSON` / `JSONObjectEachRow` / other single-document JSON formats) too, not just row-streaming paths. Parity across node and web `ResultSet`.

**4. A small, scoped hook for enriching span attributes.**
- New per-request `span_attributes` bag on `query`/`command`/`exec`/`insert`/`ping` (the per-call option Steffen preferred). Merged into the operation span; caller attributes never override the client's own `db.*`/`server.*`/`clickhouse.*` attributes.

### Relationship to #884

This **supersedes #884**. That PR *drops* the query-text plumbing from the Node log/transport layer; per the design discussion, this PR instead **guards** it behind `dangerously_log_query_text` (safe-by-default — query text is absent from logs unless explicitly opted in). The `logRequestError` hardening from #884 (scalars only, no full params/search-params object) is preserved here, and the no-SQL-leak regression test is carried forward and extended to cover the flag-on path. #884 can be closed once this lands.

## Verification

- New unit tests: common tracer (`db.query.text` on/off, summary on the query span, all-keys recording, `span_attributes` merge + precedence), node ResultSet span (`returned_rows` for `JSON`/`JSONObjectEachRow`), node no-leak/guarded-log regression, web summary parsing (present/absent/malformed).
- `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, full Node (406) and Web (255) unit suites all pass.
- End-to-end against a live ClickHouse: confirmed the `clickhouse.query` span carries the full summary (incl. `total_rows_to_read`, `memory_usage`), `db.query.text`, and the caller's `span_attributes` with core attributes intact; and `returned_rows` is present for non-streaming `json()`.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Docs updated (`docs/howto/tracing.md`)
- [x] CHANGELOG entries added (client-node, client-web)

body:
Sync `release` from `main` to cut **@clickhouse/client** and **@clickhouse/client-web** `1.24.0`.

Merging this triggers the automatic `head`-tagged beta publish for both clients (path-scoped: the shared common sources changed in #950, so both clients republish), each followed by an e2e run against a live ClickHouse.

### What's in 1.24.0
- **OTEL instrumentation improvements** (#950, requested by Langfuse / closes #948): full `X-ClickHouse-Summary` on the `clickhouse.query` span with all keys recorded (incl. `total_rows_to_read`, `memory_usage`); Web client now parses the summary header; `db.response.returned_rows` for non-streaming `json()`; per-request `span_attributes` bag; opt-in `dangerously_log_query_text` (`db.query.text`).
- **Bug fix** (#947): `Array(Date)` / `Array(Date32)` query-parameter binding.

Included commits: #950, #951 (changelog retarget), #952 / #953 (version bumps), plus #947 and #942 (Code of Conduct) which had not yet been synced to `release`.

title: Docs: own and sync ClickHouse documentation
body:
## Summary

Make `ClickHouse/clickhouse-js` the source of truth for its public ClickHouse documentation.

- Copy the JavaScript documentation from `ClickHouse/ClickHouse@21ed77718a5f454680497924d68e9f60a41e026c` into `docs/clickhouse-docs/`, with trailing whitespace normalized and a client-owned `navigation.json`. The dedicated subdirectory keeps repository-only troubleshooting docs out of the published slice.
- Add scoped Mintlify verification for the complete JavaScript documentation folder.
- Add a one-way sync workflow that replaces the corresponding folder in `ClickHouse/ClickHouse` after a release, manual dispatch, or merge carrying the `sync-docs` label.

The published URL remains unchanged. Folder ownership allows future pages to be reviewed alongside the client implementation and synchronized automatically. Fragment links use explicit `/index#...` targets so offline anchor validation resolves the folder index correctly.

No package behavior changes, so package changelogs are unaffected.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111223

After merge, maintainers should confirm the `sync-docs` label exists and the Workflow Auth GitHub App credentials are available to this repository.

## Validation

- All workflows pass `actionlint` v1.7.7 and YAML parsing.
- `navigation.json` passes JSON parsing.
- The complete ClickHouse internal-link and redirect checks pass.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- The migrated folder matches the corresponding aggregator folder in ClickHouse/ClickHouse#111223.

title: ci: roll pinned ClickHouse versions forward to LTS + 3 latest
body:
## Summary
Roll the stale pinned ClickHouse version window in CI forward to the current support set.

The `integration-tests-local-single-node` job in `.github/workflows/tests-node.yml` pinned `node: 24` against a now-stale window of ClickHouse server versions — `26.2, 26.1, 25.12, 25.11, 25.10` — all outside the current support window. This replaces them with the current support set:

- `25.8` (LTS)
- `26.3` (LTS)
- `26.5`, `26.6`, `26.7` (3 latest)

The base matrix (`clickhouse: [head, latest]`) is unchanged and continues to cover the bleeding edge; only the explicit `include:` pins are rolled forward. js's window model (a spread of pinned minors alongside `head`/`latest`) is preserved.

## Why
ClickHouse 26.7 has been released and 26.4 reached EOL, so the pinned window (newest pin was `26.2`) had drifted behind the supported releases. Pinning both current LTS lines (25.8, 26.3) plus the three newest minors keeps the version-specific regression coverage meaningful. Maintainer request, 2026-07-23.

## Notes
- **CI-only change** — no client code, no public API or observable-behavior change, so no CHANGELOG entry (per `AGENTS.md`, changelogs are for observable-behavior / public-API changes) and no version bump.
- All five image tags verified present on Docker Hub (`docker manifest inspect clickhouse/clickhouse-server:<v>`).

## Test plan
- [ ] The `node` workflow's `integration-tests-local-single-node` matrix runs green on `25.8, 26.3, 26.5, 26.6, 26.7` (node 24).

title: Fix parsing of named Tuple elements
body:
## Summary

Fixes #891. Parse named Tuple elements through an explicit branch instead of catching parse errors and retrying with a regular expression. Quoted names can contain spaces, commas, parentheses and escaped quotes. Nested tuples and unnamed parameterized types keep their existing output.

The deprecated `ParsedColumnTuple` output still omits element names. This does not change the standalone datatype parser. Release notes are included for both clients and the shared package. The existing branch incorporates main at `5b7f7e4` without rewriting its history.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit tests covering the common scenarios were added
- [x] A human-readable changelog entry was added to every affected package's `CHANGELOG.md`

## Testing

Verified candidate committed as `56502e2`, with Node24.19.0 and lockfile-pinned Vitest4.1.12. Dependencies were installed with `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`, without changing the manifest or lockfile.

```powershell
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run packages/client-common/__tests__/unit/parse_column_types --maxWorkers=2
# 56 passed across8 files

$env:TEST_MODE='unit'
$env:CLICKHOUSE_TEST_SKIP_INIT='1'
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config packages/client-node/vitest.config.ts --maxWorkers=2
# 453 passed,4 existing skips across44 files

npm run typecheck
npm run lint
```

All workspace typechecks and lint pass. The typecheck needs the workspace artifacts built first, using `npm --workspace @clickhouse/datatype-parser run build` and `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc -p packages/client-node/tsconfig.json`.

The added quoted-name cases first produced9 failures with the previous implementation. Disabling name removal produced12 failures. Removing identifier-quote tracking produced9 failures. Independent review and a built-client probe found a skipped opening quote after a comma. Four additional position-sensitive cases failed before correcting that index advance. The final56-test parser log uses the pinned Vitest4.1.12, and both client suites were rerun after the correction.

The web unit suite passed296 tests across28 files using the existing web config with only the Playwright launch executable changed to installed Chrome. The pinned headless-shell executable was not installed locally. The local override is equivalent to the following config, passed with `--config`.

```ts
import { mergeConfig } from 'vitest/config'
import { playwright } from '@vitest/browser-playwright'
import config from './packages/client-web/vitest.config'

export default mergeConfig(config, {
  test: {
    browser: {
      provider: playwright({
        launchOptions: {
          executablePath: 'C:/Program Files/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe',
        },
      }),
    },
  },
})
```

This Windows checkout stores the two shared-source symlinks as text files. Tests used temporary directory junctions pointing to `packages/client-common/src`. The original files were preserved and restored before committing. Initial collection failures from those text files and initial missing-workspace-build type errors were resolved through this local setup, not by changing tests or production behavior.

The Vite configs emit existing future-loader warnings. No live ClickHouse server, cloud account or pinned-browser run is claimed here. Latest-tip remote workflows require maintainer approval. Node run42357244162 and web run42357244188 have zero jobs. Separate Copilot-setup run42357243225 failed with zero jobs and no available log, so its workflow-level cause is not established. This is not an executed parser-test failure or a CI pass.

Built-package probes also imported the actual Node and Web client exports. Both parse the two named-tuple examples above with complete expected ASTs, while main5b7f7e4 rejects them. Three unnamed Tuple/Decimal/DateTime/Enum examples retain exactly the baseline output in both built clients. These are local parser checks, not server grammar validation. Canonical-format restrictions and strict rejection of malformed declarations are outside this legacy-parser fix.

title: fix: bind scalar Date/Date32 query parameters as date strings
body:
## Summary

A JS `Date` bound to a scalar `{name:Date}` / `{name:Date32}` query parameter was serialized as a bare Unix timestamp, which the server rejects with `BAD_QUERY_PARAMETER` - only `DateTime` / `DateTime64` accept a numeric timestamp. the bound parameter's type is now read from the query text, so a `Date` is formatted as a UTC `YYYY-MM-DD` string for `Date` / `Date32`, while `DateTime` / `DateTime64` keep the Unix timestamp and preserve the time of day

fixes #955

reproduce:

```ts
await client.query({
  query: 'SELECT {d:Date} AS d',
  query_params: { d: new Date('2023-05-05') },
})
```

on main this fails with `Code: 457. BAD_QUERY_PARAMETER` because the client sends `param_d=1683244800`; with this change it sends `param_d=2023-05-05` and the query succeeds. covered by a new unit case in `format_query_params.test.ts` and an integration case in `select_query_binding.test.ts`; the existing scalar `DateTime` / `DateTime64` cases still pass unchanged

## Checklist

- [x] Unit and integration tests covering the common scenarios were added
- [x] A human-readable changelog entry was added to every affected package's `CHANGELOG.md` (client-node and client-web)

title: [backfill: ClickHouse/clickhouse-js] client.query() unconditionally appends FORMAT after user SETTINGS clause, producing invalid SQL on older ClickHouse servers
body:
## Target client repo
`ClickHouse/clickhouse-js`

## Severity
**sev:1** — Easy client-side workaround exists (use `client.exec()` or `client.command()` for queries with a trailing `SETTINGS` clause, since those paths do not auto-append `FORMAT`). Only triggers under opt-in usage (user-supplied `SETTINGS` clause in their own query) and modern ClickHouse server parsers (24.x+) accept the resulting `... SETTINGS ... FORMAT ...` ordering for `DESCRIBE` / `format(...)` queries.

## Description
The `client.query()` method always appends `\nFORMAT <format>` to the user-supplied SQL string. This happens in `packages/client-common/src/client.ts`:

```ts
async query<Format extends DataFormat = 'JSON'>(...) {
  const format = params.format ?? 'JSON'
  const query = formatQuery(params.query, format)   // <— blind append
  ...
}

function formatQuery(query: string, format: DataFormat): string {
  query = query.trim()
  query = removeTrailingSemi(query)
  return query + ' \nFORMAT ' + format
}
```

There is no detection of a trailing `SETTINGS ...` clause. If the user passes a query that ends in `SETTINGS k = v, ...`, the client emits:

```
<user query> SETTINGS k = v, ...
FORMAT JSON
```

This is exactly the same pattern that broke `clickhouse-connect` in the source bug (issue #211). On older ClickHouse server versions (e.g., 23.3 as in the source report), this fails to parse for `DESCRIBE format(...)` because the server parser required `SETTINGS` to be the trailing clause for that statement form. The well-formed query the user wanted was `... FORMAT Native SETTINGS ...` (or `FORMAT` injected before `SETTINGS`).

## ClickHouse server version tested
26.4.2.10 — modern server **accepts** `DESCRIBE format(...) SETTINGS ... FORMAT JSON` and returns HTTP 200, so end-to-end the bug no longer reproduces against a current server. Verified with:

```bash
curl -s -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" 'http://localhost:8123/' --data-binary \
  "DESC format(JSONEachRow, '{\"id\":1}') SETTINGS schema_inference_hints='age LowCardinality(UInt8)', allow_suspicious_low_cardinality_types=1 FORMAT JSON"
# -> HTTP 200
```

The buggy *client behavior* (blind FORMAT append after user SETTINGS) is still present in clickhouse-js as of `main`; whether it surfaces as a parser error depends on the connected server version. Users on long-tail older ClickHouse versions will still hit the original failure mode.

## Reproduction

```ts
import { createClient } from '@clickhouse/client'

const client = createClient({ url: 'http://localhost:8123' })

const q = `DESC format(JSONEachRow, '{"id" : 1, "age" : 25, "name" : "Josh", "status" : null, "hobbies" : ["football", "cooking"]}') SETTINGS schema_inference_hints = 'age LowCardinality(UInt8), status Nullable(String)', allow_suspicious_low_cardinality_types=1`

const rs = await client.query({ query: q, format: 'JSONEachRow' })
console.log(await rs.json())
```

The wire-level query the client sends is:

```
DESC format(JSONEachRow, '...') SETTINGS schema_inference_hints = '...', allow_suspicious_low_cardinality_types=1
FORMAT JSONEachRow
```

**Expected** (against ClickHouse <24 or any future statement form that requires `SETTINGS` to be trailing): the client should inject `FORMAT` before the trailing `SETTINGS` clause, producing `... FORMAT JSONEachRow SETTINGS ...`.

**Actual** (against ClickHouse <24): server returns a syntax error because `SETTINGS` is not the last clause. Against current ClickHouse (26.x), the query succeeds — the bug is masked by server-side parser improvements, not fixed in the client.

## Workaround
Use `client.exec({ query })` or `client.command({ query })` for queries with a trailing `SETTINGS` clause — these paths call `removeTrailingSemi(params.query.trim())` only and do **not** append `FORMAT`, so the user's query is sent verbatim. The trade-off is that `exec()` returns a raw response stream the caller must parse themselves rather than a typed `ResultSet`.

## Suggested fix
In `packages/client-common/src/client.ts`, `formatQuery` should detect a trailing top-level `SETTINGS k = v, ...` clause (outside string literals and parens) and inject `FORMAT <format>` *before* that clause rather than after. A conservative regex-based approach (matching `\bSETTINGS\b` at top level and splitting there) would handle the common case; a more robust fix would tokenize. Care needed to skip `SETTINGS` occurrences inside string literals (e.g., `... '... SETTINGS ...' ...`) or table options. The same applies symmetrically if a user already provided their own `FORMAT` clause — currently the client would emit two `FORMAT` clauses.

## Source bug
https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-connect/issues/211

## Dedup searches
```
gh issue list --repo ClickHouse/clickhouse-js --search "SETTINGS FORMAT" --state all --limit 20            # 20 results, none related
gh issue list --repo ClickHouse/clickhouse-js --search "schema_inference_hints" --state all --limit 10    # 0 results
gh pr list    --repo ClickHouse/clickhouse-js --search "SETTINGS FORMAT" --state all --limit 10           # 10 unrelated PRs
gh issue list --repo ClickHouse/integrations-ai-playground --label backfill --label "target:clickhouse-js" --search "SETTINGS FORMAT" --state all --limit 10  # 0 results
gh issue list --repo ClickHouse/integrations-ai-playground --label backfill --label "target:clickhouse-js" --search "FORMAT" --state all --limit 20           # 1 result (Array(Date) — unrelated)
```

title: [backfill: ClickHouse/clickhouse-js] JSON keys with %2E-escaped dots are not decoded when json_type_escape_dots_in_keys=1
Fix query(): insert FORMAT before a trailing SETTINGS clause
body:
## Description

Fixes https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/issues/970.

`client.query()` builds the wire query via `formatQuery()`, which unconditionally appended `FORMAT <format>` to the **end** of the user-supplied SQL. When the query ends with a top-level `SETTINGS ...` clause, the client emitted:

```
<query> SETTINGS k = v
FORMAT JSON
```

ClickHouse servers whose parser requires `SETTINGS` to be the **trailing** clause of a statement (e.g. `DESCRIBE` / `DESC format(...)` on servers older than 24.x) reject this. Modern servers (24.x+) accept either order, which is why the bug is masked against a current server — but the client is still producing the wrong ordering. The well-formed query is `... FORMAT <format> SETTINGS ...` (this same class broke `clickhouse-connect`, issue #211).

`formatQuery()` now detects a **trailing top-level** `SETTINGS` clause and inserts `FORMAT` right before it; when there is no such clause it appends `FORMAT` at the end exactly as before (byte-for-byte unchanged on the common path).

## Changes

- `packages/client-common/src/client.ts`
  - `formatQuery()`: if the (trimmed, semicolon-stripped) query ends with a trailing top-level `SETTINGS` clause, emit `... FORMAT <format> SETTINGS ...`; otherwise append `FORMAT` at the end as before.
  - New internal `trailingSettingsClauseIndex()` scans the query with a small tokenizer that is aware of string literals (`'` / `"` / `` ` `` with backslash and doubled-quote escapes), dollar-quoted heredocs (`$$...$$`, `$tag$...$tag$`), line comments (`--`, `#`), block comments (`/* */`), and bracket depth. A `SETTINGS` keyword is treated as a clause only when it is at top level (bracket depth 0), outside strings/comments, a whole word, and immediately followed by a `<name> = ...` settings list — so `SETTINGS` inside a string/comment/subquery and a `settings` identifier/column are all left untouched.
  - Updated the `query()` JSDoc to describe the new placement.
- Since the shared `client-common` code is bundled into both clients, added a `## Bug fixes` entry under the unreleased `# 1.24.0` heading in **both** `packages/client-node/CHANGELOG.md` and `packages/client-web/CHANGELOG.md`.

## Test

`packages/client-common/__tests__/unit/format_query.test.ts` (new): a table-driven suite that captures the exact wire string `client.query()` sends (via a stub connection) and asserts `FORMAT` placement. It covers the fix (basic trailing `SETTINGS`, the issue's `DESC format(...)` reproduction, subquery-with-outer-`SETTINGS`, block-comment-then-real-clause, trailing semicolon, no-space `=`) and — as contrast cases that must keep today's append-at-end behavior — no `SETTINGS`, `SETTINGS` inside a string literal, a `settings` identifier, a subquery's own `SETTINGS`, `--`/`#` line comments, and a dollar-quoted heredoc containing `SETTINGS`-shaped text. The 7 injection cases fail on `main` and pass with the fix; the contrast cases pass both ways. Expected orderings were verified against a live ClickHouse server (all HTTP 200).

Verified in the devbox: full node unit suite green (419 passed), `typecheck`, `lint` (`--max-warnings=0`), and `prettier` all clean. (Web unit tests run in a real browser via Playwright, which isn't available in the build sandbox; the shared code is exercised by the node suite through the identical symlinked source, and `client-web` typechecks.)

## Pre-PR validation gate

- [x] Deterministic repro confirmed (unit test fails on `main`, passes with the fix)
- [x] Root cause documented above
- [x] Fix targets the root cause (query-string assembly in `formatQuery`, the sole place `FORMAT` is appended)
- [x] Test fails without fix, passes with fix; contrast cases pin unchanged behavior
- [x] No existing tests weakened or removed; full node unit suite still green
- [x] Convention compliance verified per `AGENTS.md` (CHANGELOG in both client packages, prettier/lint/typecheck)

## Notes

- Not a breaking change: on modern servers both orderings already work (verified), and queries without a trailing `SETTINGS` clause are unaffected; queries that were failing on older servers now succeed.
- Known limitation (kept out of scope): a comment placed *between* `SETTINGS` and its first setting name (e.g. `SETTINGS /* c */ x = 1`) is not recognized and falls back to the previous append-at-end behavior — no regression, just not newly fixed.

Mid-stream exception detection false-positives on any `\r\n` in the body (breaks streaming Parquet + CRLF CSV/TSV) and can hang the event loop
body:
## Summary

The in-band mid-stream exception detector (for ClickHouse 25.11+, which appends a `__exception__` trailer after a 200 response when an error occurs mid-stream) is armed on **every** streaming query against a modern server: the `x-clickhouse-exception-tag` header is a *leading* header sent on successful responses too. The detector then treats **any** `\r\n` in the body as an exception trailer, without ever validating that the `__exception__` marker bytes are actually present.

Verified against a real ClickHouse **26.5.1.882** server.

## Defects

1. **False positive on any `\r\n` in the body.** The call sites (`packages/client-node/src/result_set.ts`, `packages/client-web/src/result_set.ts`) trigger `extractErrorAtTheEndOfChunk` whenever a `\n` is preceded by `\r`, but `extractErrorAtTheEndOfChunk` (`packages/client-common/src/utils/stream.ts`) never compares the `__exception__` marker — it only uses `EXCEPTION_MARKER.length`. Any legitimate `0d 0a` pair aborts a successful query with a bogus error.
   - **Streaming Parquet** (`Parquet` is streamable and binary): a successful 289 KB response contained 1195 `0x0a` bytes, 5 preceded by `0x0d` → the detector fires (~1 false trigger per 64 KiB of binary data). Streaming Parquet is effectively always broken against 25.11+.
   - **CRLF CSV/TSV** (`output_format_csv_crlf_end_of_line` / `output_format_tsv_crlf_end_of_line`): the server emits `0d 0a` per row, so row 1 trips it and the user gets a nonsense error instead of their data.
2. **Unbounded backward scan → event-loop hang.** In `stream.ts`, `do { --errMsgLenStartIdx; } while (chunk[errMsgLenStartIdx] !== NEWLINE);` has no floor. If no `\n` exists below the start index (a single long CRLF-terminated row whose only `\n` is the final byte, or a proxy-truncated trailer), the index runs negative forever; `chunk[-1]` is `undefined` (never a newline) and nothing throws, so the surrounding `try/catch` cannot rescue it — blocking the whole Node.js event loop.
3. **Cross-chunk trailer split** (secondary): the `idx >= 1` guard and end-of-chunk length math assume the trailer is fully contained in one chunk; a trailer split across chunks yields "failed to parse the message length" instead of the real server error. (Larger change; can be tracked separately.)

Affects both `@clickhouse/client` (Node.js) and `@clickhouse/client-web`.

## Fix direction

Make detection sound: require the exact `<tag>\r\n__exception__\r\n` bytes at the end of the chunk before treating it as an exception trailer (the tag is a random per-response token, so an exact match is a reliable discriminator), and floor the backward scan so a malformed trailer returns an error instead of hanging.

<!-- polyglot-issue-classes v1 -->
**Classification:** impact: Stability · area: API & diagnostics (mid-stream errors, Parquet, CRLF)

title: Fix streaming: make mid-stream exception detection sound (no false positives, no event-loop hang)
body:
## Description

Fixes https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/issues/974.
Fixes https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/issues/1084.
Closes https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/issues/607.

ClickHouse 25.11+ reports an error that occurs after a **200** response has started to stream by appending an exception block to the body. Then it breaks the HTTP response. The random per-response token in the `x-clickhouse-exception-tag` header identifies the block. That header is sent on **successful** responses too, so the detector in `ResultSet.stream()` is armed on every streaming query. Server bytes (verified on 26.5 and 26.9, and in `WriteBufferFromHTTPServerResponse.cpp`):

```
\r\n__exception__\r\n<tag>\r\n<message>\n<message_length> <tag>\r\n__exception__\r\n
```

The whole block is at most 16 KiB.

Defects on `main`:

1. The detector treated **any** `\r\n` in the body as an exception, so a stray `0d 0a` aborted a successful query with a bogus error. This breaks streaming `Parquet` (#607) and CRLF-terminated `CSV` / `TSV` (`output_format_*_crlf_end_of_line`).
2. The trailer-length backward scan (`do { --i } while (chunk[i] !== NEWLINE)`) had no floor. A trailer with no interior newline sent the index negative forever and blocked the Node.js event loop.
3. Detection and parsing looked only at the current chunk. The client can receive the block split across chunks (socket reads, response decompression). For a split block, the first lines of the block (`\r`, `__exception__\r`, `<tag>\r`) were emitted as rows and the error message was wrong (#1084).

**Not addressed here:** #1034. When the response is compressed (or the consumer is slow), Node.js can destroy the response with `aborted` before the tail bytes of the block reach `ResultSet.stream()`. Then the stream still fails with `Error: aborted`, not with the server error. This PR does not make mid-stream errors reliable under response compression.

**Also not addressed:** #1167. (Node.js only) A consumer that waits between batches (1 ms is enough) can lose the rows that arrived in the same chunk as the exception block. The `setImmediate` below helps only a consumer that keeps up.

## Changes

- `packages/client-common/src/utils/stream.ts` (all new helpers are `@internal`; they are not re-exported from `@clickhouse/client` / `@clickhouse/client-web`):
  - `matchExceptionBlockStart(bytes, offset, tag, matchedLength = 0)`: at a `\n` that follows `\r`, tells whether the next bytes complete the block opening `__exception__\r\n<tag>` (`"match"`), are an incomplete prefix of it (`"partial"`, so the next chunk must decide), or are data (`"none"`). The random tag makes the match sound. `matchedLength` continues a `"partial"` result with the bytes of the next chunk, without a copy.
  - `errorFromExceptionBlock(block, tag, isEndOfStream)`: returns the parsed server error when the collected block ends with `<tag>\r\n__exception__\r\n`. Returns an error when the block is incomplete at the end of the response or exceeds 16 KiB. Otherwise returns `undefined` (more bytes are necessary).
  - `endsWithExceptionMarker(chunk, tag)`: byte-exact check of the closing suffix.
  - The backward scan in `extractErrorAtTheEndOfChunk` is floored, so a malformed trailer returns an error instead of spinning forever.
- `packages/client-node/src/result_set.ts` and `packages/client-web/src/result_set.ts` (intentionally duplicated, changed identically):
  - At a `\r\n`, check for the block opening. This also works when the `\r` and `\n`, or the opening itself, are in different chunks.
  - On `"partial"`, the bytes from the start of the current row are kept. The first bytes of the next chunk decide: if they are not an exception block, the kept row is emitted and the next chunk is scanned in place (no copy). This is the usual case for CRLF CSV/TSV, where most chunks end with `\r\n`. Only on a match, a partial match, or kept bytes that contain a newline, the kept bytes and the next chunk are joined and scanned again. This applies only after a `\r\n`; JSON formats never have one in their rows.
  - On `"match"`, the rest of the response is collected until the block is complete, then the stream fails with the server error. Block bytes are never emitted as rows.
  - `flush`: kept bytes that did not complete an opening are emitted as rows; an incomplete block is an error.
  - A `toRow` helper builds a row in `transform` and `flush`.
  - (Node.js only) The error from the block goes to the transform callback through `setImmediate`, the same as the `JSONEachRow` error-row path (one helper for both). A `for await` consumer that keeps up reads the rows before the error. The Web transform needs no change: it runs only for a pending read, so its enqueued rows reach the reader before `controller.error()`.
- `packages/client-common/src/index.ts`: export the helpers.
- CHANGELOGs for `@clickhouse/client` and `@clickhouse/client-web`, under the `# 1.26.0` heading (1.25.0 is released).

A row that ends at the last `\r\n` of a chunk is still emitted one chunk later. This is necessary: until the next bytes arrive, the client cannot tell a complete CRLF row from a row that the exception block cuts.

## Test

- `packages/client-common/__tests__/unit/stream_utils.test.ts`: parametrized tests for `matchExceptionBlockStart` (complete opening, prefixes, CSV row, near-miss marker, wrong tag, empty tag, continuation with `matchedLength` at every split point), `errorFromExceptionBlock` (complete block, 16 KiB block, incomplete, incomplete at end, over 16 KiB), and `endsWithExceptionMarker`. A regression test checks that `extractErrorAtTheEndOfChunk` does not hang.
- `packages/client-node/__tests__/unit/node_exception_tag.test.ts` and `packages/client-web/__tests__/unit/web_exception_tag.test.ts`, through the real `ResultSet.stream()`:
  - LF and CRLF rows followed by an exception block, split into two chunks at **every** byte, and delivered one byte at a time. Each case must surface the real server message, and the rows must be data rows only, in order.
  - A 16 KiB block delivered in 4 KiB chunks surfaces the full message.
  - A response that ends inside the block fails with an "incomplete" error.
  - Successful responses (CRLF CSV, CRLF TSV whose last row is `__exception__`, CRLF TSV with `__exception__` before rows that start like the tag, binary data with a partial marker) split at every byte give exactly the same rows as one chunk.
  - Earlier cases are kept: a successful CRLF CSV or binary body completes, and a genuine exception surfaces the real message.
- Live server, `packages/client-node/__tests__/integration/node_stream_error_handling.test.ts` and `packages/client-web/__tests__/integration/web_stream_error_handling.test.ts` (25.11+): a `CSV` response with `output_format_csv_crlf_end_of_line: 1` and a `TabSeparated` response with `output_format_tsv_crlf_end_of_line: 1` (10,000 rows, `max_block_size: 1000`) stream to completion with all rows. Against 26.9, all 10 chunks of these responses end with `\r\n`. On `main`, both tests fail (Node: `Error: 91`; Web: `failed to parse the message length`).
- Live server, same files: a `CSV` and a `TabSeparated` response that fail after row 4 give a reader the rows 0 to 4 and then the `ClickHouseError`. The Web test is skipped in Chromium: Chromium sometimes drops the end of the response when the server closes the connection after the exception block, and the read fails with `TypeError: network error` ([#1140](https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/issues/1140)). The raw `response.body` lost the exception block in 16 of 200 runs in Chromium and in 0 of 200 in Firefox.
- Live server, same files: a real failing body from the server (got with `exec()`) is given to a `ResultSet`, cut at each offset of the exception block and one byte at a time. Each case gives the `ClickHouseError` (code 395) and all rows. These tests are in the integration collections, so the cloud jobs also run them. The Web test sets `enable_http_compression: 0` (else the server gives a 500 response without the block) and gets the body again when Chromium drops its end (#1140). On `main`, both tests fail.

Gates at f6eae78: `test:node:unit` (579 passed), `test:web:unit` in Chromium (398 passed), the stream error integration tests in Node.js, Chromium and Firefox, `typecheck`, `lint --max-warnings=0`, prettier. A local fuzz test (not committed) of the Node.js and Web `ResultSet.stream()`, with random chunks, tags, CRLF rows, near-miss markers and real server bodies up to 16 KiB, found no wrong result and no hang in about 350,000 runs.

## Pre-PR validation gate

- [x] Deterministic repro confirmed (unit split tests + live 26.9 server)
- [x] Root cause documented above
- [x] Fix targets the root cause (sound opening match, block buffered across chunks, bounded scan)
- [x] Tests fail without fix, pass with fix
- [x] No existing tests weakened or edited (new tests only)
- [x] Convention compliance verified per `packages/AGENTS.md` (CHANGELOG in both affected packages, prettier, lint)
- [x] Fix on the live runtime path (proven via `ResultSet.stream()` end-to-end tests and live-server tests)

> Changes core streaming error paths used on every armed query; behavior is heavily tested but regressions could affect row delivery or error timing for async consumers.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **mid-stream exception handling** for ClickHouse 25.11+ in `ResultSet.stream()` (Node and Web). Detection no longer treats every `\r\n` as an error: it requires the `__exception__` marker plus the per-response `x-clickhouse-exception-tag`. That restores streaming for Parquet and CRLF CSV/TSV without false positives.
> 
> **Exception blocks split across chunks** are buffered until complete; block bytes are not emitted as rows, and consumers still get data rows before the parsed server error. `extractErrorAtTheEndOfChunk` now bounds its backward newline scan so malformed trailers return an error instead of hanging the event loop.
> 
> New `@internal` helpers in `client-common` (`matchExceptionBlockStart`, `errorFromExceptionBlock`, `endsWithExceptionMarker`) back the updated transform/flush logic in both `result_set` implementations. body:
## What

Adds a `.gitattributes` marking `CHANGELOG.md` with git's built-in `merge=union`
merge driver. The single bare pattern applies at every depth, so it covers the root
changelog and each package's changelog:

- `CHANGELOG.md` (root)
- `packages/client-common/CHANGELOG.md`
- `packages/client-node/CHANGELOG.md`
- `packages/client-web/CHANGELOG.md`
- `packages/datatype-parser/CHANGELOG.md`
- `skills/clickhouse-js-node-rowbinary/CHANGELOG.md`

## Why

The changelogs are append-at-the-top-of-a-section files that nearly every PR touches.
When two PRs each add an entry, git's default 3-way merge raises a textual conflict
even though the intended resolution is unambiguous and always the same — keep both
entries. That conflict then has to be resolved by hand on every concurrent PR. With
`merge=union`, git takes both sides of a conflicting hunk instead of failing.

`union` is one of git's **built-in** merge drivers, so no `git config` and no per-clone
setup is needed — it works for every contributor, for CI, and for merges performed on
GitHub. The rule is scoped to changelogs only; this file adds no other attribute (in
particular no `text`/`eol` normalisation, which would risk a tree-wide renormalisation
in a repo that has never had a `.gitattributes`).

## Corner cases (stated honestly)

Two ways this can produce a wrong-but-harmless result. Both land as plain text in the
PR diff, so a reviewer can catch and fix them:

1. **Duplicated section.** If two PRs each introduce the *same new section* (e.g. a
   `## New features` heading) and place it at *different positions* in the file, union
   merge keeps both copies and the heading appears twice. (If both add it in the same
   place with identical surrounding lines, git matches the shared context and the
   result is correct.)
2. **An old PR merged across a release cut.** If a PR was opened while its entry sat
   under the unreleased section, and `main` meanwhile cut a release — moving that
   content under a new version heading and leaving the unreleased section empty — union
   merge will silently file the old PR's entry under the **already-released** section,
   and raises **no conflict** to flag it.

Both are confined to the changelog, are visible in the diff, and are cheap for a
reviewer to spot — which trades well against hand-resolving a conflict on essentially
every concurrent PR.

## Verification

- `git check-attr merge -- <each changelog>` → `union` for all six changelogs;
  `unspecified` for non-changelog files (`README.md`, sources).
- Merge simulation: two branches each add a different entry under the same
  `## Unreleased` section; merging one into the other succeeds with **both** entries
  present and no conflict markers — using only the committed `.gitattributes` and no
  merge-driver config.

## Note on the changelog gate

This PR intentionally does **not** add a CHANGELOG entry: it changes no published
package (repo metadata only), and adding an entry would create exactly the conflict
this change removes. Flagging proactively so the usual changelog check isn't read as an
oversight.

---

Maintainer-directed repo chore (no filed issue, by request). One PR per client repo;
this one covers `clickhouse-js` only. Sibling PRs add the equivalent rule to the other
client repos.

:boom: Breaking Changes

  • docs(shim-opentracing): Notice: The @opentelemetry/shim-opentracing package will be removed in SDK 3.x, planned for approximately September 2026.
    • The OpenCensus and OpenTracing compatibility requirements in the OpenTelemetry specification have been deprecated.

:rocket: Features

  • feat(sdk-metrics): add maxExportBatchSize option to PeriodicExportingMetricReader #6655 @​psx95
    • Optimized PeriodicExportingMetricReader.forceFlush to prevent redundant concurrent export cycles. Concurrent calls to forceFlush will now await any ongoing export and reuse a fresh export cycle if one is started concurrently by another caller. This ensures the latest metrics are always exported efficiently without triggering duplicate collection and export cycles.
  • feat(sdk-trace): implement span processor metrics #6504 @​anuraaga

:bug: Bug Fixes

  • fix(propagator-jaeger): do not throw on malformed percent-encoded uber-trace-id / uberctx-* headers during extract @​pichlermarc

:house: Internal

  • perf(sdk-metrics): defer allocation of HrTime to accumulation creation #6839 @​legendecas
  • chore(*): migrate use of sdk-trace-base and sdk-trace-node to sdk-trace #6851 @​trentm
  • perf(sdk-metrics): optionally capture active context for sync instruments #6848 @​legendecas

Release notes

Sourced from @​opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-proto's releases.

experimental/v0.221.0

0.221.0

:boom: Breaking Changes

  • feat(sdk-logs)!: configure the force flush timeout per call #6931 @​LarryHu0217
    • (user-facing): LoggerProviderOptions.forceFlushTimeoutMillis has been removed; pass timeoutMillis to LoggerProvider.forceFlush() instead.
  • feat(instrumentation-http)!: emit only stable HTTP semantic conventions. The OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN environment variable no longer changes HTTP attribute or metric emission — old (v1.7.0) and duplicate (http/http/dup) semconv outputs have been removed. #6819 @​maryliag
  • feat(instrumentation-fetch)!: emit only stable HTTP semantic conventions. The semconvStabilityOptIn instrumentation config option has been removed; old (v1.7.0) and duplicate semconv outputs are no longer emitted. #6819 @​maryliag
  • feat(instrumentation-xml-http-request)!: emit only stable HTTP semantic conventions. The semconvStabilityOptIn instrumentation config option has been removed; old (v1.7.0) and duplicate semconv outputs are no longer emitted. #6819 @​maryliag
  • feat(instrumentation-grpc)!: emit only stable network semantic conventions. The OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN environment variable no longer changes attribute emission — net.peer.name and net.peer.port (old) are no longer set; only server.address and server.port (stable). #6819 @​maryliag

:rocket: Features

  • feat(sdk-logs): allow modifying ReadWriteLogRecord properties (including hrTime, hrTimeObserved, and spanContext) in accordance with the OpenTelemetry Logs specification #6923 @​Babul422
  • feat(sdk-node): emit a deprecation warning when the JaegerPropagator is selected via OTEL_PROPAGATORS or declarative config; use tracecontext instead. @​pichlermarc
  • feat(instrumentation-http): set error.type to status code in metrics for error requests. #6919 @​raphael-theriault-swi

experimental/v0.220.0

0.220.0

:boom: Breaking Changes

  • refactor(sdk-logs)!: refactor BatchLogRecordProcessor constructor signature #6817 @​trentm
    • (user-facing): BatchLogRecordProcessor now takes a single options object with all possible properties, instead of two separate arguments. For example, before new BatchLogRecordProcessor(exporter, { maxQueueSize: 1000 }), after new BatchLogRecordProcessor({ exporter, maxQueueSize: 1000 }).
    • interface BufferConfig -> interface BatchLogRecordProcessorOptions, and now includes the exporter property
    • interface BatchLogRecordProcessorBrowserConfig -> interface BatchLogRecordProcessorBrowserOptions
    • (user-facing): SimpleLogRecordProcessor now takes a single options object with all possible properties. For example, before new SimpleLogRecordProcessor(exporter), after new SimpleLogRecordProcessor({ exporter }). #6836
  • refactor(configuration)!: change config file parsing to not add default values, nor merge *_list fields #6765 @​trentm
    • Responsibility for handling declarative config "nullBehavior" and "defaultBehavior" belongs in the "create" handling, currently in the "sdk-node" package.
  • docs(shim-opencensus): Notice: The @opentracing/shim-opencensus package will be removed in SDK 3.x, planned for approximately September 2026.
    • The OpenCensus and OpenTracing compatibility requirements in the OpenTelemetry specification have been deprecated.
  • chore(sdk-node)!: Drop support for deprecated OpenCensusMetricProducer from declarative config

:rocket: Features

  • feat(configuration): bump config schema to v1.1.0; rename without_scope_info → scope_info_enabled and without_target_info/development → target_info_enabled/development on the Prometheus pull exporter (semantics inverted), rename with_resource_constant_labels → resource_constant_labels. Validate file_format per the configuration versioning spec: accept any minor version of major 1 (e.g. 1.0, 1.1), warn when the minor version is newer than supported, and reject other major versions. #6781 @​MikeGoldsmith
  • feat(sdk-node): wire up id_generator from declarative config #6782 @​MikeGoldsmith
  • feat(sdk-node): wire up tracer_provider.sampler from declarative config (always_on, always_off, trace_id_ratio_based, parent_based); unrecognized variants warn and fall back to ParentBased(AlwaysOn) #6506 @​MikeGoldsmith
  • feat(propagator-env-carrier): empty name normalization #6827 @​pellared
  • feat(propagator-env-carrier): make EnvironmentGetter read the current process.env #6853 @​pellared

:bug: Bug Fixes

  • fix(sdk-logs): stop Logger.emit() doing work (record construction, metrics, processor onEmit) after the LoggerProvider has shut down #6826 @​anneheartrecord
  • fix(sdk-node): pass all config properties (endpoint, headers, timeout, TLS, compression, temporality preference, default histogram aggregation) to OTLP metric exporters in declarative config #6814 @​MikeGoldsmith
  • fix(sdk-logs): default BatchLogRecordProcessor scheduleDelayMillis is 1000 #6796 @​trentm
  • fix(configuration): percent-decode keys and values in resource.attributes_list per spec #6787 @​MikeGoldsmith
  • fix(configuration): default log_level to info in env-based config initialization for consistency with file-based config #6788 @​MikeGoldsmith

title: chore(deps-dev): bump undici from 8.5.0 to 8.9.0
body:
Bumps [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici) from 8.5.0 to 8.9.0.
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v8.9.0

⚠️ Security fixes

High severity

  • GHSA-4cwx-7wf7-3272: malformed qualified private Cache-Control directives could cause cross-user information disclosure in shared caches or a parse-time crash. The cache parser now treats empty qualified directives conservatively and safely handles mixed qualified and unqualified directives. Fixed by 4fe5bc5f with regression coverage in 9f09b49a.

Medium severity

  • GHSA-m8rv-5g2x-5cg5: a malicious type property on a duck-typed blob-like HTTP/1.1 request body could inject CRLF sequences into the generated content-type header. Undici now coerces and validates the value before adding it to the request. Fixed by 7d3cf924.
  • GHSA-jr45-8vmc-qm54: optional whitespace around = in qualified no-cache and private directives could bypass shared-cache restrictions and disclose authenticated data across users. Cache-Control parsing now normalizes these forms and applies conservative cache decisions. Fixed by c601fff1.
  • GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524: the retry interceptor could expose a stale Content-Length after resuming a partial response, potentially causing downstream response desynchronization, hangs, or corruption. Undici now rejects partial responses whose Content-Length is inconsistent with Content-Range. Fixed by e11a68ed, with corrected fixtures in 2b3f7493.
  • GHSA-v3r7-h72x-cjcm: unsanitized domain and unparsed values passed to setCookie() could inject cookie attributes. Undici now validates cookie domains, paths, and unparsed attributes more strictly. Fixed by 10d93fc3.

Additional hardening

Undici now validates non-string header values after coercion, including array elements, preventing crafted toString() or Symbol.toPrimitive implementations from introducing CRLF sequences. This defense-in-depth change was made in 354a151f.

title: Uncompressed streaming inserts emit one HTTP chunk per row, inflating the request body ~50%
Pr 958 own docs
body:
## Summary
copy of https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/pull/958
Make `ClickHouse/clickhouse-js` the source of truth for its public ClickHouse documentation.

- Copy the JavaScript documentation from `ClickHouse/ClickHouse@21ed77718a5f454680497924d68e9f60a41e026c` into `docs/clickhouse-docs/`, with trailing whitespace normalized and a client-owned `navigation.json`. The dedicated subdirectory keeps repository-only troubleshooting docs out of the published slice.
- Add scoped Mintlify verification for the complete JavaScript documentation folder.
- Add a one-way sync workflow that replaces the corresponding folder in `ClickHouse/ClickHouse` after a release, manual dispatch, or merge carrying the `sync-docs` label.

The published URL remains unchanged. Folder ownership allows future pages to be reviewed alongside the client implementation and synchronized automatically. Fragment links use explicit `/index#...` targets so offline anchor validation resolves the folder index correctly.

No package behavior changes, so package changelogs are unaffected.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111223

After merge, maintainers should confirm the `sync-docs` label exists and the Workflow Auth GitHub App credentials are available to this repository.

## Validation

- All workflows pass `actionlint` v1.7.7 and YAML parsing.
- `navigation.json` passes JSON parsing.
- The complete ClickHouse internal-link and redirect checks pass.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- The migrated folder matches the corresponding aggregator folder in ClickHouse/ClickHouse#111223.

title: fix(examples): do not assert an exact 0 distance from approximate QBit search
body:
## Summary

The `examples` workflow has been red on **every** PR and every push to `main` since
2026-08-04 — all four legs (`head`/`latest` × `node`/`web`) fail on
`examples/{node,web}/coding/qbit.ts`:

```
AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal:
+ 0.04572148248553276
- 0
❯ coding/qbit.ts:95:8    assert.strictEqual(nearest[0].dist, 0);
```

The example is not flaky — it is deterministically wrong now. It ran

```sql
L2DistanceTransposed(vec, {ref:Array(Float32)}, 16)
```

i.e. an **approximate** distance that reads only the top 16 of the 32 Float32 bit
planes, and then asserted that the row identical to the reference vector sat at
distance *exactly* `0`.

### Root cause

ClickHouse 26.7 shipped ClickHouse/ClickHouse#110911, which changed how a value
truncated to `precision` bit planes is reconstructed: it is now placed at the
**centre** of the range the retained bits describe, instead of having the dropped
bits zero-filled. Zero-filling biased every reconstructed value towards zero and
was degenerate at low precision (at `precision = 1` every value collapsed to `±0.0`,
so the distance carried no ranking information at all — ClickHouse/ClickHouse#110898).
So this was a deliberate server-side *fix*, not a regression, and the PR explicitly
calls out that the midpoint rule holds at the `QBit(Float32)` `p = 16` boundary —
exactly the case this example used.

The consequence is that an exact-match reference vector no longer yields `0` at
reduced precision. Each stored element comes back half an ULP high, and the reported
distance is precisely the norm of that offset vector:

| element | exponent | ½ ULP at 7 retained mantissa bits |
| ------- | -------- | --------------------------------- |
| 1.0     | 0        | 0.00390625                        |
| 2.0, 3.0 | 1       | 0.0078125                         |
| 4.0 … 7.0 | 2      | 0.015625                          |
| 8.0     | 3        | 0.03125                           |

`sqrt(Σ (½ULP)²) = 0.045721484…` — the value CI reports.

### Verified locally

| ClickHouse | `dist` at `bits: 16` | example on `main` | example with this PR |
| ---------- | -------------------- | ----------------- | -------------------- |
| 26.6.2.160 | `0`                  | passes            | passes               |
| 26.7.1.1315 | `0.04572148402624854` | **fails**       | passes               |

Reproduced the failure on `main` against 26.7 and confirmed both the `node` and the
`web` leg go green with this change, on 26.7 **and** on 26.6 (so the fix is not a
one-way ratchet onto new servers).

## Changes

- `examples/node/coding/qbit.ts`, `examples/web/coding/qbit.ts`:
  - Keep the `bits: 16` approximate search and its ranking assertion (`[1, 3, 2]`),
    which is the property that actually matters and is what makes the reduced-precision
    read useful.
  - Replace `dist === 0` with "the exact match is decisively closer than the
    runner-up". The residual is deliberately **not** pinned to a literal: its magnitude
    depends on the server version and on the SIMD kernel the host CPU selects. Concretely,
    the same 26.7 release returns `0.04572148248553276` on the GitHub-hosted runners but
    `0.04572148402624854` on an AVX-512 Xeon 8175M — one computes the accumulation at
    Float32 width, the other at Float64 (cf. ClickHouse/ClickHouse#96764 for prior art on
    CPU-dependent results in these functions). Both `head` and `latest` agreed with each
    other on each machine, so this splits by host, not by version.
  - Add a companion full-precision (`bits: 32`) query that retains a hard `=== 0`
    assertion, where exactness genuinely does hold and is stable across versions and
    CPUs. This also makes the accuracy-vs-I/O trade-off that the `bits` argument
    controls explicit in the example, rather than implying reduced precision is free.

No client code is touched, so there is no changelog entry — `examples/` is not a
published package.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit and integration tests covering the common scenarios were added — n/a; the
      changed files *are* the executed examples, verified red→green on 26.7 and green
      on 26.6, plus `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` and `prettier --check` clean in both packages.

## Note for maintainers

The `bits: 8` case is worth knowing about if this example is extended: at that
precision ClickHouse 26.7 returns the *same* distance (`7.43303442`) for row 1 and
row 3, so any ordering assertion there would be ambiguous. Once `precision` starts
truncating exponent bits, #110911 deliberately keeps the lower edge rather than the
midpoint.

Some public API types are not exported from @clickhouse/client since 1.23.0
body:
**Describe the bug**

Since 1.23.0, when `@clickhouse/client-common` was bundled into the client (#845), a few types that the client's own public methods use are not re-exported from `@clickhouse/client`:

- `QueryParamsWithFormat`: the parameter of `query()`
- `PingParams`: the parameter of `ping()`
- `ResultJSONType` and `RowJSONType`: what `ResultSet.json()` and `Row.json()` return
- `ClickHouseSummary` and `WithClickHouseSummary`: fields of `InsertResult` and `CommandResult`

I could not find a supported place to import them from. `@clickhouse/client-common` is deprecated, and its npm deprecation message says to import from `@clickhouse/client` instead, but these types are not there. There is also no `exports` map in the package, so the only options left are copying the type into my own code or importing from `dist/`.

The internal things (`Connection*`, `LogWriter`, `getConnectionParams` and so on) are obviously left out on purpose, but these ones are part of the public API. Probably the same miss as #935, where `EXCEPTION_TAG_HEADER_NAME` and `extractErrorAtTheEndOfChunk` were added back in 1.23.1.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `npm i @clickhouse/client@1.23.1 typescript`
2. Put the code below into `probe.ts`
3. `npx tsc --noEmit probe.ts --module nodenext --moduleResolution nodenext --target esnext --strict`

**Expected behaviour**

If a type is used in the signature of a public method, it should be importable from the package root. Otherwise you cannot write a wrapper with the same signature.

**Code example**

```ts
import type {
  ClickHouseSummary,
  PingParams,
  QueryParamsWithFormat,
  ResultJSONType,
  RowJSONType,
  WithClickHouseSummary
} from '@clickhouse/client'
```

What I needed it for: a wrapper around `query()` that adds a `query_id` to every request, so the query can be killed on abort. To keep format inference it has to take the same params as `query()`:

```ts
async function chQuery<Format extends DataFormat = 'JSON'>(
  params: QueryParamsWithFormat<Format> // cannot be imported
) { /* ... */ }
```

Copying the type from `common/client.d.ts` as is works fine, so I don't think anything changed in the API here:

```ts
type QueryParamsWithFormat<Format extends DataFormat> = Omit<QueryParams, 'format'> & {
  format?: Format
}
```

**Error log**

```
probe.ts(2,3): error TS2305: Module '"@clickhouse/client"' has no exported member 'ClickHouseSummary'.
probe.ts(3,3): error TS2305: Module '"@clickhouse/client"' has no exported member 'PingParams'.
probe.ts(4,3): error TS2305: Module '"@clickhouse/client"' has no exported member 'QueryParamsWithFormat'.
probe.ts(5,3): error TS2305: Module '"@clickhouse/client"' has no exported member 'ResultJSONType'.
probe.ts(6,3): error TS2305: Module '"@clickhouse/client"' has no exported member 'RowJSONType'.
probe.ts(7,3): error TS2305: Module '"@clickhouse/client"' has no exported member 'WithClickHouseSummary'.
```

**Configuration**

- Client version: 1.23.1, same on `1.24.0-head.443b2f0.1` and on `@clickhouse/client-web@1.23.1`
- Node.js 26.7.0, TypeScript 7.0.2
- macOS

title: fix(types): re-export public API types dropped in 1.23.0
body:
Closes #997. The issue lists six of these; I found the other four (the ping ones and `ResultStream`) while preparing the change.

All ten were exported from the root of `@clickhouse/client-common`, and the ping ones sit in the block that its `index.ts` marks with `/** Should be re-exported by the implementation */`. The lower level exports (`Connection*`, `LogWriter`, the encoders and utils) are clearly internal, so I left them out. `WithHttpStatusCode` was never exported from `client-common` either, so it is not here; happy to add it if you want the whole intersection nameable.

Type-only re-exports: I built the tree with and without the change, `dist/index.js` is byte identical for both packages, only the `.d.ts` files differ. Locally green: typecheck, lint, prettier, build, `test:node:unit` (408 passed). `test:web:unit` needs Playwright browsers, which I don't have set up.

No test included, and I would rather ask than guess: a type level assertion would not fail anywhere in CI today, since the package tsconfigs include only `src/**` and vitest runs without `typecheck`.
