title: [rowbinary] readRows/streamRowBatches silently drop all rows when every column is zero-width (Tuple())
fix(rowbinary): support compiling empty Tuple() type AST
body:
## Summary

Resolves the AST compilation failure for empty tuples (`Tuple()`) in `@clickhouse/rowbinary`.

## Background & Root Cause

When `@clickhouse/datatype-parser` parses an empty tuple type string (such as `Tuple()` or `Tuple(Tuple())`), it returns a node with `kind: NodeKind.DataType` and `name: "Tuple"` (rather than `NodeKind.TupleDataType` which is returned for multi-element tuples like `Tuple(UInt8, String)`).

In `skills/clickhouse-js-node-rowbinary/src/readers/compile.ts`, `dataTypeReader()` did not have a handler for `case "Tuple"`. As a result, folding an empty tuple AST fell through to the default branch and threw:

```
RowBinaryTypeError: unsupported RowBinary type: Tuple
```

Additionally, `tupleReader()` previously checked `named` via `names.length === readers.length && names.every((n) => n.length > 0)`. For empty tuples where `names` and `readers` are both empty arrays (`[]`), `[].every(...)` evaluated to `true`, causing an empty tuple to be erroneously dispatched to `readTupleNamed({})` (which returns an object `{}`) instead of `readTuple([])` (which returns an array `[]`).

## Changes

1. **`compile.ts`**: Added `case "Tuple": return tupleReader(node);` to `dataTypeReader()`.
2. **`compile.ts`**: Updated `tupleReader()` so `named` requires `names.length > 0` before treating a tuple as a named object tuple.
3. **`compile.test.ts`**: Added unit tests validating that `Tuple()`, `Tuple(Tuple())`, and `Tuple(Tuple(), UInt8)` compile cleanly and decode the expected zero-byte tuples without error.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` in `skills/clickhouse-js-node-rowbinary` passed with 0 errors.
- `npx vitest run -t "empty Tuple" tests/compile.test.ts` passed 3/3 tests cleanly.
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` built without errors.

Partially addresses #1000.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Localized AST-to-reader logic and new tests; no auth, I/O, or wire-format changes beyond fixing empty-tuple decoding.
> 
> **Overview**
> RowBinary reader compilation now handles **empty `Tuple()`** AST nodes (parsed as `DataType` named `Tuple`) by routing them through `tupleReader` in `dataTypeReader`, instead of failing with an unsupported type error.
> 
> **Named vs positional tuple folding** now requires at least one element name before treating a tuple as a named object; empty tuples decode as **`[]`** (not `{}`), including nested `Tuple(Tuple())` and mixes like `Tuple(Tuple(), UInt8)`. Changelog and compile unit tests cover these cases.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1f2c041e2d83471fe2979d2992368bc5fbd82beb. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

:boom: Breaking Changes

  • feat(sdk-logs)!: configure the force flush timeout per call #6931 @​LarryHu0217
    • (user-facing): LoggerProviderOptions.forceFlushTimeoutMillis has been removed; pass timeoutMillis to LoggerProvider.forceFlush() instead.
  • feat(instrumentation-http)!: emit only stable HTTP semantic conventions. The OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN environment variable no longer changes HTTP attribute or metric emission — old (v1.7.0) and duplicate (http/http/dup) semconv outputs have been removed. #6819 @​maryliag
  • feat(instrumentation-fetch)!: emit only stable HTTP semantic conventions. The semconvStabilityOptIn instrumentation config option has been removed; old (v1.7.0) and duplicate semconv outputs are no longer emitted. #6819 @​maryliag
  • feat(instrumentation-xml-http-request)!: emit only stable HTTP semantic conventions. The semconvStabilityOptIn instrumentation config option has been removed; old (v1.7.0) and duplicate semconv outputs are no longer emitted. #6819 @​maryliag
  • feat(instrumentation-grpc)!: emit only stable network semantic conventions. The OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN environment variable no longer changes attribute emission — net.peer.name and net.peer.port (old) are no longer set; only server.address and server.port (stable). #6819 @​maryliag

:rocket: Features

  • feat(sdk-logs): allow modifying ReadWriteLogRecord properties (including hrTime, hrTimeObserved, and spanContext) in accordance with the OpenTelemetry Logs specification #6923 @​Babul422

    • interface BatchLogRecordProcessorBrowserConfig -> interface BatchLogRecordProcessorBrowserOptions

title: ci: roll ClickHouse version matrix to 26.9, 26.8, 26.7, 26.3
body:
## Description

CI maintenance chore. Align the ClickHouse version coverage of the Node.js
integration tests with the support policy: the 3 latest series + the 2 latest
LTS series + `head`.

Derived from ClickHouse `utils/list-versions/version_date.tsv` (as of 2026-10-05):
- LTS (newest 2): 26.8, 26.3
- Latest (newest 3): 26.9, 26.8, 26.7

26.8 is both a latest series and an LTS, so the numeric set is 4 entries.

## Changes

`.github/workflows/tests-node.yml`, job `integration-tests-local-single-node`:

:rocket: Features

  • feat(sdk-metrics): add maxExportBatchSize option to PeriodicExportingMetricReader #6655 @​psx95
    • Optimized PeriodicExportingMetricReader.forceFlush to prevent redundant concurrent export cycles. :bug: Bug Fixes

:house: Internal

  • perf(sdk-metrics): defer allocation of HrTime to accumulation creation #6839 @​legendecas
  • chore(*): migrate use of sdk-trace-base and sdk-trace-node to sdk-trace #6851 @​trentm

Release notes

experimental/v0.221.0

0.221.0

:boom: Breaking Changes

  • feat(sdk-logs)!: configure the force flush timeout per call #6931 @​LarryHu0217
    • (user-facing): LoggerProviderOptions.forceFlushTimeoutMillis has been removed; pass timeoutMillis to LoggerProvider.forceFlush() instead.
  • feat(instrumentation-http)!: emit only stable HTTP semantic conventions. The OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN environment variable no longer changes HTTP attribute or metric emission — old (v1.7.0) and duplicate (http/http/dup) semconv outputs have been removed. #6819 @​maryliag
  • feat(instrumentation-fetch)!: emit only stable HTTP semantic conventions. The semconvStabilityOptIn instrumentation config option has been removed; old (v1.7.0) and duplicate semconv outputs are no longer emitted. #6819 @​maryliag
  • feat(instrumentation-xml-http-request)!: emit only stable HTTP semantic conventions. The semconvStabilityOptIn instrumentation config option has been removed; old (v1.7.0) and duplicate semconv outputs are no longer emitted. #6819 @​maryliag
  • feat(instrumentation-grpc)!: emit only stable network semantic conventions. The OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN environment variable no longer changes attribute emission — net.peer.name and net.peer.port (old) are no longer set; only server.address and server.port (stable). #6819 @​maryliag

:rocket: Features

  • feat(sdk-logs): allow modifying ReadWriteLogRecord properties (including hrTime, hrTimeObserved, and spanContext) in accordance with the OpenTelemetry Logs specification #6923 @​Babul422
  • feat(sdk-node): emit a deprecation warning when the JaegerPropagator is selected via OTEL_PROPAGATORS or declarative config; use tracecontext instead. @​pichlermarc
  • feat(instrumentation-http): set error.type to status code in metrics for error requests. #6919 @​raphael-theriault-swi

    • interface BatchLogRecordProcessorBrowserConfig -> interface BatchLogRecordProcessorBrowserOptions

Release notes

Sourced from @​opentelemetry/instrumentation-fetch's releases.

experimental/v0.221.0

0.221.0

:boom: Breaking Changes

  • feat(sdk-logs)!: configure the force flush timeout per call #6931 @​LarryHu0217
    • (user-facing): LoggerProviderOptions.forceFlushTimeoutMillis has been removed; pass timeoutMillis to LoggerProvider.forceFlush() instead.
  • feat(instrumentation-http)!: emit only stable HTTP semantic conventions. The OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN environment variable no longer changes HTTP attribute or metric emission — old (v1.7.0) and duplicate (http/http/dup) semconv outputs have been removed. #6819 @​maryliag
  • feat(instrumentation-fetch)!: emit only stable HTTP semantic conventions. The semconvStabilityOptIn instrumentation config option has been removed; old (v1.7.0) and duplicate semconv outputs are no longer emitted. #6819 @​maryliag
  • feat(instrumentation-xml-http-request)!: emit only stable HTTP semantic conventions. The semconvStabilityOptIn instrumentation config option has been removed; old (v1.7.0) and duplicate semconv outputs are no longer emitted. #6819 @​maryliag
  • feat(instrumentation-grpc)!: emit only stable network semantic conventions. The OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN environment variable no longer changes attribute emission — net.peer.name and net.peer.port (old) are no longer set; only server.address and server.port (stable). #6819 @​maryliag

:rocket: Features

  • feat(sdk-logs): allow modifying ReadWriteLogRecord properties (including hrTime, hrTimeObserved, and spanContext) in accordance with the OpenTelemetry Logs specification #6923 @​Babul422
  • feat(sdk-node): emit a deprecation warning when the JaegerPropagator is selected via OTEL_PROPAGATORS or declarative config; use tracecontext instead. @​pichlermarc
  • feat(instrumentation-http): set error.type to status code in metrics for error requests. #6919 @​raphael-theriault-swi

experimental/v0.220.0

0.220.0

:boom: Breaking Changes

  • refactor(sdk-logs)!: refactor BatchLogRecordProcessor constructor signature #6817 @​trentm
    • (user-facing): BatchLogRecordProcessor now takes a single options object with all possible properties, instead of two separate arguments. For example, before new BatchLogRecordProcessor(exporter, { maxQueueSize: 1000 }), after new BatchLogRecordProcessor({ exporter, maxQueueSize: 1000 }).
    • interface BufferConfig -> interface BatchLogRecordProcessorOptions, and now includes the exporter property
    • interface BatchLogRecordProcessorBrowserConfig -> interface BatchLogRecordProcessorBrowserOptions
    • (user-facing): SimpleLogRecordProcessor now takes a single options object with all possible properties. For example, before new SimpleLogRecordProcessor(exporter), after new SimpleLogRecordProcessor({ exporter }). #6836
  • refactor(configuration)!: change config file parsing to not add default values, nor merge *_list fields #6765 @​trentm
    • Responsibility for handling declarative config "nullBehavior" and "defaultBehavior" belongs in the "create" handling, currently in the "sdk-node" package.
  • docs(shim-opencensus): Notice: The @opentracing/shim-opencensus package will be removed in SDK 3.x, planned for approximately September 2026.
    • The OpenCensus and OpenTracing compatibility requirements in the OpenTelemetry specification have been deprecated.
  • chore(sdk-node)!: Drop support for deprecated OpenCensusMetricProducer from declarative config

:rocket: Features

  • feat(configuration): bump config schema to v1.1.0; rename without_scope_info → scope_info_enabled and without_target_info/development → target_info_enabled/development on the Prometheus pull exporter (semantics inverted), rename with_resource_constant_labels → resource_constant_labels. Validate file_format per the configuration versioning spec: accept any minor version of major 1 (e.g. 1.0, 1.1), warn when the minor version is newer than supported, and reject other major versions. #6781 @​MikeGoldsmith
  • feat(sdk-node): wire up id_generator from declarative config #6782 @​MikeGoldsmith
  • feat(sdk-node): wire up tracer_provider.sampler from declarative config (always_on, always_off, trace_id_ratio_based, parent_based); unrecognized variants warn and fall back to ParentBased(AlwaysOn) #6506 @​MikeGoldsmith
  • feat(propagator-env-carrier): empty name normalization #6827 @​pellared
  • feat(propagator-env-carrier): make EnvironmentGetter read the current process.env #6853 @​pellared

:bug: Bug Fixes

  • fix(sdk-logs): stop Logger.emit() doing work (record construction, metrics, processor onEmit) after the LoggerProvider has shut down #6826 @​anneheartrecord
  • fix(sdk-node): pass all config properties (endpoint, headers, timeout, TLS, compression, temporality preference, default histogram aggregation) to OTLP metric exporters in declarative config

title: chore(deps-dev): bump baseline-browser-mapping from 2.10.8 to 2.11.28
body:
Bumps [baseline-browser-mapping](https://github.com/web-platform-dx/baseline-browser-mapping) from 2.10.8 to 2.11.28.
Release notes

Sourced from baseline-browser-mapping's releases.

v2.11.0

What's Changed in 2.11.0

  • feat: Adds a new getTimeline() method for getting the series of minimum browser changes, either grouped by date or by browser.
  • refactor: Substantial refactoring of the data compression process that replaces the full list of browsers from @mdn/browser-compat-data and downstream-browsers.json and features from web-features (in their very pared down form) with a change-list timeline that reflects which versions supported Baseline (newly available) on a given date. Thanks to @​swwind for the idea!
  • refactor: Some common functions have been moved to a util.ts module for use in other scripts.
  • fix: Removes process.exit() calls when unsupported option combinations are passed to getCompatibleVersions() and getAllVersions() in favour of throwing an Error. There is a small security risk with process.exit() calls that sites accepting unsanitised inputs could be the subject of attacks. Unsupported config options now throw and Error which should allow for more graceful handling. Thanks to @​bnbdr for flagging this as vulnerability CVE-2026-45819 .

Fixes #134

Full Changelog: https://github.com/web-platform-dx/baseline-browser-mapping/compare/v2.10.44...v2.11.0

title: fix(client-common): quote table identifiers in insert query
body:
Fixes #1004.

Quote table identifiers in `client.insert()` so names containing special characters, such as hyphens, produce valid SQL. Qualified database/table names are quoted component by component, while dots and escaped quotes inside quoted identifiers remain part of the identifier.

The focused unit tests cover plain, hyphenated, qualified, quoted and mixed names, escaped quotes, column lists and exclusions. Changelog entries cover the common package and both clients. Current upstream `main` was merged into this existing branch.

Validation passed in Docker with Node.js 24.21.0, using a Linux checkout to preserve the repository's source symlinks:

- `CLICKHOUSE_TEST_SKIP_INIT=1 TEST_MODE=unit npx vitest run --config packages/client-node/vitest.config.ts packages/client-common/__tests__/unit/client.test.ts --maxWorkers=2`: 15 tests passed.
- The same focused command with `packages/client-web/vitest.config.ts`: 15 tests passed in Chromium.
- `npm run --workspace @clickhouse/client build`, `npm run --workspace @clickhouse/client-web build` and `npm run --workspace @clickhouse/client-common build`: passed.
- `npm run lint`: passed across repository workspaces.
- Prettier check on the two modified TypeScript files and three package changelogs: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The full test suite and database integration tests were not run locally.

title: chore(deps-dev): bump undici from 8.9.0 to 8.10.2
body:
Bumps [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici) from 8.9.0 to 8.10.2.
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v8.10.2

⚠️ Security fixes

High severity

  • GHSA-vp8m-p9jh-q5pm: cache and deduplication interceptors could use caller-controlled request metadata instead of the authoritative dispatcher origin, enabling cross-origin cache poisoning and data disclosure. Undici now derives interceptor identities from the dispatcher origin and bypasses origin-dependent interceptors when no authoritative origin exists. Fixed by caf6194d.
  • GHSA-w293-vg96-wgc3: BalancedPool could drop function-valued connection options while cloning its configuration, including custom TLS certificate validation callbacks. Undici now preserves connect and legacy tls options when creating upstreams. Fixed by 8f5868fb.
  • GHSA-rfgv-xxqx-mfg5: a WebSocket server could select a subprotocol when none was requested, causing an uncaught TypeError that could terminate the process. Undici now rejects the handshake with protocol error 1002. Fixed by 66e12816.

Medium severity

  • GHSA-3wwx-pv8p-q78v: a malformed permessage-deflate payload exceeding the configured decompression limit could emit an unhandled zlib error and terminate the process. Undici now destroys the inflater after reaching the limit. Fixed by 4411a238.
  • GHSA-rx4f-c7p8-82vq: an unclean WebSocketStream close could create an unobserved rejected promise when its writable stream was locked, potentially terminating the process. Undici now propagates the failure through the retained writable stream controller. Fixed by 662d0ea6.
  • GHSA-2jfj-6hjv-fm6j: shared caches could store and replay responses containing Set-Cookie, disclosing one user's cookies to another caller. Undici now excludes these responses from shared caches, including existing entries and revalidation paths. Fixed by cb75bbb3.
  • GHSA-3xpg-4rpp-hhhm: the decompression interceptor did not bound decoded output, allowing compressed responses to consume excessive memory. Undici now limits every decompression stage to 64 MiB by default and supports a configurable maxSize. Fixed by 7aac7f12.
  • GHSA-pmjh-fq2x-6v4x: a terminal retry failure after response headers were exposed could orphan the original response body, causing consumers to hang indefinitely. Undici now propagates the terminal error to the exposed body. Fixed by e905b5b8.

Low severity

  • GHSA-8436-99hf-9mmv: cache interceptors could store and replay responses to unsafe HTTP methods such as POST or DELETE. Undici now restricts cache reads and writes to safe methods while preserving invalidation by successful unsafe requests. Fixed by 2be07bf9.
  • GHSA-2gqq-gqf2-x968: the dump interceptor could treat an oversized chunked response as successfully truncated when no Content-Length was present. Undici now enforces maxSize against received bytes and aborts oversized responses. Fixed by 6d583124.
  • GHSA-r53p-7pc4-xj5r: the retry interceptor could concatenate a resumed response with inconsistent framing into downstream output, enabling response splitting or corruption. Undici now validates Content-Range against the original response framing before resuming. Fixed by 0160a719.

title: fix: export public API types from the client packages
body:
Closes #997

## Problem

Six types that appear in the public API's own method signatures aren't
re-exported from the package root, so there's no supported way to import them:

| Type | Used by |
|---|---|
| `QueryParamsWithFormat` | parameter of `query()` |
| `PingParams` | parameter of `ping()` |
| `ResultJSONType` | return of `ResultSet.json()` |
| `RowJSONType` | return of `Row.json()` |
| `ClickHouseSummary` | field of `InsertResult` / `CommandResult` |
| `WithClickHouseSummary` | field of `InsertResult` / `CommandResult` |

All six are exported from `client-common`, but since 1.23.0 bundled it into the
client (#845) the package root re-exports a curated list, and these were left
out. `@clickhouse/client-common` is deprecated and its npm message points back
at `@clickhouse/client`, and there's no `exports` map, so the only workarounds
are copying the type or reaching into `dist/`. Same shape as #935.

The consequence is that you can't write a wrapper with the same signature as the
method you're wrapping.

## Change

Added the six type re-exports, each next to its existing sibling in the block:
`QueryParamsWithFormat` after `QueryParams`, the two summary types after
`InsertResult`, the two JSON result types after `BaseResultSet`, and
`PingParams` after `PingResult`.

The gap is in **both** clients, so this fixes `client-node` and `client-web`
alike — their re-export blocks are byte-identical apart from the package name in
one doc comment. Types only; no runtime change.

I left the internals alone (`Connection*`, `LogWriter`, `getConnectionParams`
and friends), since those are clearly excluded on purpose.

## Verification

Using the repro from the issue, compiled against the built package with
`tsc --noEmit --module nodenext --moduleResolution nodenext --target esnext --strict`:

- before this change: fails, one error per type
- after: compiles clean

## A note on tests

I didn't add a test, because I don't think one would hold here. `npm run
typecheck` is `tsc --noEmit` per workspace with `include: ["./src/**/*.ts"]`, so
anything under `__tests__` is outside its scope, and Vitest goes through esbuild,
which strips types without checking them. A type-level test asserting these
imports would therefore pass just as happily with the exports missing, which
seemed worse than no test at all.

If you'd like real coverage for the public type surface, I'm happy to follow up
with a dedicated `tsc` project that compiles a type-assertion file against
`dist/index.d.ts` and wire it into CI — that would have caught both this and
#935. Just say which shape you'd prefer.

title: fix: remove a trailing semicolon that is followed by a comment
body:
Closes #973

## Problem

`query()` appends ` \nFORMAT <format>` after `removeTrailingSemi()`, which only strips semicolons that are the very last characters of the string. With a comment after the semicolon, the loop stops at the comment, the `;` survives, and the appended `FORMAT` becomes a second statement:

```
SELECT 13 AS a; -- trailing comment
FORMAT JSONEachRow
```

```
Code: 62. Syntax error (Multi-statements are not allowed): failed at position 15 (end of query)
```

## Change

`removeTrailingSemi()` now scans the query and removes only the semicolons that come after the last character of the statement, skipping string literals (`'...'`, with `''` and backslash escapes), heredocs (`$tag$...$tag$` and `$$...$$`), quoted identifiers (`` `...` `` and `"..."`) and comments (`--`, `#`, `/* */`). Heredocs are lexed before comments, so a `--` inside one is not taken for a comment. Comments are kept, so the query that's sent still reads as written: `SELECT 1; -- note` becomes `SELECT 1 -- note`, and the `\n` before `FORMAT` still terminates the line comment as it does today for a comment without a semicolon.

It's a single linear pass. Two small consequences, both of which I think are improvements but am flagging:

- semicolons separated by whitespace are removed too (`SELECT 1 ; ;` → `SELECT 1`; previously the inner one was left behind);
- `command()` and `exec()` share the helper, so they no longer send a stranded `;` before a trailing comment either. That was harmless for them, as the issue notes, since they append nothing.

A query made only of semicolons is still returned unchanged, as before.

`removeTrailingSemi` is now exported from `client.ts` so it can be unit-tested; the package index re-exports named items only, so it does not become public API.

## Verification

Against a real ClickHouse server (26.9.10.4, Docker), using the built client:

| query | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `SELECT 13 AS a WHERE 0 -- trailing comment` | OK | OK |
| `SELECT 13 AS a; -- trailing comment` | **error 62** | `[{"a":13}]` |
| `SELECT 13 AS a; /* block */` | **error 62** | `[{"a":13}]` |
| `SELECT 13 AS a; # hash comment` | **error 62** | `[{"a":13}]` |
| `SELECT ';' AS a; -- semicolon in a string` | **error 62** | `[{"a":";"}]` |
| `SELECT $$;$$ AS a; -- note` | **error 62** | `[{"a":";"}]` |
| `SELECT $tag$-- text$tag$ AS a;` | OK | OK |
| `SELECT $$a # b /* c$$ AS a;` | OK | OK |

The string and heredoc rows check that a `;` or comment marker inside a literal is left alone; the last two already worked on `main` and are there to make sure they still do.

New unit tests in `remove_trailing_semi.test.ts` (25 cases) cover trailing semicolons, each comment style, strings/heredocs/identifiers/comments containing `;` or comment markers, and the all-semicolons case. Against the previous implementation the comment cases fail; with this change all pass. The full unit suite passes (45 files, 433 tests), as do `prettier --check`, `eslint --max-warnings=0` on `client.ts`, and `tsc --noEmit` for `client-common`.

title: ResultSet.stream(): mid-stream server error surfaces as `Error: aborted` with response compression (or a slow consumer)
body:
### Describe the bug

A query can fail after ClickHouse (25.11+) has sent `200 OK` and started to stream the body. In that case the server appends the in-band exception block (`x-clickhouse-exception-tag`) and then closes the connection. `ResultSet.stream()` is the path that parses this block, but it raises the server error only when the client reads the body as fast as it arrives.

When the consumer is slower than the socket, the last bytes of the body are still queued in the `http.IncomingMessage` when the connection closes. Node.js destroys the response with `Error: aborted` (`ECONNRESET`) and drops those queued bytes. The exception block is in those bytes, so the parser never sees it, and the caller gets `Error: aborted` instead of the `ClickHouseError`.

Response compression always causes this, because zlib decompresses asynchronously and is slower than the socket. All three codecs (`gzip`, `zstd`, `br`) are affected. Without compression, a consumer that waits only 1 ms per batch has the same result.

Results on `main` (live server, every run listed):

| Consumer | Result |
|---|---|
| no compression, fast loop | `ClickHouseError` code 395 (7/7) |
| no compression, `await` 1 ms or 5 ms per batch | `Error: aborted` (4/4) |
| `compression: { response: true }` (gzip) | `Error: aborted` (7/7) |
| `compression: { response: { codec: 'zstd' } }` | `Error: aborted` (3/3) |
| `compression: { response: { codec: 'br' } }` | `Error: aborted` (3/3) |

With gzip, the formats `JSONEachRow`, `JSONCompactEachRow`, `CSV`, `TabSeparated`, and `json()` on `JSONEachRow` (it uses `stream()`) all give `Error: aborted`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a client with `compression: { response: true }`.
2. Stream a query that fails after about 25 MB of output (the code example below).
3. The loop rejects with `Error: aborted` (`code: 'ECONNRESET'`) after about 415 000 rows. With `compression: { response: false }`, the same query rejects with `ClickHouseError` code `395`.

### Expected behaviour

The same `ClickHouseError` (code `395`, message `boom`) that the uncompressed path gives. The client receives the error from the server, but does not report it.

Evidence that the server sends a complete error block with every codec (same query, `curl` with `Accept-Encoding: <codec>`, then decoded with a strict decoder):

```
curl: (18) transfer closed with outstanding read data remaining
gzip: 16507702 compressed bytes, strict gunzip OK, ends with "\r\n__exception__\r\n<tag>\r\nCode: 395. DB::Exception: boom-425000: ..."
br:   15962956 compressed bytes, strict decode OK, ends with the same block
zstd: 16352526 compressed bytes, strict decode OK, ends with the same block
```

The compressed stream is complete and only the HTTP chunked framing is cut. Node.js also receives all the bytes: when the raw `IncomingMessage` is read with no backpressure (`res.on('data')`), the collected body decodes to the full exception block in 3/3 runs.

### Code example

```js
// node repro.cjs  (client built from main)
const { createClient } = require('@clickhouse/client')

;(async () => {
  const client = createClient({
    url: 'http://localhost:8123',
    compression: { response: true }, // `false` -> ClickHouseError 395
  })
  let rows = 0
  try {
    const rs = await client.query({
      query: `SELECT toInt32(number) AS n, randomPrintableASCII(40) AS s,
                     throwIf(number = 425000, 'boom') AS e
              FROM system.numbers LIMIT 1000000`,
      format: 'JSONEachRow',
      clickhouse_settings: { max_block_size: '1000' },
    })
    for await (const batch of rs.stream()) {
      rows += batch.length
      // without compression, this line alone also gives `Error: aborted`:
      // await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1))
    }
  } catch (e) {
    console.log(rows, e.constructor.name, e.code, e.message)
  } finally {
    await client.close()
  }
})()
```

### Error log

```
415738 Error ECONNRESET aborted

[ERROR][@clickhouse/client][Connection] An error occurred while decompressing the response
Caused by: Error: aborted
    at Socket.socketCloseListener (node:_http_client:535:19)
    at Socket.emit (node:events:531:35)
    at TCP.<anonymous> (node:net:347:12) {
  code: 'ECONNRESET'
}
```

### Root cause

- `packages/client-node/src/connection/compression.ts:24-35` (gzip; zstd `55-66`, br `72-83`) connects the response to the decompressor with `Stream.pipeline(response, decompressor)`. Without compression, `compression.ts:18-20` and `socket_pool.ts:307` give the raw `IncomingMessage` to `ResultSet`, and `result_set.ts:284-299` connects it to the row parser with `Stream.pipeline`.
- When the server closes the connection, Node.js (`_http_client` `socketCloseListener`) calls `res.destroy(new ConnResetException('aborted'))` because the response is not complete. This discards the data still queued in the `IncomingMessage`. `Stream.pipeline` then destroys the next stages with the same error, which also discards the decompressor's input and output buffers.
- Measured at the `aborted` event with gzip: `res.readableLength` = 46 716 and 57 221 bytes, `gunzip.writableLength` = 65 536 bytes. The exception block is at the end of this data, so the parser at `result_set.ts:249-256` never gets it.
- With a fast synchronous consumer and no compression, the queue is empty when the socket closes, so the block is already parsed. That is why the uncompressed case appears to work.

### Suggested fix

Do not let the connection close discard bytes that the client already received. One shape, in the client-node HTTP layer, for a `200` response that has `x-clickhouse-exception-tag`:

1. On `aborted`, move the bytes still queued in the `IncomingMessage` to the next stage, before they are discarded. Do not let `Stream.pipeline` forward the error at once.
2. Call `end()` on the decompressor, not `destroy()`, so that it emits its buffered output.
3. Let the existing parser in `ResultSet` read the tail. If a complete exception block is there, raise the `ClickHouseError`. If not, still fail with the original `aborted` error.

A standalone Node.js check of this shape (gzip): on `aborted`, write `res.readableBuffer` (33-58 KB) into the gunzip stream, then call `gunzip.end()`. This gave the full exception block in 3/3 runs, and memory stays bounded. `readableBuffer` is not a documented Node.js API, so a maintainer may prefer another way to keep these bytes.

Behavior that must not change:

- A connection drop that has no exception block must still fail with an error. It must never end as a successful, truncated result.
- Fast uncompressed consumers must keep the current behavior, and so must responses without the tag header (servers before 25.11).

The fix also applies to the uncompressed slow-consumer path. Related: #976 (`text()` / `exec()` have no detector). A detector added there gets the bytes from the same `IncomingMessage`, so it has the same loss. #974 / #975 change the parser itself and do not change this behavior: the result is the same before and after #975.

### Configuration

#### Environment

- Client version: `@clickhouse/client` 1.24.0 (`main` at 7c01e77)
- Language version: Node.js v22.23.3
- OS: Linux (Debian, Docker)

#### ClickHouse server

- ClickHouse Server version: 26.9.1.1629
- ClickHouse Server non-default settings, if any: none. `http_write_exception_in_output_format` is `0` (the server default). The query sets `max_block_size=1000` only to make blocks small.
- `CREATE TABLE` statements for tables involved: none (`system.numbers`)

`@clickhouse/client-web` is not tested here. Browsers decompress the response themselves, so the behavior there can be different.

**Classification:** impact: none · area: API & diagnostics (mid-stream errors, response compression)

---

title: Aborting a request that waits for a socket destroys that socket under a later request (socket hang up)
body:
### Describe the bug

When all `max_open_connections` sockets are busy, new requests wait for one. If a waiting request is aborted, a later request fails with `socket hang up` (`ECONNRESET`) about `idle_socket_ttl` after the socket it uses was last released.

Node.js releases that socket twice: once when the previous request finishes, and again from `onSocketNT`, which emits `free` when it hands the socket to the already-aborted request ([source](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/lib/_http_client.js#L1192-L1218)). The `free` listener in `socket_pool.ts` starts a new idle timer each time and overwrites `idle_timeout_handle` without clearing the previous one ([source](https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/blob/main/packages/client-node/src/connection/socket_pool.ts#L437-L474)). When the next request takes the socket, only the latest timer is cleared, so the first one fires and calls `socket.destroy()` mid-request.

It needs two things: more concurrent requests than `max_open_connections`, so requests wait for a socket, and an `abort_signal` that fires while a request is waiting. We hit it in production at Vercel when a change packed more concurrent requests per process: thousands of `socket hang up` errors per hour, from zero before. A short `AbortSignal.timeout()` on a side query was enough to trigger it, even without client cancellations.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `max_open_connections: 1`, default `keep_alive`.
2. Request A takes the only socket (1s query). Requests R and B wait for it.
3. Abort R while it waits. B is a 4s query.
4. B fails with `socket hang up` at about 3.5s: A's release plus the 2.5s TTL.

### Expected behaviour

B succeeds. Aborting a waiting request should not affect other requests.

### Code example

No ClickHouse needed: the server answers `SELECT <ms>` after `<ms>` milliseconds.

```js
const http = require('node:http')
const { createClient } = require('@clickhouse/client')

const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
  let body = ''
  req.on('data', (c) => (body += c))
  req.on('end', () => {
    const delay = Number(/SELECT (\d+)/.exec(body)?.[1] ?? 0)
    setTimeout(() => res.end('Ok.'), delay)
  })
})

server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', async () => {
  const client = createClient({
    url: `http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}`,
    max_open_connections: 1,
  })
  const t0 = Date.now()
  const run = (name, query, abort_signal) =>
    client
      .command({ query, abort_signal })
      .then(() => console.log(`${Date.now() - t0}ms ${name}: ok`))
      .catch((e) => console.log(`${Date.now() - t0}ms ${name}: ${e.message}`))

  const controller = new AbortController()
  const a = run('A', 'SELECT 1000')
  const r = run('R (aborted while waiting)', 'SELECT 100', controller.signal)
  const b = run('B', 'SELECT 4000')
  setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 500)
  await Promise.all([a, r, b])
  await client.close()
  server.close()
})
```

### Error log

```
 513ms R (aborted while waiting): The user aborted a request.
1014ms A: ok
3516ms B: socket hang up
```

Clearing the previous timer at the top of the `free` listener fixes it (B succeeds at about 5s). In a 400-query stress run with 3 sockets and 30% of queries aborted at random, that change takes `socket hang up` from 18 to 19 per run to 0, and idle sockets still close after the TTL. I'll open a PR with the fix and a regression test.

### Configuration

#### Environment

- Client version: 1.23.1, 1.24.0 and `main` (1.16.0 has the same code in `node_base_connection.js`)
- Language version: Node.js 24.14.0
- OS: macOS, and Linux on Vercel Functions

#### ClickHouse server

- Not server-specific. Reproduced against ClickHouse Cloud and a plain HTTP server.

title: fix(client-node): stop an aborted waiting request from destroying a socket in use
body:
tl;dr; stops `socket hang up` errors after an aborted request, by clearing the previous idle-socket timer when a socket is released a second time.

## Problem
- When all `max_open_connections` sockets are busy, new requests wait for one. If a waiting request is aborted, Node.js releases the next free socket twice: once for the request that finished, once for the aborted one.
- Each release starts an idle timer and overwrites `idle_timeout_handle` without clearing the previous timer. The first timer fires `idle_socket_ttl` later and destroys the socket while another request is using it.

## Solution
- We clear the pending timer before starting a new one. Idle sockets still close after the TTL.

<details>
<summary>Implementation details</summary>

- Fixes #1040, which has a standalone repro.
- The second release comes from `onSocketNT` in Node's `_http_client.js`, which emits `free` on the socket it hands to an already-destroyed request.
- The new test uses a plain HTTP server and `max_open_connections: 1`: one request holds the socket, a waiting request is aborted, and a third request runs past the release plus the TTL. It fails on `main` with `socket hang up` and passes with the fix.
- Stress run (400 requests, 3 sockets, 30% aborted at random): 18 to 19 hang-ups per run before, 0 after.
- We hit this on Vercel Functions, where one process serves many concurrent requests: thousands of `socket hang up` errors per hour once requests started waiting for sockets.
- Includes the test and a changelog entry for `@clickhouse/client`.

</details>

title: fix(client-node): honor already-aborted request signals
body:
An abort signal already aborted before a Node client call was ignored because the request wrapper subscribed only to future abort events. Initialize the wrapper from the signal's current state so a pre-aborted command rejects with `AbortError` before reaching the HTTP server.

The native regression uses a real local HTTP server and checks both `AbortError` and zero requests. The existing queued-abort/socket regression remains green. Node-only package, runtime version, lockfile and changelog are prepared for the next patch version, 1.24.2; no package is released by this PR.

Validation: identical integration cases give 1 pass / 1 failure before and 2 passes after on Node 24.19. Package source typecheck, lint and changed-file formatting pass. Cached focused dependencies were used; no full workspace, ClickHouse-server, browser, Bun or Node-version matrix was run.

Related: [#802](https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/pull/802) is closed and unmerged; [#1041](https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/pull/1041) addresses a separate queued-socket timer path. This fix does not change custom abort reasons or all cancellation behavior.

title: Documented URL parameter application_id is rejected: "Unknown URL parameters: application_id"
JSONEachRow: in-band {"exception": ...} row (http_write_exception_in_output_format=1) is returned as data; stream()/json() raise no error
docs: drop application_id from the supported URL parameters
body:
## Description

Fixes #1052 by updating the documentation instead of the parser.

The URL parameters table listed `application_id`, but the parser in `loadConfigOptionsFromURL` only ever accepted the legacy `application` name — passing `application_id` is rejected with an unknown-parameter error. Since it has never worked, no user can be relying on it, so the smallest correct fix is to remove the row from the supported URL parameters table rather than teach the parser a second name.

No code, test, or changelog changes.

Updates `playwright` from 1.63.0 to 1.64.0
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.64.0

🧰 WebMCP

New page.webmcp and frame.webmcp give access to the tools that a page registers through the experimental WebMCP browser API, so you can test them like any other part of your app:

const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ['--enable-features=WebMCP'] });
const page = await browser.newPage();
await page.goto('https://example.com');

for (const tool of await page.webmcp.tools())
console.log(tool.name, tool.description);


const result = await page.webmcp.callTool('add', { a: 2, b: 40 });
console.log(result.content[0].text); // "42"

Playwright MCP also supports WebMCP by default, with page-defined tools offered to the agent as webmcp_<tool>. Pass --no-webmcp to opt out.

playwright-cli exposes them as well:

playwright-cli webmcp-list
playwright-cli webmcp-call search_catalog --params '{"query":"cats"}'

🎬 Better videos

Videos can now be recorded at a custom frame rate, and the decorations for actions are styled with plain CSS:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

use: {

title: Support a token provider callback for `access_token` (parity with Python's `token_provider`)
body:
## Problem

`access_token` is a static string captured at client construction:

```ts
/** A JWT access token to authenticate with ClickHouse.
 *  JWT token authentication is supported in ClickHouse Cloud only.
 *  Should not be set if {@link username} or {@link password} are provided.
 *  @default empty */
access_token?: string;
```

It is read once in `getConnectionParams()` and the connection precomputes
`` this.defaultAuthHeader = `Bearer ${params.auth.access_token}` `` in its constructor.
Nothing re-reads it afterwards.

That works for long-lived tokens, but JWTs issued by an external IdP are often
short-lived — commonly 5–15 minutes. With a static string there are only two
options today:

1. **Per-request override** — `auth: { access_token }` on every `query` / `insert` /
   `command` / `exec` call. This works (and correctly takes precedence over the
   client-level credential), but it has to be remembered at every call site, it
   can't be applied to `ping()` in its `/ping` form, and there's no safety net if
   one call site is missed.
2. **Recreate the client** — `await client.close()` then `createClient(...)`, which
   discards the connection pool on every rotation.

Neither is a good fit for a credential that rotates every few minutes.

## Prior art in other official clients

**Python (`clickhouse-connect`)** has exactly this, and additionally re-invokes the
provider after an auth rejection:

> `token_provider` — Callable that supplies a JWT initially and after an
> authentication rejection. An async provider may be used with `get_async_client`.

**Go (`clickhouse-go` v2.35+)** has a callback too:

```go
// GetJWT should return a JWT for authentication with ClickHouse Cloud.
// This is called per connection/request, so you may cache the token in your app if needed.
// Use this instead of Auth.Username and Auth.Password if you're using JWT auth.
GetJWT GetJWTFunc

type GetJWTFunc = func(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
```

**Java v2** takes a static string but at least offers a mutator,
`client.updateBearerToken(newJwtToken)`.

So the JS client is currently the only one of the four with no way to supply a
fresh token without rebuilding the client or threading the token through every
call site.

## Proposal

Allow `access_token` to accept a provider in addition to a string:

```ts
access_token?: string | (() => string | Promise<string>);
```

Invoked per request when a function is supplied, so the existing per-request
override semantics and the connection pool are both unaffected. A caller that
wants caching can implement it inside the provider, as the Go docs suggest.

Optionally — and this is the part Python gets right that Go doesn't — re-invoke
the provider once after an authentication rejection and retry, which removes the
race where a token expires between being fetched and being used.

Happy to open a PR if the shape sounds reasonable. An alternative that avoids
widening the existing field would be a separate `token_provider` option matching
Python's naming.

## Unrelated docs issue noticed while investigating

The hosted docs page for the JS client
(https://clickhouse.com/docs/integrations/language-clients/javascript) appears to
be behind the typings:

- `access_token` is not listed in the configuration options table at all.
- The `BaseQueryParams` snippet shows `auth?: { username: string, password: string }`
  without the `| { access_token: string }` variant — so the per-request override,
  which is currently the only workable pattern for rotating tokens, isn't documented.

Happy to split that into a separate issue if preferred.

## Environment

- `@clickhouse/client` 1.24.1
- Behaviour confirmed against the published package typings and `dist` output.

title: test: pin the SQL that query(), command() and exec() send
body:
Tracking issue: #1074. Stack: **#1065** → #1066 → #1067 → #1068 → #1069 → #1070 → #1071 → #1072

Part 1 of the stack that adds optional support for the official ClickHouse SQL lexer (`@clickhouse/lexer`). No behavior change.

## Why

title: feat: add an internal lexer-based SQL rewriter
body:
Tracking issue: #1074. Stack: #1065 → #1066 → **#1067** → #1068 → #1069 → #1070 → #1071 → #1072

Part 3 of the lexer stack. Depends on #1066. No user-visible change: nothing calls the new code yet.

## Why

The client's string-based handling of trailing semicolons can't tell a `;` inside a comment, string or heredoc from a real one (#973). The official lexer, `@clickhouse/lexer`, is ClickHouse's own `Lexer.cpp` compiled to WASM, so it splits a query exactly as the server does. This PR adds the code that uses it, on its own, so it can be reviewed before any public API is involved.

## What

- `sql/tokens.ts`:
  - `ClickHouseSqlLexer`: our own description of the four lexer members we use (`loadLexer`, `tokenizeSync`, `isError`, `TOKEN_NAMES`). `import * as lexer from "@clickhouse/lexer"` fits it as-is, and the client doesn't depend on the package's types.
  - `createSqlTokenizer`: maps the lexer's token types to a few kinds, **by name**, because the numbers change between lexer releases. Unknown names map to `other`.
  - It returns `null` when:
    - the lexer reports an error, such as an unclosed quote;
    - the lexer throws;
    - the tokens don't add up to the query exactly, which happens with a lone UTF-16 surrogate.
- `sql/lexer_rewriter.ts`:
  - `stripTrailingSemi` removes the semicolons after the last statement token and keeps comments, so `SELECT 1; -- note` becomes `SELECT 1 -- note`.
  - When the tokenizer returns `null`, it falls back to the existing string-based logic.
  - `withFormat` is unchanged for now; part 5 switches it over.
- `@clickhouse/lexer@1.0.1`: a root dev dependency, pinned exactly and used only by tests. The lockfile diff is only the new entry.
- ESLint `no-restricted-imports` blocks `@clickhouse/lexer` in the clients' source. The package is ESM-only, and an import there would compile to a `require()` that fails on Node versions before 20.19. Users pass it in instead (part 4).

## Testing

New `sql_lexer_rewriter.test.ts` runs against the real WASM lexer in both the Node and browser suites. It covers:
- strings, quoted identifiers, heredocs and nested comments;
- the #973 shapes;
- multiple statements;
- each fallback path;
- token mapping with a fake lexer.

Full Node unit suite, typecheck and lint pass.

Part 3 added a lexer-based rewriter that nothing used yet. This PR adds the public option and turns it on for the two lowest-risk call sites: `command()` and `exec()`. They only strip trailing semicolons and append nothing, so the worst a mistake can do is leave a stray `;`. `query()`, which also appends FORMAT, moves over in part 5.

- **New option:** `sql_lexer?: ClickHouseSqlLexer` (`client-common/src/config.ts`), with `@default undefined`.

  ```ts

  const client = createClient({ sql_lexer: lexer });
  ```

  - The user imports the lexer and passes it in; the client never imports it. Like the existing `tracer` option, this keeps the client free of dependencies, works with every bundler, and avoids loading an ESM-only package from the CommonJS build.
  - `ClickHouseSqlLexer` is exported as a type from `@clickhouse/client` and `@clickhouse/client-web`.
- **Loading:** the lexer is loaded once, on first use, and the promise is cached.
  - Without `sql_lexer`, the code path is unchanged, with no added `await`.
- **Load failure** (for example a CSP without `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, or Cloudflare Workers): the client logs one WARN and keeps its built-in handling.

  - The message links to the new `docs/howto/sql_lexer.md`.
- **Optional peer dependency:** `@clickhouse/lexer` (`^1.0.0`, `peerDependenciesMeta.optional`) in both client packages. It's only a compatibility signal; nothing is installed for users who don't opt in.
- **Changelogs:** a new `# 1.25.0` heading in both `packages/client-node/CHANGELOG.md` and `packages/client-web/CHANGELOG.md`.

| `SELECT 1;`            | `SELECT 1`                         | `SELECT 1`            |

title: fix: with sql_lexer, query() strips a semicolon before a comment
body:

Part 5 of the lexer stack. Depends on #1068. Addresses #973 for users who set `sql_lexer`.

## Why

`query()` appends `FORMAT <format>` to the user's SQL. When the query ends with a semicolon followed by a comment (`SELECT 1; -- note`), the built-in handling doesn't remove the semicolon. The server then sees two statements and rejects the query with `Multi-statements are not allowed` (#973).

| `SELECT 1 -- comment;` | `SELECT 1 -- comment \nFORMAT JSON`        | `SELECT 1 -- comment; \nFORMAT JSON` |

title: test: compare the built-in SQL handling with the official lexer
body:
Tracking issue: #1074. Stack: #1065 → #1066 → #1067 → #1068 → #1069 → #1070 → #1071 → **#1072**

Part 8 of the lexer stack. Depends on #1071. Tests only, no behavior change.

## Why

The client's built-in SQL handling is hand-written, and every fix to it (#1031, #972, …) risks missing a rule of ClickHouse's real lexer. This PR turns `@clickhouse/lexer` into a reference for that code, so a change to the built-in handling gets immediate feedback in the unit suite, without a server.

## What

- **`__tests__/utils/sql_corpus.ts`:**
  - `sqlCorpus`: about 50 queries that are easy to get wrong by hand. They cover semicolons before every comment style (including `//`, `#!` and `\r`), semicolons in strings, quoted identifiers and heredocs, nested comments, `$` in identifiers, and trailing `SETTINGS` clauses.
  - `sqlLexerModes`: the two modes, for `describe.each`.
  - `KNOWN_DIFFERENCES`: where the built-in handling reads a corpus query differently from the lexer, per method, each with a reason (#973, #970, or spaced semicolons).
- **New `unit/sql_rewriting_vs_lexer.test.ts`** (no server): for every corpus query, compares what `query()` and `command()`/`exec()` would send, in each mode.
  - Two rewrites count as the same when the official lexer reads them as the same tokens, ignoring whitespace and comments.
  - It fails when a query differs and isn't listed, showing both outputs. It also fails when a listed query **no longer** differs, telling you to remove the entry.
- **`integration/sql_lexer.test.ts`:** the same corpus, judged by the server.
  - The expected answer is the original query sent through `exec()` with `default_format`, so no FORMAT clause is appended to it.

  - the trailing-semicolon blocks of `node_exec.test.ts` and `web_exec.test.ts`.

title: Add optional support for the official ClickHouse SQL lexer
body:
## Summary

Add optional support for the official ClickHouse SQL lexer, [`@clickhouse/lexer`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@clickhouse/lexer), so the client can read user SQL the same way the server does. It would stay opt-in: no new runtime dependency, and no change in behavior unless a user turns it on. Separately, use it in this repository's tests to check our own SQL handling against the server's tokenizer.

## Why

The client makes small edits to the user's SQL before sending it:

- `query()`, `command()` and `exec()` strip trailing semicolons;
- `query()` appends `FORMAT <format>`.

This is done with plain string handling, which can't tell whether a `;` or a keyword is inside a comment, a string, a quoted identifier or a heredoc. That has produced a steady stream of bugs:

- #973: `SELECT 1; -- note` fails with `Multi-statements are not allowed`, because the `;` before the comment is kept and the appended `FORMAT` becomes a second statement.
- #970: `FORMAT` is appended after a trailing `SETTINGS` clause, which older servers reject.

Each open fix adds its own small hand-written scanner. #1031 does this for #973, and #972 for #970. ClickHouse's lexer has many rules that are easy to miss: `$` is allowed inside identifiers, `//` starts a comment, comments can nest, and more. Testing #1031 against a live server found two such cases that its unit tests didn't cover ([details](https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-js/pull/1031#issuecomment-6319861312)).

`@clickhouse/lexer` is ClickHouse's own `src/Parsers/Lexer.cpp` compiled to WebAssembly:

- about 9 KB, Apache-2.0, no dependencies;
- runs in Node.js and browsers;
- published whenever the upstream lexer changes.

Using it removes the guesswork: the client splits the query exactly as the server will.

## How it would stay optional

- **The client never imports the package.** Users install it and pass the module in through a new `sql_lexer` option, the same pattern as the existing `tracer` option. This:
  - keeps `@clickhouse/client` and `@clickhouse/client-web` free of runtime dependencies;
  - avoids bundler errors for users who don't install the lexer;
  - avoids loading an ESM-only package from the clients' CommonJS build.
- **It's declared as an optional `peerDependency`**, only to signal which versions are compatible.
- **Without `sql_lexer`, nothing changes.** The query text sent to the server stays the same, byte for byte.
- **Safe fallback.** If the lexer can't load, the client logs one warning (linking to a docs page) and keeps its built-in handling. This happens, for example, under a Content Security Policy without `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, or on runtimes that don't allow compiling WebAssembly, such as Cloudflare Workers. A query the lexer can't tokenize, such as one with an unclosed quote, also uses the built-in handling and is left for the server to report.

## How it would be used

```ts
import { createClient } from "@clickhouse/client"; // or "@clickhouse/client-web"
import * as lexer from "@clickhouse/lexer";

const client = createClient({ sql_lexer: lexer });

// Works: sent as `SELECT 1 -- note` followed by `FORMAT JSON`
await client.query({ query: "SELECT 1; -- note" });

// Sent as `SELECT 1 FORMAT JSON SETTINGS max_threads = 1`
await client.query({ query: "SELECT 1 SETTINGS max_threads = 1" });
```

With `sql_lexer` set:

- `query()`, `command()` and `exec()` remove trailing semicolons using the lexer's tokens. Comments are kept, and `;` inside strings, identifiers, heredocs and comments is left alone.
- `query()` puts `FORMAT` before a trailing top-level `SETTINGS` clause. A `SETTINGS` clause in a subquery, a column named `settings`, or `... SETTINGS a = 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2` keeps today's behavior.

Possible later uses: safer quoting of identifiers in `insert()` (#945, #1004), and a safe SQL builder.

## How it helps testing

This part is useful on its own, even before any user opts in. The lexer would only be a dev dependency here.

- **Checking hand-written fixes against the server's tokenizer.** We send a query unchanged (with `?default_format=...`) and as the client would rewrite it, then compare the server's answers. On a 44-query corpus:

  | Implementation | Same answer as the server |
  |---|---|
  | `main` | 25 / 44 |
  | PR #1031 | 42 / 44 |
  | official lexer | 44 / 44 |

  The same corpus can check #972 and any future fix that touches SQL text. Step 8 of the rollout below makes this a permanent test. When PR #1031's scanner was swapped in, the unit test reported the 16 cases it fixes and the 2 it still misses within seconds.
- **The repo's own SQL scanners.** The upstream test runner in `tests/clickhouse-test-runner` scans SQL by hand to split statements (`split-queries.ts`) and to detect statement kinds (`backends/rowbinary.ts`). These could use the lexer, or at least be tested against it.
- **Generating test cases.** Expected splits and token boundaries can come from the server's own lexer instead of being written by hand.

## Proposed rollout

An implementation is open as a stack of small draft PRs, each building on the one before it:

1. **Characterization tests** that pin the exact SQL `query()`, `command()` and `exec()` send today. No behavior change. (#1065)
2. **Move today's logic, unchanged,** behind an internal interface. (#1066)
3. **Internal lexer-based rewriter,** not used yet. The lexer is a dev dependency, and a lint rule blocks importing it from client source. (#1067)
4. **The `sql_lexer` option,** used by `command()` and `exec()`, with the load-failure fallback and a docs page. (#1068)
5. **`query()` uses it,** which fixes #973 when opted in. (#1069)
6. **FORMAT goes before a trailing SETTINGS clause,** which fixes #970 when opted in. (#1070)
7. **README, docs and troubleshooting-skill updates.** "Zero external dependencies" becomes "no runtime dependencies", with a pointer to the optional lexer. (#1071)
8. **Tests that compare the built-in handling with the official lexer.** These use a shared corpus of tricky queries, run as a fast unit test with no server and as a server-judged integration test. An explicit list of known differences fails both when a new difference appears and when a listed one disappears. The existing `select` and `exec()` tests also run in both modes. (#1072)

A future major version could make the lexer a regular dependency of the Node.js client and turn it on by default. That needs a `require()` of an ES module, so Node.js `^20.19 || >=22.12`. The Web client would keep the opt-in model because of the CSP and Workers limits above.

## Open questions

- Should the hand-written fixes (#1031, #972) be merged anyway, so users who don't opt in also get them? They don't conflict with this proposal.
- Is `sql_lexer` the right option name?
- Lexer releases follow ClickHouse `master`. Is a `^1.0.0` peer range right, or should the supported range be narrower?

title: test: fix two integration tests that are flaky on ClickHouse Cloud
body:
## Summary

Fixes two integration tests that fail intermittently on ClickHouse Cloud only. They showed up across the draft PRs #1065 to #1072, which only add tests and opt-in code. Both tests pass on local single-node and cluster runs.

**`node_max_open_connections` › "should use only one connection for insert"** (all Node versions, Cloud)
- The test created its table with the same client it uses for the inserts, which has `request_timeout: 3000`. In every failing attempt, the call that timed out was the `CREATE TABLE`, not an insert. On a busy Cloud service the DDL alone can take longer than 3 seconds.
- The table is now created with a default test client. The inserts still use `max_open_connections: 1` and `request_timeout: 3000`, so an insert that keeps holding the only socket still makes the next one time out, which is what the test checks.
- Removed the extra `setTimeout(() => { throw ... }, 3000)`. It repeated the request timeout, and throwing from a timer callback shows up as an uncaught error rather than a test failure.

**`web_abort_request` › "cancels a select query while reading response"** (Chromium and Firefox, Cloud)
- The test streamed `system.numbers LIMIT 100000` with `max_block_size: 1`. That's a small result produced slowly, and on Cloud the response is buffered, so the headers didn't arrive within the 60-second Cloud `request_timeout` (`Error: Timeout error.` from `WebConnection.request`).
- It now streams `SELECT number FROM system.numbers` with no limit and default block sizes, like the Node.js version of this test. The query can't finish before the abort, and the test still checks that reading the stream fails with an "aborted" error.

## Testing

- Both tests pass against a local single-node server: 3 runs each in Node.js, Chromium and Firefox.
- The Cloud behavior can only be checked by this PR's Cloud jobs. Note that the shared Cloud service was recently returning `TOO_MANY_TABLES` (code 724) under the load of many concurrent runs, so a failure with that error here would be environmental.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests only; no changelog entry needed.

title: ci: run Cloud tests after merge or on request, and clean up Cloud hourly
body:
## Summary

Runs the ClickHouse Cloud integration tests after a PR is merged, or on request, instead of on every push to every PR. Also runs them one job at a time. This follows what [clickhouse-go](https://github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/blob/main/.github/workflows/run-tests-cloud.yml) does against the same Cloud service.

### Why

The Cloud jobs use one ClickHouse Cloud service, which is shared with other client repositories (clickhouse-go uses the same `INTEGRATIONS_TEAM_TESTS_CLOUD_HOST_SMT_PROD` secret). On Cloud, every test file creates its own database, and `clean-up.yml` only drops databases older than 60 minutes.

Each push to a PR started six Cloud jobs at once. Pushing a stack of eight PRs (#1065 to #1072) twice within 15 minutes filled the service:

```
Too many databases. The limit (max_database_num_to_throw) is set to 2800,
the current number of databases is 2800. (code 725)
```

From then on, every Cloud job, including #1075's, failed during setup before running any tests. This likely affects the other repositories that use the same service too.

### What

- **New `tests-cloud.yml`** with the Node.js and Web Cloud jobs, which are removed from `tests-node.yml` and `tests-web.yml`. It runs:
  - after a merge (push to `main` or `release`, with the same path filters as before), on the daily schedule, and on `workflow_dispatch`;
  - on a PR only when a maintainer adds the **`tests:run-cloud`** label. A final job removes the label, so adding it again runs the tests again.
- **One Cloud job at a time across the repository:**
  - one workflow-level concurrency group, `tests-cloud`, with `cancel-in-progress: false`, so a whole run holds the lock and other runs wait. Of the waiting runs, only the newest is kept.
  - within a run, `max-parallel: 1` runs the matrix jobs one by one, and the Web jobs wait for the Node.js jobs.
  - runs whose jobs will be skipped, for example a PR that got a different label, get a group of their own (`tests-cloud-skipped-<run id>`), so they can't replace a waiting Cloud run.
- **`examples.yml` passes the Cloud credentials only after a merge and on manual runs.** On PRs they're empty, so the `create_table_cloud` example (Node.js and Web) skips itself, which it already did when the credentials were missing. Before this, each of the 4 examples jobs of every PR hit the Cloud service. With the lexer stack's PRs running at once, that example timed out in 28 jobs.
- **`clean-up.yml` runs hourly instead of on every push.** It used to run on every push to every branch, and a new push cancelled one still in progress. Dropping databases one by one takes a while, so a burst of pushes kept restarting it. It now runs at :17 every hour, which also puts a run before the 09:00 scheduled Cloud tests, and on demand (`workflow_dispatch`). Only one runs at a time, and a running cleanup is never cancelled.
- **Fork and Dependabot PRs are still skipped**, as before, because Cloud secrets aren't available to them. It uses `pull_request`, not `pull_request_target`, so a PR's code never runs with secrets unless it comes from a branch in this repository.
- **`npm ci` instead of `npm install`** in the new workflow, so dependencies are installed exactly as locked, verified by hash. This resolves the Scorecard Pinned-Dependencies alerts on these two steps. The other workflows still use `npm install`, so their existing alerts are unchanged.
- **`codecov.yml`:** `after_n_builds` goes from 7 to 5, the uploads every PR gets. With 7, Codecov never posted a status on fork PRs (for example #1041 and #1024), which skip the Cloud jobs, and with this change it wouldn't post on most PRs. The cloud flags are carried forward (`carryforward: true` was already set).

### Trade-offs

- **Cloud regressions show up after merge** (on `main`), unless the label is added before merging.
- **A Cloud run takes longer** with jobs one at a time: 4 Node.js versions and then 2 browsers. The first run from this branch took about 7 minutes (about a minute per job), against about 1–2 minutes when they all ran in parallel.
- **The `tests:run-cloud` label is new.** I've created it in the repository.

## Testing

- All workflow and Codecov YAML parses, and Prettier passes. `actionlint` wasn't available locally.
- The new workflow can only really be checked on GitHub: after merge (push to `main`), and by adding `tests:run-cloud` to a PR once the Cloud service has been cleaned up.

## Checklist

- [x] CI only; no changelog entry needed.

title: Send query() format as default_format instead of appending FORMAT to the SQL
body:
## Summary

Send the output format of `query()` to the server as the `default_format` setting, and send the user's SQL unchanged, instead of appending `FORMAT <format>` to it. This is how the Go, Rust and Java clients already work. A colleague suggested it while we were looking at a series of bugs caused by the client editing SQL text, and it removes the whole class of problems rather than fixing each case.

## Why

Today `query()` changes the user's SQL before sending it: it trims it, strips trailing semicolons, and appends `\nFORMAT <format>`. Every one of these reported problems comes from that appended clause:

- **A semicolon followed by a comment** (`SELECT 1; -- note`) fails with `Syntax error (Multi-statements are not allowed)`. Only a `;` at the very end is stripped, so the appended `FORMAT` becomes a second statement.
- **A trailing `SETTINGS` clause** gets `FORMAT` appended after it (`… SETTINGS max_threads = 1 FORMAT JSON`). Some older server versions reject that order.
- **The short `SHOW ROW POLICIES` syntax** fails, because the server parser doesn't accept a `FORMAT` suffix there.

The fixes proposed so far make the text editing smarter, with hand-written scanners or ClickHouse's own lexer compiled to WebAssembly. They work, but the client would still be guessing where `FORMAT` can safely go, so each new SQL shape is a new chance to get it wrong.

With `default_format`, there's nothing to guess: the server receives exactly the SQL the user wrote, and the format travels separately in the request URL.

## How the other ClickHouse clients handle it

| Client | Queries and commands | A user-written `INSERT … FORMAT` followed by data |
|---|---|---|
| **Go** (`clickhouse-go`, HTTP) | SQL sent as written; format sent as `default_format` | Normalizes the `INSERT` and strips a trailing `;`, because the data follows the statement |
| **Rust** (`clickhouse-rs`) | SQL sent as written; format sent as `default_format`. Its changelog describes switching to this "allowing queries to have trailing comments and/or semicolons" | Builds its own `INSERT INTO … FORMAT …` |
| **Java** (`client-v2`) | SQL sent as written; format passed through the query settings. Its docs say to specify the format in settings, not with a `FORMAT` clause | Builds its own `INSERT … FORMAT` |
| **Python** (`clickhouse-connect`) | Strips trailing semicolons from non-insert queries | Leaves inserts unchanged |

Go, Rust and Java agree: don't modify the SQL of a query or command, and only strip a trailing `;` when the client sends data right after the user's statement.

## Proposed behavior

| Method | Today | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| `query()` | trims, strips trailing `;`, appends `\nFORMAT <format>` | SQL sent as written; `format` (default `JSON`) sent as `default_format` |
| `command()` | trims and strips trailing `;` | SQL sent as written |
| `exec()` without `values` | trims and strips trailing `;` | SQL sent as written |
| `exec()` with `values` | trims and strips trailing `;` | **unchanged**: still strips a trailing `;` |
| `insert()` | builds `INSERT INTO … FORMAT …` | unchanged |

Why `exec()` with `values` keeps the stripping: the SQL goes in the URL, the data goes in the request body, and the server reads the data straight after the statement. It rejects a `;` there with `You have excessive ';' symbol before data for INSERT`. This matches what the Go client does on its insert path.

## Observable changes

This changes behavior that users can see, so I'd treat it as a feature in a minor release rather than a bug fix:

- **The query text** recorded in `system.query_log`, in logs and in traces no longer ends with `FORMAT <format>`.
- **A `FORMAT` clause in the query** passed to `query()` used to cause a syntax error. Now the server uses it instead of `default_format`, and the client would parse the response in the wrong format. The docs will say not to include one, and to use `exec()` for full control over the SQL. This matches the other clients.
- **Precedence:** the `format` option overrides a `default_format` set in `clickhouse_settings`, since it's the format the result is parsed as.
- **Trailing semicolons** reach the server in `query()`, `command()` and `exec()` without `values`. The server accepts them, including `;;;` and a `;` followed by a comment.

## Verified locally

I have a working implementation locally (not pushed yet). Results against a local ClickHouse server, both as a single node and as a two-node cluster:

- **The three problems above all work,** in the Node.js and Web clients: a `;` before each comment style (`--`, `#`, `/* */`), a trailing `SETTINGS` clause, and the short `SHOW ROW POLICIES`. The same holds for a `;` inside a string literal and for queries sent with `use_multipart_params`.
- **New integration tests fail before the change and pass after it.** A guard test checks that `exec()` with `values` still strips the trailing `;`.
- **The existing unit and integration suites pass** for both clients. The only test changes are the expected SQL text (traces, `query_log`) and the number of URL parameters.

## Open questions

- Is a minor release right, or should this wait for, or be optional until, a major release because of the observable changes above?
- Should `query()` detect a `FORMAT` clause in the query, for example via the `X-ClickHouse-Format` response header, or behave exactly like the other clients and leave it to the server?
- Should `command()` and `exec()` keep trimming leading and trailing whitespace, purely for compatibility?

title: fix: raise a ClickHouseError for an in-band JSONEachRow exception row
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1053

With `http_write_exception_in_output_format` enabled (the server default before 25.11, e.g. 25.8 LTS), a query that fails after the response has started streaming is reported by one more row, `{"exception": "Code: ... DB::Exception: ..."}`, and the body then ends normally. `ResultSet.stream()` and `ResultSet.json()` returned that row as data and raised no error, so the failure was silently lost.

**How the row is detected.** The server writes this row with `JSONUtils::writeException`, which calls `writeTitle("exception", out, indent, " ")`, so there is a space after the colon. Data rows of `JSONEachRow` / `JSONStringsEachRow` are written with no space after the colon. I checked this in the 24.8, 25.3, 25.8 and master sources and on real 25.8.33.6 and 26.11.1.578 servers. So the check is:

1. the format is `JSONEachRow` or `JSONStringsEachRow`;
2. the row starts with `{"exception": "` and ends with `"}`. This is a cheap string check, and only rows that pass it are parsed;
3. the row parses to an object whose only key is `exception`, with a string value.

A matching row fails the stream with `parseError(message)`, which gives a `ClickHouseError` with `code` and `type`. A genuine column named `exception` (`SELECT '...' AS exception`) is written as `{"exception":"..."}` and is still returned as data. This holds even when the value looks like a server error. The issue's "only the last row" / "key set differs from the first row" ideas aren't needed, so nothing is buffered and a body that contains only the error row is still detected.

The logic is shared in `client-common/src/utils/stream.ts` (`extractInBandExceptionFromRow`, `canHaveInBandExceptionRow`). It is called from the row-splitting loop of both the Node.js and Web `ResultSet.stream()`, next to the existing `__exception__` trailer check. No public API changes.

**Out of scope, unchanged:**
- `JSONCompact*EachRow*`: the server writes the error as `["<message>"]`, which can't be told apart from a single `String` column row, so there is no safe rule.
- `JSONEachRowWithProgress`: it already exposes `{"exception":...}` to callers on purpose (`isException`).
- `text()`: it returns the raw body, as before.

## How it was tested

- Unit (no server): new tests in `stream_utils.test.ts`, `node_result_set.test.ts` and `web_result_set.test.ts`.
  - Positive: an error row in its own chunk or sharing a chunk with data rows, through `stream()` and `json()`, and with `JSONStringsEachRow`.
  - Negative: a genuine `exception` column (including one whose value looks like a server error), `exception` together with other columns, malformed rows, and `JSONEachRowWithProgress` unchanged.
  - Results: `npm run test:node:unit`: 413 passed, 10 skipped. `npm run test:web:unit`: 265 passed. Without the `result_set.ts` changes, 4 Node and 2 Web tests fail.
- Integration: new cases in `node_stream_error_handling.test.ts` / `web_stream_error_handling.test.ts` with `http_write_exception_in_output_format: true`, plus a real `exception` column case. They pass against ClickHouse 25.8.33.6 and head (26.11.1.578), and the existing tagged-trailer tests still pass on head.
- Full integration suites against head: the only failure is `query_log.test.ts > ... with exec`. It fails the same way on unmodified `main` when the full suite runs and passes on its own, so it's a timing flake unrelated to this change.
- `typecheck` and `lint` pass for client-common, client-node and client-web. Prettier was applied.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit and integration tests covering the common scenarios were added
- [x] A human-readable changelog entry was added to every affected package's `CHANGELOG.md` (`client-node` and `client-web`; the `[#TBD]` link will be updated with this PR's number)
