title: fix: format pre-1970 Date query params as valid negative timestamps
body:
## Summary

A `Date` query parameter before the Unix epoch is sent as a malformed timestamp:

| `Date` | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `new Date(-1000)` | `00000000-1` | `-1` |
| `new Date(-500)` | `00000000-1.500` | `-0.500` |
| `new Date(-1500)` | `00000000-2.500` | `-1.500` |
| `new Date(-1)` | `00000000-1.999` | `-0.001` |
| 1969-12-31T00:00:00Z | `0000-86400` | `-86400` |

There are two causes in `formatQueryParamsInternal`:
- `Math.floor(ms / 1000).toString().padStart(10, "0")` puts the padding zeros in front of the minus sign.
- Flooring a negative time and then appending the (always positive) `getUTCMilliseconds()` moves the value by up to 2 seconds (`-1.5 s` becomes `-2.500`).

The fix formats the absolute time and prefixes `-` for negative values. For dates from 1970 on the output is byte-for-byte the same as before: I compared old and new output for 200k random non-negative timestamps. Dates inside arrays/tuples/maps take the ISO-string branch and are not affected.

This doesn't overlap with #968 (which adds date strings for `Date`/`Date32` columns). DateTime/DateTime64 still use this numeric path, but both PRs edit the same few lines, so whichever lands second will need a small rebase.

I haven't run this against a live server. The new output is a plain signed decimal Unix timestamp, which is what DateTime64 needs for pre-1970 values.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit tests covering the common scenarios were added (`formats a date before the Unix epoch as a negative timestamp`: fails before the change with `"00000000-1"`, passes after; `format_query_params.test.ts` 31 passed)
- [x] A human-readable changelog entry was added to every affected package's `CHANGELOG.md` (`client-node` and `client-web`)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow bug fix in shared query-param formatting with new unit tests; only changes wire format for pre-1970 scalar `Date` params (correcting invalid values).
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **scalar** `Date` query parameter serialization in `formatQueryParams` so times before the Unix epoch are sent as proper signed Unix timestamps (e.g. `new Date(-1500)` → `-1.500` instead of malformed strings like `00000000-2.500`).
> 
> The formatter now derives seconds and milliseconds from the **absolute** millisecond value and applies a leading `-` when needed, avoiding zero-padding before the minus sign and the up-to-2s error from combining `Math.floor` on negative times with positive `getUTCMilliseconds()`. **Post-1970** scalar output is unchanged (still 10-digit padded seconds when applicable). Dates inside arrays/tuples/maps still use quoted ISO date strings.
> 
> Adds unit coverage for pre-epoch cases and changelog notes in `@clickhouse/client` and `@clickhouse/client-web`.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit b49279f42789309aa8abdd71a64a1325ecb7b250. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: fix: raise a ClickHouseError for an in-band JSONEachRow exception row
body:
Closes #1053. Supersedes #1083 by @AmineBenzaazaa (CLA not signed), with the review changes.

## Summary

With `http_write_exception_in_output_format` enabled (the default before 25.11, for example 25.8 LTS), a query that fails mid-stream ends with the row `{"exception": "..."}` and HTTP 200. `stream()` and `json()` returned this row as data and gave no error.

The client now fails the stream with a `ClickHouseError` for this row, for `JSONEachRow` and `JSONStringsEachRow`. The server writes the error row with a space after the colon. Data rows have no space, so a column named `exception` stays data.

On Node.js, rows that the caller has not read are dropped when the stream fails. The `__exception__` path has the same behavior. #1167 tracks this.

Not changed: `JSONCompact*EachRow*`, `JSONEachRowWithProgress`, `text()`, and the `JSON` format.

## Changes from #1083

- The Web integration test sets `enable_http_compression: 0`. Without it, the server answers the browser with HTTP 500, and the test passed without the fix.
- The changelog entries are under the unreleased headings.

## Tests

- `curl` on 24.8.14 and 26.11.1: the error row has the space, data rows do not.
- Unit: Node.js 458 passed, Web 286 passed. Without the fix, 4 Node.js and 2 Web tests fail.
- Integration on head and 24.8: the new tests pass. Without the fix, they fail on head.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes streaming error detection for common JSON row formats; apps that treated `{"exception":...}` as data will now get thrown errors, which is intended but behavior-changing.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Streaming JSON result sets now surface mid-query server failures as errors** instead of silent partial success when ClickHouse writes an in-band exception row (`http_write_exception_in_output_format`, default on before 25.11).
> 
> New shared helpers `canHaveInBandExceptionRow` and `extractInBandExceptionFromRow` detect the server’s `{"exception": "<message>"}` row (space after the colon) and turn it into a `ClickHouseError`. **Node and Web `ResultSet.stream()`** call this while splitting chunks; the stream or `json()` rejects with that error and never exposes the exception row as data. Only **`JSONEachRow`** and **`JSONStringsEachRow`** get this behavior; genuine columns named `exception` stay data because the server omits the space after the colon for normal rows.
> 
> Changelogs and unit/integration tests (fixtures, ResultSet tests, stream error handling) document and lock in the fix ([#1053]).
>

title: ResultSet.stream(): Node.js drops unread rows on a mid-stream error, and an error row without a final newline is not detected
body:
### Summary

Two gaps remain in the mid-stream error handling of `ResultSet.stream()` after #1166 and #975. Both apply to the in-band `{"exception": "..."}` row (#1053, #1166) and to the tagged `__exception__` block of ClickHouse 25.11+ (#975).

### 1. Node.js: rows that the caller has not read are dropped when the stream fails

When the client finds a mid-stream error, it pushes the rows before the error and then fails the `Transform` with `callback(err)`. Node.js then destroys the stream, and a destroyed stream discards the batches in its buffer. The caller gets the error, but not the rows that came before it.

Reproduction against the built `@clickhouse/client` (`ResultSet.instance` with a `JSONEachRow` body of two rows and one in-band error row, read with `for await`):

| Body | Rows delivered | Error |
|---|---|---|
| 2 rows + error row in one chunk | 0 | `ClickHouseError` 395 |
| 2 rows, then the error row as a separate chunk | 0 | `ClickHouseError` 395 |
| 2 rows, then the error row 20 ms later | 2 | `ClickHouseError` 395 |

On `main`, the tagged `__exception__` path does not push the rows of the current chunk at all. #975 pushes them, but it fails the stream in the same way, so the result is the same.

The Web client delivers the rows. With a fast reader and with a slow reader (20 ms for each read), it delivered 2 of 2 rows in all layouts.

Expected: the caller reads all complete rows before the error, then the stream fails with the server error. This must work for `for await`, `'data'` listeners, and `'readable'` + `read()`. `json()` must still reject.

Fix direction: when rows are still in the buffer, keep the error and ignore the rest of the body. Fail the stream when the consumer has read the buffer (for example, when `read()` returns `null` and `readableLength` is `0`). Do not end the readable side from `flush` while an error is pending. Use the same helper for both error paths.

### 2. Both clients: an error row with no newline at the end of the body is not detected

The client checks a line only when a newline terminates it. At the end of the stream, the bytes after the last newline are dropped. #975 adds `flush` handlers that keep this behavior. If the body ends with `{"exception": "..."}` and no newline, `stream()` and `json()` complete without an error, and the result is incomplete.

ClickHouse 24.8.14 and 26.11.1 always write the newline after the error row, so we did not see this with a real server. This is a defensive fix.

Fix direction: in `flush`, for `JSONEachRow` and `JSONStringsEachRow`, give the remaining bytes to `extractInBandExceptionFromRow`, and fail the stream if it returns an error. Add unit tests for an error-only body and for data rows plus an error row, both with no final newline.

### Order

Do this after #1166 and #975 are merged. Both PRs change the same transform code in `packages/client-node/src/result_set.ts` and `packages/client-web/src/result_set.ts`.

Found during the review of #1166.

title: fix: reject in-band JSONEachRow error rows
body:
Fixes #1053.

Thanks to @AmineBenzaazaa for the original investigation and proposed fix in #1083. That PR could not be merged because the CLA was not signed. This PR replaces it with a new implementation.

When a query fails after the response body starts, ClickHouse can append an error envelope if `http_write_exception_in_output_format` is enabled. Both clients previously returned that envelope as data. `ResultSet.stream()` and `ResultSet.json()` now fail with the server error for `JSONEachRow` and `JSONStringsEachRow`.

The internal decoder matches the error envelope and captures its message as an encoded JSON string. It decodes only that string and passes the result to the existing error parser. Recognized messages produce a `ClickHouseError` with the server code and message. Other messages still cause the result to fail.

ClickHouse puts a space after the colon in an error envelope and omits it in normal data rows. The decoder uses that distinction without tracking the first row or parsing ordinary data. A real column named `exception` stays as data, even when its value looks like an error. A later server error is detected even when `exception` is the only result column. The configured data parser stays lazy, and no public exports are added.

The Node.js error path yields before reporting the error so an active consumer can receive preceding rows. Stream destruction can still discard rows buffered for a slow consumer, as with tagged errors. Compact JSON row formats remain outside this change because their error rows have no equivalent distinction. The embedded documentation explains this limit and tagged error blocks on ClickHouse 25.11 and later.

## Validation

- Full unit suites passed: Node.js 523 tests, with 7 skipped; Web 342 tests in headless Chromium.
- Regression tests cover a real `exception` column followed by a server error, split chunks, UTF-8, escaped strings, line separators, large messages, malformed envelopes, unrecognized server messages, and lazy custom parsers.
- Rebuilt-package integration tests passed against local ClickHouse 26.11: 12 tests per client cover both formats, both consumption methods, both result schemas, and genuine error-like column values. Existing Node.js tagged error tests also passed.
- A benchmark of 200,000 rows of about 1.3 KB took 56 ms with `exception` as the first column and 55 ms as the second column (median of five runs, rebuilt Node.js package).
- Workspace build, type checks, lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit and integration tests covering the common scenarios were added
- [x] A human-readable changelog entry was added to every affected package's `CHANGELOG.md`

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes query result parsing and error surfacing for two common formats; behavior shifts when servers emit in-band exception rows, though ambiguity around an `exception` column is documented.
> 
> **Overview**
> When `http_write_exception_in_output_format` is enabled, ClickHouse can append an `{"exception": "..."}` row after partial data. **`ResultSet.stream()`** and **`ResultSet.json()`** (via streaming) for **`JSONEachRow`** and **`JSONStringsEachRow`** now recognize that row and throw a **`ClickHouseError`** with the parsed server code and message instead of returning it as data.
> 
> The logic lives in **`createJSONEachRowErrorDetector`** in `client-common` and is applied in both Node and Web result-set stream transformers. It uses a lightweight string scan so normal rows stay lazy; results whose only column is **`exception`** are still treated as data, and compact JSON formats are unchanged.
> 
> Docs and changelogs describe the ambiguity and recommend **`http_write_exception_in_output_format: false`** on ClickHouse 25.11+ for tagged error blocks. Integration and unit tests cover split chunks, UTF-8, escaped payloads, real `exception` columns, and custom JSON parsers.
>

title: test(upstream-sql-tests): use the shared harness design, fix shim gaps, run all passing tests
body:
## Summary

The upstream SQL test harness ran 2,945 of the about 12,900 `.sql` tests of `tests/queries/0_stateless`. The harnesses of clickhouse-cs, clickhouse-connect and clickhouse-cpp run about 10,000 each and share one design. This PR changes our harness to that design, fixes the shim gaps that the sweep showed, adds a `json` backend that reads rows through `query()` and `ResultSet.json()`, and makes the allowlists from a full sweep. Only test code changes.

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| passthrough: tests that run | 2,945 | **10,791** |
| rowbinary: tests that run | 2,189 | **10,260** |
| json: tests that run | – | **10,087** |
| Known failures (kept in the lists, in groups by cause) | 0 | 147 passthrough, 531 rowbinary, 704 json |

## Changes

**Harness design** (as in the other harnesses)

- `clickhouse-version` (26.10.4.207) pins the server and the upstream tests together. `scripts/fetch-upstream.sh` checks out the matching release tag. `run-upstream-tests.sh` stops on a version mismatch.
- CI starts the stock server image of the pinned version, not `docker-compose.yml`. The `clickhouse_version` input of a manual run replaces `upstream_ref`.
- No random settings. Each allowlist name selects exactly one test. `.sh` tests are not selected.
- A test that fails because of a client bug or a shim gap stays in the allowlist as `# <test>  # [<id>]`, in a group with a header that gives the cause. `KNOWN_FAILURES=<id>` runs a group. A test that cannot pass through any client is not listed.
- `scripts/run-with-real-client.sh` runs tests through the real `clickhouse-client`, to find environment causes.

**Shim** (it now copies `clickhouse-client` more exactly)

- Statements are split as `clickhouse-client` does (a port of the clickhouse-connect splitter): each statement keeps its `;` and its same-line comment, and inline `INSERT` data ends at an empty line.
- Test hints come from that comment, also after the last statement. `-- { echo }` is supported.
- An error hint is compared by code (`src/error-codes.ts`, generated from `ErrorCodes.cpp`). The shim also checks that `ClickHouseError.type` is the name of the code, so a wrong type stays a visible client failure.
- `--param_<name>` becomes a query parameter. `USE` changes the database of the next statements. A `SET` replaces the command-line setting of the same name.
- rowbinary backend: the format goes as `default_format`, so the query text does not change. The TSV writer escapes `'`, `\b` and `\f` at the top level, writes DateTime in the time zone of the column or the session, and writes Geometry and Nested.

**json backend** (new)

- Each statement that returns rows and has no `FORMAT` clause goes through `client.query({ format: 'JSONCompactEachRowWithNamesAndTypes' })` and `ResultSet.json()`, the read path that most users use. The shim writes the values as TSV again (`src/json-serialize.ts`), so the `.reference` diff applies.
- `json-allowlist.txt` is a subset of the passthrough list. CI runs it as a third matrix backend.
- The FORMAT check now also sees a quoted name (``FORMAT `Null` ``), for all backends.

## Known-failure groups

Client bugs, with a reproduction in the group header:

- `[error-type-from-message]` (101): `parseError` takes the first `(UPPERCASE)` word of the message as the error type and cuts the message there. Example: `SELECT tupleElement(1, 'a')` gives `type: 'JSON'`.
- `[error-without-type]` (7): an error with a code but no `(TYPE)` (Poco, std exceptions) is a plain `Error` without a code.
- `[rowbinary-value-without-type]` (208, #910): `@clickhouse/rowbinary` gives Dynamic, Variant and JSON values without their type.
- `[rowbinary-unsupported-types]` (126): `Tuple()`, typed `JSON(...)`, `SimpleAggregateFunction`, `AggregateFunction`.
- `[rowbinary-geometry-discriminant]` (2): `readGeometry` throws for a discriminant that it does not know.

Client findings of the json backend, each reproduced with the public API only:

- `[json-number-precision]` (284): `ResultSet.json()` rounds 64-bit integers and Decimals with no error. `18446744073709551615::UInt64` gives `18446744073709552000`.
- `[json-nan-inf-null]` (142): `nan` and `inf` become `null`, the same as NULL.
- `[json-invalid-utf8]` (11): bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD.
- `[json-map-as-object]` (10): a Map is a JS object, so integer-like keys move to the front and duplicate keys are lost (related: #996).
- `[datatype-parser-unsupported-types]` (104): `@clickhouse/datatype-parser` cannot parse typed `JSON(...)`, `SimpleAggregateFunction` and `AggregateFunction`.

Shim gaps: KQL splitting (13), DateTime text edge cases (28), `WITH TOTALS`/`extremes` in RowBinary (109), the query cache key and `default_format` (2 rowbinary, 3 json). json only: `WITH TOTALS`/`extremes` (121), Dynamic and Variant values without a type in JSON (25), TSV output settings (4). Untriaged: 26 passthrough, 56 rowbinary.

Not listed: 27 tests that drop the current database of the session. Over HTTP, each later request names that database. Also not listed: `05166_external_distinct_ratio_rounding`, which sets `max_memory_usage_for_user` to 512 MiB; that limit applies to the tests that run at the same time.

## How the lists were made

All 12,961 `.sql`/`.sql.j2` tests ran on a fresh 26.10.4.207 server (`--no-long`). Each failure also ran through the real `clickhouse-client`, and a test that failed there too is an environment cause. Trial fixes of the shim and the client confirmed the groups; the client fixes were reverted. The final lists ran on a fresh server at `-j 12` (CI uses `-j 4`). The json list passed 10,088 / 10,088 there (before the removal below). One passthrough test, `05257_aggregation_single_level_result_fanout`, failed there under load; it passed 13 / 13 times alone.

Not covered: the 424 long tests and 17 tests that the runner skips on macOS.

- [x] A Codex review of the first commit; its 3 findings are fixed.

title: fix: avoid mutating caller param_entries array in toSearchParams
body:
## Summary

`toSearchParams` previously assigned `const entries = param_entries` and pushed `['query_id', query_id]` directly into the caller-supplied array when `param_entries` was provided. Copying into a new array `[...param_entries, ['query_id', query_id]]` prevents mutating caller arrays across repeated calls.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit tests covering the scenario were added in `packages/client-common/__tests__/unit/to_search_params.test.ts` (`npx vitest run packages/client-common/__tests__/unit/to_search_params.test.ts --config=packages/client-node/vitest.config.ts`: 9 passed; full `packages/client-node` unit suite: 49 files passed, 524 passed, 7 skipped; `npm run build && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run prettier:check` passed)
- [x] A human-readable changelog entry was added to `packages/client-node/CHANGELOG.md` and `packages/client-web/CHANGELOG.md`

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Small behavioral fix in shared URL helper; avoids accidental cross-request leakage of query_id into reused param arrays.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **`toSearchParams()`** so a reused **`param_entries`** array is not modified when **`query_id`** is added. The branch that takes pre-serialized params now builds **`[...param_entries, ['query_id', query_id]]`** instead of pushing onto the caller’s array.

v1.65.1

  • Chromium 159.0.8154.6
  • Mozilla Firefox 159.0

v1.65.0

🥟 Run tests with Bun

The test runner now runs under Bun. Bun transpiles your TypeScript test files itself, so Playwright does not use Babel or its compilation cache. Pass the --bun flag, because without it bunx playwright test runs on Node.js:

bunx --bun playwright test

Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux. Some features work differently under Bun:

  • There is no watch mode. UI mode does not run tests again when files change, and --only-changed does not follow imports.
  • Bun loads modules itself, so --tsconfig and the JSX options in tsconfig.json have no effect, and custom ESM loaders are not supported.
  • Stack traces do not include async frames, and API names do not include the class name: click instead of locator.click. This changes some step locations, step titles and error messages.
  • Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

🚨 Reports with only failures

New failures reporter prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.

New onlyFailures option of the HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters keeps only tests with unexpected outcomes, flaky tests and interrupted tests:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
reporter: [
['failures'],
['html', { onlyFailures: true }],
],
});

Updates `undici` from 8.12.3 to 8.12.4
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v8.12.4

⚠️ Security Fixes

This release fixes six vulnerabilities.

CVE-2026-116592 / GHSA-mqg3-3v4r-cm32 (high)

Undici 8.12.2 and 8.12.3 could cache the final response from a redirect chain under the original request key without applying the origin, cache policy, freshness, or Vary requirements of every intermediate hop. This could poison a cache or expose one user's response to another user. The fix validates every redirect hop, combines their Vary fields, limits freshness and stale serving to the most restrictive hop, and invalidates persistent SQLite entries written by vulnerable releases.

CVE-2026-120474 / GHSA-7xg3-fphp-28hg (medium)

A shared cache used with compose(redirect(), cache()) could store a credential-dependent response from a same-origin redirect under the original URL. A later authenticated or unauthenticated request could then receive another user's response. Redirected requests carrying Authorization, Cookie, or Proxy-Authorization are no longer stored under the original alias key.

CVE-2026-116630 / GHSA-5rm8-gv32-r954 (medium)

A cross-origin redirect during cache revalidation could let a 304 Not Modified response from the redirect target validate a cached response from the original origin. Undici now checks that the revalidation target matches the cached URL and that any returned validator matches the stored representation before replaying the cached body.

CVE-2026-120415 / GHSA-9v6h-8rgp-m69f (medium)

The redirect interceptor did not strip credentials correctly when request headers were supplied as an array of [name, value] pairs. With a header-normalizing interceptor outside redirect(), credentials could be sent to a cross-origin redirect target. Undici now handles both tuple arrays and flat header arrays when removing sensitive headers.

CVE-2026-120222 / GHSA-3g9m-rv3r-w5w2 (medium)

A downstream handler exception during cache replay could escape as an uncaught exception or unhandled promise rejection and terminate the process. title: ClickHouseError.type is wrong when the message has an (UPPERCASE) group before the type
fix: give ClickHouseError.type from the end of the server error
body:
Closes #1173

## Summary

`parseError` took the first `(UPPERCASE)` group in a server message as `ClickHouseError.type` and cut the message there. Groups such as `Nullable(JSON)`, `failed at position 38 (TABLE)` or `(NULL)` then gave a wrong type (`JSON`, `TABLE`, `NULL`). This bug came with #819.

The parser now takes the type at the end of an exception:
- before ` (version ...)`;
- or at the end of the text (the server leaves out the version for a request with a `session_id`);
- the text from `, Stack trace (` is ignored (`stacktrace` setting).

For a wrapped error (`CANNOT_EXTRACT_TABLE_STRUCTURE` around `INCORRECT_DATA`), the type is the outer one, which matches `code`. The message is the innermost one, as before (#819). A text with no type at the end of an exception keeps the old rule.

The parser is a linear scan, not a regex: a regex that requires the suffix backtracks badly on a large text without one (found in review).

## Tests

- Unit tests with server texts of 26.10.4.207: the three kinds of groups, no version, stack trace, wrapped error, a 940 KB input with a time limit, and a body that is not a server error.
- Upstream SQL harness: the 101 tests of `[error-type-from-message]` pass. 93 of them also pass with rowbinary and 97 with json. The other 12 go to the groups of their causes, with a new group `[rowbinary-invalid-utf8]`.
- A local fuzz run (not committed): 250,000 generated server errors parsed exactly, 250,000 random or mutated texts with no throw, linear time.

Changelog: `@clickhouse/client` and `@clickhouse/client-web` (shared code).

title: parseError: ClickHouseError takes its code from a data row in a compressed HTTP 500 response
body:
<!-- delete unnecessary items -->

### Describe the bug

When a query fails during execution and the response is compressed, the server answers `HTTP 500` with the rows that it already produced, followed by the exception text. If a row before the exception contains text such as `Code: <N>` or `Error: <N>`, `client.query()` rejects with a `ClickHouseError` whose `code` comes from that row. For a JSONEachRow column named `exception` (or JSONCompactEachRow with one String column), `code`, `type` and `message` all come from the row.

Values of this form are normal, for example in `SELECT exception FROM system.query_log`.

Affected:
- `@clickhouse/client` with `compression: { response: ... }`: gzip, zstd and br; formats JSONEachRow, JSONCompactEachRow, JSON, TabSeparated and CSV.
- `@clickhouse/client-web` with every compression setting: `fetch` sends `Accept-Encoding`, and the server compresses by default (`enable_http_compression` is 1 on 26.10). Tested with the Node.js `fetch`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the program below. Each query fails with `throwIf` after the server produced some rows.
2. Compare the `code` of each error with the server's `X-ClickHouse-Exception-Code`.

### Expected behaviour

The server reports code 395, in the header and as the last text of the body (decompressed, `curl -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip'`):

```
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
X-ClickHouse-Exception-Code: 395
Content-Encoding: gzip

{"exception":"Code: 60. DB::Exception: Unknown table x. (UNKNOWN_TABLE) (version 1)","number":0}
...
{"exception":"Code: 60. DB::Exception: Unknown table x. (UNKNOWN_TABLE) (version 1)","number":3}
Code: 395. DB::Exception: boom: while executing 'FUNCTION throwIf(...)'. (FUNCTION_THROW_IF_VALUE_IS_NON_ZERO) (version 26.10.4.207 (official build))
```

All three queries must reject with code `395`, type `FUNCTION_THROW_IF_VALUE_IS_NON_ZERO` and the message `boom: ...`.

### Code example

```js
import { createClient } from '@clickhouse/client'

const client = createClient({ url: 'http://localhost:8123', compression: { response: true } })
const tail = `FROM numbers(10) WHERE throwIf(number = 5, 'boom') = 0 SETTINGS max_block_size = 1`
const cases = [
  ['JSONEachRow', `SELECT 'Code: 60. DB::Exception: Unknown table x. (UNKNOWN_TABLE) (version 1)' AS exception, number ${tail}`],
  ['TabSeparated', `SELECT 'Error: 404 from upstream' AS msg, number ${tail}`],
  ['JSONEachRow', `SELECT 'hello' AS msg, number ${tail}`], // contrast
]
for (const [format, query] of cases) {
  try { await (await client.query({ query, format })).text() }
  catch (e) { console.log(format, e.code, e.type, JSON.stringify(e.message.slice(0, 30))) }
}
await client.close()
```

### Error log

```
JSONEachRow 60 UNKNOWN_TABLE "Unknown table x. "
TabSeparated 404 FUNCTION_THROW_IF_VALUE_IS_NON_ZERO "boom: while executing 'FUNCTIO"
JSONEachRow 395 FUNCTION_THROW_IF_VALUE_IS_NON_ZERO "boom: while executing 'FUNCTIO"
```

Only the contrast case (no such text in the rows) is correct.

### Root cause

`parseError` (`packages/client-common/src/error/error.ts:103`) tries the `exception` string of every JSON row first (`jsonExceptionCandidates`, line 53), so a data row wins over the real exception. For the plain text, `errorRe` (line 15) is not anchored and takes the code from the first `Code: <N>` or `Error: <N>` in the body. The real exception is the last text of the body; the client uses the `X-ClickHouse-Exception-Code` header only to detect the failure.

The fix is in `parseError`: take the exception from the end of the body. Polyglot AI can open a fix PR if a maintainer assigns this issue to `@polyglotAI-bot`.

Related: #1174 (open) changes the same parser; with it, these cases give the same codes.

### Configuration

#### Environment

- Client version: `@clickhouse/client` 1.25.0 (`main` f28f2f3); `@clickhouse/client-web` on the same commit
- Language version: Node.js 22.23.5
- OS: Linux (Docker)

#### ClickHouse server

- ClickHouse Server version: 26.10.4.207
- ClickHouse Server non-default settings, if any: none

<!-- polyglot-issue-classes v1 -->
**Classification:** impact: none · area: API & diagnostics (error parsing)

title: Mid-stream error with a long message: plain Error with no code when the server cuts the message to 16 KiB
body:
### Describe the bug

When a query fails after the server started to stream the result, ClickHouse (25.11+) writes the error in an exception block. The whole block is at most 16 KiB, so the server cuts a long message. The cut message has the `Code: <n>` prefix, but no `(TYPE)` and no ` (version ...)` at the end.

`parseError` needs a `(TYPE)` group. For the cut message, the client throws a plain `Error`, not a `ClickHouseError`, and `code` is `undefined`, although the text starts with `Code: 395.`. The HTTP status and the `X-ClickHouse-Exception-Code` header cannot help here: the server sent them (200, no code) before the error.

Affects `@clickhouse/client` and `@clickhouse/client-web` (shared `parseError`).

Note: on `main`, the same query fails earlier with `there was an error in the stream; failed to parse the message length`. That is #1084, which #975 fixes. With #975, the result is the plain `Error` below.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a server of 25.11 or later.
2. Run the code example, with the code of #975 (or `main` after #975 merges).

### Expected behaviour

A `ClickHouseError` with `code: '395'` and the cut message. `type` can stay `undefined` when the text does not have it.

### Code example

```ts
import { createClient } from "@clickhouse/client";
const client = createClient();

for (const len of [1000, 16000]) {
  const rs = await client.query({
    query: `SELECT number, throwIf(number = 10, repeat('x', ${len})) FROM system.numbers LIMIT 100`,
    format: "JSONEachRow",
    clickhouse_settings: { max_block_size: "1" },
  });
  try {
    for await (const _ of rs.stream()) {
    }
  } catch (e) {
    console.log(len, e.constructor.name, e.code, e.type);
  }
}
```

### Error log

```
1000 ClickHouseError 395 FUNCTION_THROW_IF_VALUE_IS_NON_ZERO
16000 Error undefined undefined
```

The end of the raw block for `len = 16000` (16,382 bytes):

```
... 'S... UInt8 : 3'. (FUNCTIO\n16308 <tag>\r\n__exception__\r\n
```

The same message before the first row (an HTTP 500 response, no 16 KiB limit) gives a `ClickHouseError` with code 395.

### Notes

- Same cause as the upstream SQL harness group `[error-without-type]` (`tests/clickhouse-test-runner/upstream-allowlist.txt`): a server error without `(TYPE)` is not a `ClickHouseError`.
- Found with a fuzz test of #975 on real server bodies.

### Configuration

#### Environment

- Client version: `main` at 67ef113 (1.25.0 + unreleased), and #975 at f6eae78
- Language version: Node.js 22.23.5
- OS: macOS

#### ClickHouse server

- ClickHouse Server version: 26.11.1.312
- ClickHouse Server non-default settings, if any: none

title: fix: give a ClickHouseError for a server error without a (TYPE) group
body:
Fixes #1179

## Summary

The server cuts a mid-stream exception block to 16 KiB. A long message then has the `Code: <n>` prefix but no `(TYPE)` group, and `parseServerError` returned `undefined` when it found no group. `parseError` then gave a plain `Error` with no `code`.

Now, a text without a group that starts with `Code: <n>. DB::...Exception: ` gives a `ClickHouseError` with the `code`, `type: undefined`, and the rest of the text as the message. The match on the start of the text keeps other texts (for example, a proxy error page) as a plain `Error`.

Limit: if the cut message has an `(UPPERCASE)` group of its own, the client still takes it as the type, as before. This change does not touch that path.

Both clients use this parser, so the changelogs of `client-node` and `client-web` have an entry.

Tests: two unit tests in `error.test.ts`. The test for the cut message fails without the fix. The Node.js unit suite and `tsc --noEmit` pass. The reproduction from the issue was not run against a live server.

## Checklist

- [x] Unit and integration tests covering the common scenarios were added (unit tests)
- [x] A human-readable changelog entry was added to every affected package's `CHANGELOG.md`

This change was prepared with the help of an AI coding assistant.

title: fix: parse server errors whose message looks like a server marker; trim ClickHouseError.message
body:
Follow-up to #1174 (review feedback after the merge), refs #1173. It ships in the same release as #1174.

- `ClickHouseError.message` no longer ends with the whitespace before ` (TYPE)` (`Table x already exists. ` → `Table x already exists.`). Code that compares the exact text must change (Migration Notes). `code` and `type` do not change.
- `parseServerError` makes one pass over the type groups instead of two. The results are the same.
- The parser now also gives the right `type` and the full `message` when the user's text in the message looks like a server marker, for example from `throwIf`:
  - `see (FOO_BAR) (version 1) here` cut the message at the user's group. An end of an exception now needs the server's version format: ` (version ` and four numbers (`26.11.1.312`).
  - With `stacktrace=1`, `x (ABC), Stack trace (y)` gave `type` `ABC` and a cut message, and some texts gave a plain `Error` with no code. The parser now cuts only at the server's full sentence `, Stack trace (when copying this message, always include the lines below):`, after a group that can be a type, and only when no end of an exception follows it (the server adds no stack trace when the message has `Stack trace` text).
- The parser tests use double quotes where no interpolation is needed.

| Fix | Unit test (fails on the old code) | Integration test (real server) |
|---|---|---|
| a user `(TYPE) (version …)` | 3 tests (version, `session_id`, `(version 1.2)`) | 3 tests (fail on the old code) |
| a user `, Stack trace (` text | 6 tests | 2 tests with `stacktrace=1` (fail on the old code) |
| a real stack trace stays out of `message` | existing tests | 1 new test with `stacktrace=1` |
| the whitespace trim | 1 guard test (passes on the old code too) | none: the server always writes one space |

Fuzz (old parser vs new, and texts with the markers in the user text, with the `throwIf` echo): 3M cases, 0 failures. 4 of 6 mutants of the fix are caught. The other 2 are equivalent: the check for a later end of an exception already covers them.

Upstream SQL tests (26.10.4.207, both backends, full run): no regression. 3 tests fail also when run alone, for server reasons on a long-running server (a permission error in `01601_detach_permanently`, `text_log` in `02813_starting_in_text_log`, a merge counter in `03221_merge_profile_events`). The known-failure groups that can be affected (`error-without-type`, `untriaged`) still fail.

Review (a checklist subagent, `code-review`, Codex, the docs reviewer): no must-fix. The two remaining cases that it found are fixed, and its stack trace test is added.

Known limits: user text in exactly the server's format, for example `(FOO) (version 26.11.1.312)`, can still cut the message. The server stack trace (`stacktrace=1`) is still dropped.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the public `ClickHouseError.message` text for all parsed server errors, which can break exact string comparisons; the parser logic is central to every failed request path but is heavily covered by new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Refactors **`parseServerError`** in `packages/client-common/src/error/error.ts` so it scans type groups in **one pass**, trims trailing whitespace from parsed messages, and distinguishes **real server markers** (four-part ` (version x.x.x.x)` and the full stack-trace sentence) from **user text** in `throwIf` that mimics those patterns. **`ClickHouseError.message`** no longer ends with the space before `(TYPE)`—**`code`** and **`type`** are unchanged; changelogs document this as a migration note ([#1181]).
>

title: fix: give slow consumers all rows before a mid-stream error
body:
Closes #1167

## Summary

- **Node.js:** a mid-stream server error (the `__exception__` block of 25.11+, or an in-band `{"exception": ...}` row) no longer makes a slow consumer lose rows. The row stream keeps its rows until the consumer reads them, then fails with the server error. The server aborts the connection after the error, and Node.js destroys the response with `aborted` and discards its buffer, which can hold the error. The client now reads that buffer in the `'error'` callback, also through the gzip, zstd and br decompressors. The client logs the error and records it on the span when it finds it, also when the consumer stops before the end. Before: with 100k rows, 1 ms per batch, the consumer got `Error: aborted` after 77–79% of the rows (27–55% with gzip), every run.
- **Node.js:** a network error comes after the rows that were received before it. A cut exception-block opening does not become a row.
- **Both clients:** an in-band error row with no final newline is detected.
- `stream()` no longer uses `Stream.pipeline` (it destroys the row stream when the source fails); it uses `pipe` with `Stream.finished`.

## Coverage

| Fix | Unit | Integration (real server) |
|---|---|---|
| Rows before the error (`for await`, `'data'` + pause, `'readable'` + `read()`, `pipe`), `json()` | yes | yes, both error kinds |
| Source buffer read on abort | yes | yes |
| Decompressors (gzip, br, zstd) | yes | yes |
| Error row with no final newline (Node, Web) | yes | yes (real body, newline removed) |
| Network error after the rows; cut opening at each offset | yes | yes (proxy that cuts the response) |
| Destroyed source, `close()` then `json()`, `close()` with a pending error | yes | yes |
| One `read()` for each `'readable'` event | yes | no: Node.js stops that read pattern when more than one batch is in the buffer |
| Source closes with no error | yes | no: a real network does not give this state |

The new tests fail on `main`.

## Other checks

- Fuzz (real server bodies; random splits, source timing, abort time, read mode and delays; abort, close, network cut and early stop as separate modes): 14,500 cases, 0 failures, 0 hangs.
- Upstream SQL tests: full passthrough list, no regressions. No known failure passes because of this change.
- Codex review: 5 rounds; the findings of rounds 1–4 are fixed in this PR, round 5 found nothing.

## Known limit

After a network error, cut data and a cut exception-block opening can be the same bytes. The client keeps complete CSV/TSV rows. The one loss: a data line that is exactly `__exception__` at the cut, followed by the first bytes of the tag. A test documents it.

Web client: when the server closes the connection after the error, `fetch` itself discards the end of the body: Chromium (#1140), and also the `fetch` of Node.js (a raw `response.body` reader with 1 ms per read gets `TypeError: terminated` and no exception block). A slow Web consumer can lose rows and get a `TypeError`; the client cannot read those bytes. The Web changelog says so.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core streaming, decompression, and error/span lifecycle on the query hot path; behavior changes for mid-stream failures are intentional but high-impact for production consumers.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **#1167**: slow `ResultSet` consumers no longer lose rows or get `ECONNRESET`/`aborted` when ClickHouse fails mid-stream and tears down the HTTP connection.
> 
> **Node.js `ResultSet.stream()`** stops using `Stream.pipeline` (which discarded buffered rows on source failure). It pipes through a new **`RowsTransform`** that surfaces the server error only after the consumer drains already-emitted row batches, and on abort it drains the source’s remaining buffer before ending. Errors are logged and the `clickhouse.query.stream` span is finished when the client detects the failure—even if the app never reads further. **`close()`** also tears down the row stream. **`flush`** now catches **JSONEachRow/JSONStringsEachRow** in-band error rows with **no trailing newline**.
> 
> **Response decompression** (`gzip`/`br`/`zstd`) uses a custom pipe path so when the upstream response aborts, buffered compressed bytes are flushed through the decompressor instead of being dropped like `Stream.pipeline`.
> 
> **Web client**: same trailing error-row-without-newline handling in `result_set.ts` (fetch still cannot recover unread bytes on connection close—changelog note).
> 
> Docs add tracing guidance for mid-stream errors vs. `close()`. Changelogs and broad unit/integration tests cover slow consumers, compression, proxies, and network cuts.

title: Type-check the test files in CI
body:
## Problem

No CI job type-checks the test files.

- `npm run typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit` in each package. The package `tsconfig.json` files have `"include": ["./src/**/*.ts"]`, so `__tests__/` is not checked.
- Vitest removes the types from the test files without checking them.
- The root `tsconfig.dev.json` includes `./packages/**/*.ts` and maps `@test/*`, but no script runs it (only workflow path filters name it). It also extends `./tsconfig.json`, which does not exist anymore: `tsc -p tsconfig.dev.json` stops with `error TS5083: Cannot read file '.../tsconfig.json'`.

So a type error in a test passes all of CI. Example: on #1103, a test used the `const` object `ClickHouseSpanStatusCode` as a type (TS2749). Only the Copilot review found it, by reading the code.

## How big it is

`npx tsc -p tsconfig.dev.json --noEmit` on `main` reports 195 errors: 166 in `packages/client-node/__tests__`, 9 in `client-web/__tests__`, 9 in `client-common/__tests__`, and some in `datatype-parser`. The most frequent are TS2345, TS2322, TS2741 and TS7006. Part of these errors can come from the missing base config, so the real number is known only after step 1.

## Proposal

1. Fix the test type-check config: make `tsconfig.dev.json` extend `tsconfig.base.json`, or add a `tsconfig.test.json` in each package with the `@test/*` paths.
2. Add a `typecheck:tests` script, and run it in CI.
3. Fix the type errors in the tests. If there are many, record them first as a baseline, so that CI fails only on new errors, and fix the old errors in later PRs.

Classification: `impact: none · area: Docs & project (test type checking)`

title: Add a review skill for local code review
body:
## Problem

The repository has no review skill for agents. The review guidance is the section "When reviewing code changes" in the root `AGENTS.md`: it lists general aspects (security, API stability, changelog) but no checks for the problems that review often finds in this repository, and no process for a local review (target, tests on the old code, independent reviewers). The changelog rules also exist a second time in `.github/instructions/review.instructions.md`.

## Proposal

Add a local review skill, with the criteria in one place:

- `.claude/skills/review/review-core.md`: what to check: a severity scale, checks for errors and streams, requests and settings, both clients, the public API, tests, security, changelog, docs, CI and packaging, a list of low-value findings, and the commands.
- `.claude/skills/review/SKILL.md`: how to review a branch, a PR, a range or uncommitted changes: tests also on the old code, independent reviewers, a check of each finding, a report. It posts to GitHub only when the user asks and approves the text.
- `.agents/skills/review/SKILL.md`: a short pointer for other agent harnesses (Codex), with no copy of the text.
- Short contributor rules in the `AGENTS.md` files (docs name only things that exist, examples run as written, `// SAFETY:` comments, comments stay true, Prettier on every file, one concern per PR).

The checks come from incidents in this repository and from 881 review comments on 860 closed PRs.

## Evidence

Blind A/B tests on 6 closed PRs (#1024, #1045, #1076, #1087, #1103, #1169), at the commit that the reviewers saw, with the same review process in both arms. 10 findings of the human and bot reviewers were in scope.

- With the checks from incidents only: 7 of 10 found.
- With the mined checks added: 5 of 10 found. A "do not report" list from the rejected review comments dropped two real findings in dev scripts. That list now says to report such findings as one-line nits, never to drop them. This fixed version is not tested yet.
- Both arms also found problems that nobody reported (for example 5 public types that are still not exported after #1024), and neither reported the one bot finding that the maintainers rejected.

### Time-split test

The checks were mined only from PRs closed before 2026-06-01 (209 accepted review comments from 111 PRs). Both arms then reviewed blind 9 PRs from June to August 2026 (#542, #584, #793, #836, #852, #879, #886, #915, #950), with the same process (the "low-value" list reports findings as nits). A separate agent scored the reports without knowing the arms. 40 accepted review findings were in scope:

| | Checks from incidents and mined checks | Checks from incidents only |
|---|---|---|
| Found | 29 | 27 |
| Partly found | 5 | 6 |
| Missed | 5 | 7 |
| Rejected findings reported | 0 of 9 | 1 of 9 |
| Extra nits and pre-existing notes | 48 | 26 |

The mined checks help a little (2 of 40 findings, which can also be noise), and they make the reports longer. Both arms found must-fix problems that no reviewer reported, for example a Web client that returns raw zstd bytes (#836), and injected connections that drop `database` and the credentials (#879).

title: Examples CI runs against @clickhouse/client 1.18.3 from npm, not against the code of the PR
body:
## What happens

`examples/node` and `examples/web` depend on `"@clickhouse/client": "latest"` and `"@clickhouse/client-web": "latest"`. Their lockfiles pin version 1.18.3. The `examples` workflow runs `npm install`, which keeps the locked version. Thus:

- The examples run against 1.18.3: not against the latest release (1.25.0), and not against the code of the PR. The workflow runs for each change in `packages/**`, but it does not test that change.
- A PR that adds an API cannot update the examples in the same PR, because the typecheck of the examples fails: 1.18.3 does not have the API. For example, #778 adds `ResultSet.binaryStream()`, but `examples/node/performance/select_parquet_as_file.ts` cannot use it in that PR.

How I checked: with `examples/node/package.json` and `examples/node/package-lock.json` of `main`, `npm install --package-lock-only` resolves `@clickhouse/client` to 1.18.3. The lockfile of `examples/web` also has `@clickhouse/client-web` 1.18.3.

## Expected

The examples CI type-checks and runs the examples against the client packages that are built from the same commit. Then a PR can change the client and its examples together.

## Possible fix

In the examples CI, install the packages of the workspace (for example, the `npm pack` tarballs of the built packages, or a `file:` dependency) in place of the npm packages. If a check against the published packages is useful, keep it as a separate job.

**Classification:** impact: none · area: Docs & project (examples CI)

title: Read the bytes of a binary format from query(), with the mid-stream server error
body:
## Problem

`query()` gives no way to read the bytes of a binary format, such as `Parquet`, together with a server error that comes in the middle of the response (ClickHouse 25.11+):

- `ResultSet.stream()` splits the response into rows at each `\n` byte and decodes them as UTF-8 text. The rows do not give the original bytes. For `SELECT number, sipHash128(number) FROM numbers(100000)`, the joined rows are 4,365,828 bytes, but the Parquet file is 2,471,392 bytes.
- The stream of `client.exec()` gives the correct bytes, but it does not find a mid-stream error. The server closes the connection after the exception block, so the caller gets `ECONNRESET` (`aborted`) in Node.js, not a `ClickHouseError` with the code and the type.

#607 reported this use case (Parquet through `query()` and `stream()`). #975 fixed the false error in `stream()` from that issue, but not this part.

## Proposal

Add two methods to `ResultSet`, in `@clickhouse/client` and `@clickhouse/client-web`:

- `binaryStream()`: the response bytes, with no split into rows (`Buffer` chunks in Node.js, `Uint8Array` chunks in the Web client). When the server sends an error after a part of the result, the stream gives the bytes before the error, then fails with a `ClickHouseError`. It must give the error as soon as the exception block is complete, because the response does not end normally.
- `rawStream()`: the response stream as it is, with no check for a mid-stream error.

```ts
const rs = await client.query({ query: "SELECT * FROM t", format: "Parquet" });
await pipeline(rs.binaryStream(), fs.createWriteStream("t.parquet"));
```

PR #778 implements this.

**Classification:** impact: none · area: API & diagnostics (binary result stream)
